pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
Shared Task on

Identifying misogynistic videos in Dravidian languages

MMLow @ AACL-IJCNLP 2026

The Shared Task on Identifying Misogynistic Videos in Dravidian Languages aims to advance research in multimodal content analysis and online safety by developing automated systems capable of detecting misogynistic content in video data. Misogyny, expressed through hatred, prejudice, discrimination, objectification, or derogatory attitudes toward women, has become increasingly prevalent across social media and video-sharing platforms. Early detection of such harmful content is essential for creating safer and more inclusive digital spaces. In this shared task, participants will be provided with a curated collection of videos in two major Dravidian languages: Malayalam and Tamil. Each video may contain spoken content, visual cues, textual overlays, or a combination of these modalities. The primary objective is to build computational models that can analyze the videos and determine whether they contain misogynistic content or non-misogynistic content. Participants are encouraged to explore multimodal approaches that leverage audio, text, visual, and contextual information for effective classification. The task seeks to foster innovation in natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and multimodal machine learning for low-resource languages. The shared task will provide benchmark datasets, evaluation protocols, and performance metrics to facilitate fair comparison among participating systems. The outcomes of this task are expected to contribute to the development of robust content moderation tools and promote responsible AI solutions for combating online gender-based hate and discrimination in Dravidian language communities.

Objective: Identify videos in Dravidian languages containing misogynistic content

Languages: Malayalam and Tamil

Details: Participants will be provided with videos in Malayalam and Tamil and are required to classify these comments into misogynistic and non-misogynistic. This task requires a deeper level of multimodal understanding and precision.

Authors' Kit for Participation

  • Account Setup:
    • 'Codabench' Account: All participants must create an account on Codabench to participate. This platform will be used for accessing competition details and datasets (click HERE to create an account).
  • Registration Process:
    • Joining the Competition: After logging into Codabench, navigate to the 'My Submission' tab → accept the terms and conditions → select 'Register' to join the competition.
    • Access to Data: Once your registration is approved, you will gain access to the necessary datasets through Codabench in the 'Dataset files' tab.
  • Result Submission:
    • Procedure: Results must be submit via 'Google Form' in 'Result' or 'Evaluation' tab provided by the organizers. Detailed submission guidelines are available in the 'Evaluation' tab.
    • Note: Do not submit your results directly on the Codabench platform.
  • Timeliness: It is crucial to follow the submission deadlines strictly. Late submissions may not be considered for evaluation.

Paper Submission Guidelines

  • Format and Naming Convention:
    • Title Format: The title of the paper should follow this format: TEAM_NAME@MMLow 2026: Title of the paper. For example, XYZ@MMLow 2026: Identifying misogynistic videos in Dravidian languages
    • Authors' Names: Ensure that the authors' names on the paper match those entered in the Google Form during result submission.
  • Length and Content:
    • Document Length: The paper should be a maximum of 4 pages, excluding appendix and citations (references).
    • Paper Template: Paper submissions must use the LaTeX templates.
    • Must include the GitHub link (upload your code and attach that link) in the paper.
    • Note: Poster and demo submissions should be no longer than 4 pages (plus an unlimited number of pages for references and ethics/broader impact statements).
  • References and Citations:
    • Citing the Dataset: Make sure to cite the dataset and any overview papers relevant to the competition. BibTeX entries for these citations will be provided below.
  • Additional Points:
    • Innovation and Originality: Submissions that demonstrate innovative approaches and original research will be highly valued.

  The following are some general guidelines to remember while submitting the working notes.

  • Basic sanity check for grammatical errors and reported results
  • Papers should have sufficient information for reproducing the mentioned results.- Papers should follow the appropriate style.
  • Check the papers for text reuse / plagiarism. This includes self-plagiarism as well. We want to stress this point, as ACL is quite strict about it. Any paper found to have plagiarized content should be rejected without further consideration.
  • Please ensure the author names do not have any salutations like Dr., Prof., etc, in the final version

 All submissions should be in ACL templates below:

  • Overleaf:https://www.overleaf.com/latex/templates/association-for-computational-linguistics-acl-conference/jvxskxpnznfj
  • Paper submission: https://openreview.net/group?id=aclweb.org/AACL-IJCNLP/2026/Workshop/MMLow

# 拖雨林语言中厌女视频识别共享任务

## 共享任务介绍

德拉威语言厌女视频识别共享任务旨在通过开发能够检测视频数据中厌女内容的自动化系统，推进多模态内容分析和在线安全研究。厌女主义通过对女性的仇恨、偏见、歧视、物化或贬损态度表现出来，已在社交媒体和视频分享平台上日益普遍。早期检测此类有害内容对于创建更安全、更包容的数字空间至关重要。

在本共享任务中，参赛者将获得两种主要德拉威语言的精心策展视频集合：马拉雅拉姆语和泰米尔语。每个视频可能包含语音内容、视觉线索、文本覆盖或这些模态的组合。主要目标是构建能够分析视频并判断其是否包含厌女内容或非厌女内容的计算模型。

鼓励参赛者探索利用音频、文本、视觉和语境信息进行有效分类的多模态方法。该任务旨在促进自然语言处理、计算机视觉、语音处理和低资源语言多模态机器学习的创新。

共享任务将提供基准数据集、评估协议和性能指标，以便参赛系统之间进行公平比较。该任务的成果预计将有助于开发强大的内容审核工具，并为德拉威语言社区中应对在线性别仇恨和歧视推广负责任的人工智能解决方案。

**目标：** 识别德拉威语言中包含厌女内容的视频

**语言：** 马拉雅拉姆语和泰米尔语

**详情：** 参赛者将获得马拉雅拉姆语和泰米尔语的视频，需要将这些内容分类为厌女和非厌女。本任务需要更深层次的多模态理解和精确度。

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
Submission Format

Participants must submit a single ZIP file. The ZIP file should contain one or two folders, depending on the language(s) in which they are participating.

Folder Structure

  • If participating in both Malayalam and Tamil: Include two folders named Malayalam and Tamil.
  • If participating in only one language: Include only the corresponding language folder (Malayalam or Tamil).

CSV Files

  • Each language folder can contain a maximum of three CSV files.
  • Each CSV file corresponds to one submission run.
  • A maximum of three runs are permitted for each language.

File Naming Convention

Each CSV file must follow the naming format shown below:

<TeamName>_<TaskName>_<Language>_Run<RunNumber>.csv

Examples

TeamAlpha_Task1_Malayalam_Run1.csv
TeamAlpha_Task1_Malayalam_Run2.csv
TeamAlpha_Task1_Tamil_Run1.csv

CSV File Format

Each CSV file must contain exactly two columns with the following headers:

Id prediction
1 Label1
2 Label2
Important: The column headers must be exactly Id and prediction. Submissions with incorrect column names, additional columns, missing columns, or invalid file formats may not be evaluated.

Evaluation Criteria

We accept the test prediction results only through the Google Form

Google Form Link

Evaluation Methodology

  • Submissions for this task will be evaluated at the video level using the following metrics: Accuracy, Macro Precision, Macro Recall, Macro F1-score, Weighted Precision, Weighted Recall, and Weighted F1-score.

  • Official Ranking Criterion: Participants will be ranked based on the Macro F1-score.

 

Participants are required to submit the predicted data in a comma-separated value (CSV) file.

Paper submissions should be in the below format.
Overleaf Template:

https://www.overleaf.com/latex/templates/association-for-computational-linguistics-acl-conference/jvxskxpnznfj

Paper Submission Link:

https://openreview.net/group?id=aclweb.org/AACL-IJCNLP/2026/Workshop/MMLow

 

The classification system’s performance will be measured in terms of macro-averaged precision, macro-averaged recall, and macro-averaged F1 score across all the classes. Participants are encouraged to check their system with the sklearn classification report

15830.description:
Predict fixation-aligned MEG activity (204 gradiometer channels, 110 ms post-fixation) for a held-out subject, given natural scene images and eye movement metadata from the Active Vision Semantics (AVS) dataset.

Sulewski, P., Amme, C., Hebart, M., König, P., & Kietzmann, T. (2025). Why we linger: Memory encoding, rather than visual processing demand, drives fixation timing on natural scenes-evidence from a large-scale MEG dataset.

Academic use only. The AVS dataset and all derived materials are provided exclusively for academic research and educational purposes within the course "Neural encoding with deep neural networks" (SoSe 2026) at Osnabrück University.

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# MEG Brain Encoding Challenge

## Goal

Build a model that predicts how the human brain responds to visual scenes during natural free viewing. Specifically, you will predict **fixation-aligned MEG activity** — the pattern of neural responses measured across 204 MEG gradiometer channels at 110 ms after each eye fixation onset.

## Background

The data come from the **Active Vision Semantics (AVS)** dataset, in which participants freely explored natural scene photographs while their eye movements and whole-head MEG were simultaneously recorded.

You are given data from five training subjects (subjects 1–5) and asked to generalise to a **held-out subject (subject 60)**, whose scene-viewing behaviour and associated MEG responses form the evaluation set.

## Task

**Challenge 1 — Snapshot encoding at 110 ms**

Given the fixation metadata (scene ID, gaze coordinates, duration, sequence position, etc.) and the corresponding scene images, predict the vector of 204 MEG gradiometer amplitudes at 110 ms post-fixation onset.

**Submission shape:** `(7750, 204)` — one row per fixation in the development set, 204 channels.

## Timeline

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| April 2026 | Challenge opens |
| July 2026 | Challenge closes |

## Limits

- 5 submissions per day
- 50 submissions total
pages.content_zh:
# MEG脑编码挑战

## 目标

构建一个模型，预测人类大脑对自然自由观看视觉场景的反应。具体地说，您将预测**注视对齐的MEG活动**——在每次眼动注视开始后110毫秒时在204个MEG梯度计通道上测得的神经反应模式。

## 背景

数据来自**主动视觉语义学（AVS）**数据集，其中参与者在同时记录眼动和全脑MEG的情况下自由探索自然场景照片。

您获得来自五名训练受试者（受试者1-5）的数据，并被要求推广到**保留的受试者（受试者60）**，其场景观看行为和相关的MEG反应构成评估集。

## 任务

**挑战1——110毫秒处的快照编码**

给定注视元数据（场景ID、凝视坐标、持续时间、序列位置等）和对应的场景图像，预测注视开始后110毫秒时204个MEG梯度计振幅的向量。

**提交形状：** `(7750, 204)` ——开发集中每次注视一行，204个通道。

## 时间表

| 日期 | 事件 |
|------|------|
| 2026年4月 | 挑战开放 |
| 2026年7月 | 挑战关闭 |

## 限制

- 每天5次提交
- 总共50次提交

pages.title: Data
pages.content:
# Data

## What You Receive

All data are distributed through the course repository. You do **not** upload data to Codabench — only your predictions.

### Training data (subjects 1–5)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `training/meg_110ms.npy` | MEG at 110 ms, shape `(n_fixations, 204)` |
| `training/metadata.csv` | Per-fixation metadata (see columns below) |
| `training/channel_names.txt` | Ordered list of 204 gradiometer channel names |
| `avs_scenes/` | Full scene images (shared across subjects) |

### Development set (subject 60)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `subject60/challenge1_dev/metadata.csv` | 7750 fixations for which you submit predictions |

The ground truth MEG for subject 60 is **withheld** and used only for scoring.

## Metadata Columns

Key columns in `metadata.csv`:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `sceneID` | Integer scene identifier — links to image file |
| `mean_gx`, `mean_gy` | Mean gaze position in screen-centred pixels (origin = centre, y-axis up) |
| `duration` | Fixation duration [ms] |
| `fix_sequence` | Fixation index within the trial (1 = first fixation) |
| `time_in_trial` | Time since trial onset [ms] |
| `subject` | Subject identifier |

## Scene Images

Scene images are JPEGs named `{sceneID:012d}_MEG_size.jpg`, scaled to the presentation resolution (1024 × 768 px). Fixation patches (112 × 112 px, centred on gaze) can be extracted using `megcourselib.data.stim.extract_crop()`.
pages.content_zh:
# 数据

## 您将获得的数据

所有数据通过课程资源库分发。您**不**将数据上传到 Codabench — 仅提交预测结果。

### 训练数据（被试 1–5）

| 文件 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| `training/meg_110ms.npy` | 110 ms 时的脑磁图，形状为 `(n_fixations, 204)` |
| `training/metadata.csv` | 每个注视点的元数据（见下表列名） |
| `training/channel_names.txt` | 204 个梯度计通道名称的有序列表 |
| `avs_scenes/` | 完整场景图像（各被试共用） |

### 开发集（被试 60）

| 文件 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| `subject60/challenge1_dev/metadata.csv` | 7750 个注视点，需要提交预测 |

被试 60 的真实脑磁图数据**被隐藏**，仅用于评分。

## 元数据列

`metadata.csv` 中的关键列：

| 列名 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| `sceneID` | 整数场景标识符 — 链接到图像文件 |
| `mean_gx`, `mean_gy` | 屏幕中心坐标系中的平均凝视位置（像素）（原点 = 中心，y 轴向上） |
| `duration` | 注视点持续时间 [ms] |
| `fix_sequence` | 试次内的注视点索引（1 = 第一个注视点） |
| `time_in_trial` | 试次开始后的时间 [ms] |
| `subject` | 被试标识符 |

## 场景图像

场景图像为 JPEG 格式，命名为 `{sceneID:012d}_MEG_size.jpg`，缩放至呈现分辨率（1024 × 768 像素）。注视点补丁（112 × 112 像素，以凝视点为中心）可使用 `megcourselib.data.stim.extract_crop()` 提取。

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation

## Metric

Submissions are evaluated using **Pearson correlation (r)** between predicted and actual MEG amplitudes, computed **independently for each of the 204 channels** across all 7750 fixations in the development set.

This gives a vector **r** ∈ ℝ^204, from which four leaderboard scores are derived:

| Column | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| **Mean r** *(primary)* | `mean(r)` — average encoding across all channels |
| **Median r** | `median(r)` — robust central tendency |
| **Max r** | `max(r)` — best single-channel encoding |
| **Worst-10 Channels** | `mean(r[argsort(r)[:10]])` — average of the 10 worst channels |

Rankings are determined by **Mean r** (higher is better). All other columns are shown for diagnostic purposes.

## Submission Format

1. Create a NumPy array of predictions with shape `(7750, 204)` and dtype `float64`.
   - Row order must match `subject60/challenge1_dev/metadata.csv` exactly.
   - Column order must match `channel_names.txt` exactly (MEG0001 … MEG0204).

2. Save it as `predictions.npy`:
   ```python
   import numpy as np
   np.save("predictions.npy", pred)   # shape (7750, 204)
   ```

3. Zip it (the file must be at the root of the zip, not in a subfolder):
   ```bash
   zip submission.zip predictions.npy
   ```

4. Upload `submission.zip` via the Submit button.

## Validity Checks

The scoring program rejects submissions that:
- Have the wrong shape (anything other than 7750 × 204)
- Contain NaN or Inf values

Invalid submissions receive a score of 0.0 on all columns.
pages.content_zh:
# 评估

## 指标

提交的作品使用**皮尔逊相关系数（r）**进行评估，该系数在开发集的所有7750个注视点中**独立计算每个204个通道**的预测MEG振幅与实际MEG振幅之间的相关性。

这产生一个向量 **r** ∈ ℝ^204，从中导出四个排行榜分数：

| 列 | 定义 |
|--------|-----------|
| **平均 r** *（主要指标）* | `mean(r)` — 所有通道的平均编码 |
| **中位数 r** | `median(r)` — 稳健的中心趋势 |
| **最大 r** | `max(r)` — 最佳单通道编码 |
| **最差10个通道** | `mean(r[argsort(r)[:10]])` — 最差10个通道的平均值 |

排名由**平均 r** 决定（越高越好）。所有其他列仅用于诊断目的。

## 提交格式

1. 创建一个形状为 `(7750, 204)` 且数据类型为 `float64` 的NumPy数组。
   - 行顺序必须与 `subject60/challenge1_dev/metadata.csv` 完全匹配。
   - 列顺序必须与 `channel_names.txt` 完全匹配（MEG0001 … MEG0204）。

2. 将其保存为 `predictions.npy`：
   ```python
   import numpy as np
   np.save("predictions.npy", pred)   # 形状 (7750, 204)
   ```

3. 压缩它（文件必须在zip的根目录下，不能在子文件夹中）：
   ```bash
   zip submission.zip predictions.npy
   ```

4. 通过提交按钮上传 `submission.zip`。

## 有效性检查

评分程序会拒绝以下提交：
- 形状错误（除7750 × 204外的任何形状）
- 包含NaN或Inf值

无效提交在所有列中得分为0.0。

pages.content:
# Update on Task 3 HD/ASD Evaluation

We found an issue in the previous calculation of the last two Task 3 metrics, namely Task 3 HD and Task 3 ASD. The evaluation rule has now been updated.

The updated Task 3 evaluation uses the corrected HD/ASD calculation. This update is intended to make the Task 3 distance metrics more reasonable and fair for all participants.

To ensure fairness, each team now has **10 valid submission attempts**. The platform allows up to **20 total submissions** to account for possible submission errors or failed evaluations. However, the number of valid submissions must not exceed 10.

All new submissions will be evaluated using the updated rule. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and thank you for your understanding.

# Important Notice: Final Test Docker Evaluation

The MVAA 2026 challenge has entered the final hidden-test Docker evaluation stage.

Participants must submit a Docker image reference through this CodaBench portal. Direct upload of prediction masks is **not** used for the official final ranking.

## Required Submission

Each team should submit a `submission.zip` containing a root-level `submission.json` file:

    {
      "image": "registry.example.com/mvaa/team001@sha256:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
      "timeout_seconds": 21600
    }

The Docker image must contain the complete inference environment, including model weights, code, runtime dependencies, and an automatic entrypoint.

## Hidden Test Evaluation

After a descriptor is accepted, a private organizer-side CodaBench worker forwards it to the MVAA GPU runner. The runner pulls the Docker image, runs it on the hidden test inputs, computes official DSC/HD/ASD metrics using the private reference annotations, and returns the scores to this CodaBench leaderboard.

The hidden test images and labels are not released to participants. Labels are never mounted into participant containers.

## Hardware Compatibility

The final evaluation server uses an NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB GPU. Submitted images must be compatible with compute capability `sm_70`.

## Method Paper Submission

The MWM2026 method paper submission deadline has been extended to **July 20, 2026**.

Participants should submit their method papers through the MWM2026 website:

https://mwm2026.github.io/

Please note that submitting a method paper is one of the prerequisite conditions for award eligibility.

## Deadline

The final Docker submission deadline is **August 01, 2026, 23:59 (UTC+8)**.

# MVAA 2026 Final Test ## Docker-Based Hidden Test Evaluation for Mitral Valve Anatomy Analysis
Mitral valve assessment plays a central role in the diagnosis, treatment planning, and intraoperative guidance of structural heart disease. The MVAA challenge evaluates automated methods for mitral valve anatomy analysis across three imaging modalities: cardiac CT, 3D transesophageal echocardiography (3D TEE), and surgical video frames. This CodaBench portal is dedicated to the **final hidden-test stage**. Participants submit Docker images containing their complete inference pipelines. The organizers then run the submitted images on the hidden test set and compute the official metrics using the private reference annotations. ## Final Test Objective The final test phase evaluates whether submitted algorithms can generalize to unseen data under a standardized computing environment. The evaluation covers: - Task 1: cardiac CT segmentation; - Task 2: 3D TEE multi-class segmentation; - Task 3: surgical video frame segmentation. ## Submission Mode For this stage, participants submit a lightweight `submission.zip` containing only a Docker image reference. The Docker image itself must be hosted in an accessible registry and must include all inference code, model weights, and dependencies. Please read the **Final Docker Submission** page before submitting. ## Resources - Challenge website: https://mwm2026.github.io/mvaa - Baseline code: https://github.com/db0725/MVAA - CodaBench platform: https://www.codabench.org/ - Contact: dbd2002@foxmail.com

pages.content:
# Final Docker Submission

This page describes the required Docker submission format for the MVAA 2026 hidden test phase.

During the final test phase, participants do **not** upload prediction masks directly. Instead, each team submits a lightweight `submission.zip` containing a Docker image reference. A private organizer-side CodaBench worker will forward the descriptor to the MVAA GPU runner. The runner pulls the image, runs it on the hidden test set, computes official metrics, and returns the scores to CodaBench.

## 1. What to Submit to CodaBench

Submit a single `submission.zip` file with the following structure:

```text
submission.zip
`-- submission.json
```

The root-level `submission.json` must contain:

```json
{
  "image": "registry.example.com/mvaa/team001:final",
  "timeout_seconds": 21600
}
```

Fields:

- `image`: Docker/OCI image reference containing your inference code, model weights, dependencies, and default entrypoint.
- `timeout_seconds`: Optional runtime limit requested by the participant. The default limit is 21600 seconds (6 hours). The hard maximum is 43200 seconds (12 hours).


Privacy note: the submitted Docker image reference is used only for organizer-side evaluation and is not shown in the public leaderboard or detailed result page. Do not put registry passwords or access tokens in `submission.json`. If your image is hosted in a private registry, please make sure the organizers have pull access before submission.

For reproducibility, a digest-pinned image is recommended:

```json
{
  "image": "registry.example.com/mvaa/team001@sha256:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
}
```


## 2. Reference Baseline Docker Image

The organizers provide a public reference baseline Docker image so participants can inspect the expected Docker-based inference style:

```bash
docker pull db0725/mvaa-baseline-infer:final-20260626
```

This image is provided only as a reference example. Participants may build their own images using any compatible environment, as long as the final image follows the input/output contract described below.

## 3. Docker Image Requirements

Your Docker image must include:

- all inference code;
- all model weights and checkpoints;
- all Python/system dependencies required at runtime;
- a default `ENTRYPOINT` or `CMD` that starts inference automatically.

Your Docker image must **not** require:

- internet access at runtime;
- interactive terminal input;
- downloading extra model weights during evaluation;
- access to hidden labels or organizer-only files.

The submitted image must be a Linux `amd64` Docker/OCI image.

## 4. Organizer Runtime Contract

The organizer runner will execute the submitted image with the following input/output contract. The exact Docker flags may vary by organizer-side infrastructure:

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all \
  --network none \
  --memory 28g \
  --cpus 14 \
  --pids-limit 2048 \
  --shm-size 8g \
  --cap-drop ALL \
  --security-opt no-new-privileges \
  -v /hidden/test_data:/input:ro \
  -v /job/output:/output:rw \
  -v /job/work:/work:rw \
  -e MVAA_INPUT_DIR=/input \
  -e MVAA_OUTPUT_DIR=/output \
  -w /work \
  YOUR_IMAGE
```

Your container must:

- read test inputs from `/input`;
- write predictions to `/output`;
- exit with code `0` on success.

## 5. Expected Output Layout

After inference, `/output` should contain:

```text
/output/
|-- t1_ct/
|   |-- task1_predictions.json
|   |-- case001_pred.nii.gz
|   `-- ...
|-- t2_tee/
|   |-- task2_predictions.json
|   |-- case001_pred.nii.gz
|   `-- ...
`-- t3_vid/
    |-- task3_predictions.json
    |-- REC_xxx/frame001_pred.png
    `-- ...
```

Task 1 prediction JSON:

```json
{
  "cases": [
    {
      "case_id": "case001",
      "segmentation": "case001_pred.nii.gz"
    }
  ]
}
```

Task 2 prediction JSON:

```json
{
  "cases": [
    {
      "case_id": "case001",
      "segmentation": "case001_pred.nii.gz"
    }
  ]
}
```

Task 3 prediction JSON:

```json
{
  "cases": [
    {
      "case_id": "REC_xxx_000001",
      "segmentation": "REC_xxx/REC_xxx_000001_pred.png"
    }
  ]
}
```

The `segmentation` field must be a relative path under the corresponding task output folder. Absolute paths and path traversal such as `../` are not allowed.

## 6. Mask Format

Task 1:

- File format: `.nii.gz`
- Labels: `0` for background, `1` for target foreground.

Task 2:

- File format: `.nii.gz`
- Labels: `0` for background, `1` and `2` for the two target classes.

Task 3:

- Recommended file format: `.png`
- Labels: `0` for background, any positive value for foreground. Binary masks using `255` for foreground are recommended.

## 7. GPU Compatibility

The official final-test server uses:

```text
GPU: NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB
CUDA driver: 550.x / CUDA 12.4
Compute capability: sm_70
```

Your Docker image must be compatible with NVIDIA V100 / `sm_70`. Do not rely on Ampere/Ada/Hopper-only features such as BF16-only execution, TF32-only kernels, or CUDA extensions compiled only for `sm80`, `sm86`, or `sm89`.

If you compile custom CUDA extensions, include:

```bash
TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.0"
```

## 8. Minimal Dockerfile Example

```dockerfile
FROM pytorch/pytorch:2.5.1-cuda12.4-cudnn9-runtime

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
ENV MVAA_INPUT_DIR=/input
ENV MVAA_OUTPUT_DIR=/output

WORKDIR /workspace

COPY requirements.txt /workspace/requirements.txt
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /workspace/requirements.txt

COPY src/ /workspace/src/
COPY weights/ /workspace/weights/
COPY run.sh /workspace/run.sh
RUN chmod +x /workspace/run.sh

ENTRYPOINT ["/workspace/run.sh"]
```

Example `run.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

INPUT_DIR="${MVAA_INPUT_DIR:-/input}"
OUTPUT_DIR="${MVAA_OUTPUT_DIR:-/output}"

mkdir -p "${OUTPUT_DIR}/t1_ct" "${OUTPUT_DIR}/t2_tee" "${OUTPUT_DIR}/t3_vid"

python /workspace/src/infer.py \
  --input "${INPUT_DIR}" \
  --output "${OUTPUT_DIR}"
```

## 9. Local Test Command

Before final submission, test your image locally:

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all \
  --network none \
  -v /path/to/test_input:/input:ro \
  -v /path/to/output:/output:rw \
  your-image:final
```

Then package `submission.json`:

```bash
zip submission.zip submission.json
```

pages.title: Core Task
pages.content:
# Core Task

The MVAA challenge is designed to reflect the real-world clinical workflow across multiple imaging modalities. The challenge is structured into three primary segmentation tasks.

### Participation and Model Submission Requirements

Participants are required to complete and submit results for all three tasks. The official final ranking will be determined using the normalized final score described on the **Final Ranking** page; therefore, submissions for only one or two tasks will not be sufficient for the final ranking.

However, participants are not required to use a single unified multimodal model. Each task may be addressed independently, and participants may train and submit separate models for the CT, 3D TEE, and surgical video frame segmentation tasks.

### Task 1: Mitral Valve Segmentation in Cardiac CT
This task focuses on the automated, multi-class anatomical segmentation of the mitral valve from 3D cardiac CT scans.
*   **Target:** Participants are required to segment the mitral annulus and the anterior/posterior leaflets.
*   **Clinical Significance:** High-resolution CT segmentation provides the precise spatial geometry necessary for pre-procedural planning, including device sizing and the selection of repair strategies for interventions like TEER or annuloplasty.

### Task 2: Mitral Valve Segmentation in 3D Transesophageal Echocardiography (3D TEE)
This task addresses the segmentation of valve structures from volumetric 3D TEE (ultrasound) data, which serves as the key intraoperative reference for valve function.
*   **Target:** Delineation of the valve leaflets from 3D ultrasound volumes.
*   **Technical Focus:** Algorithms must be robust enough to handle ultrasound-specific artifacts, acoustic noise, signal dropout, and ambiguous boundaries between the leaflets and surrounding cardiac tissues.

### Task 3: Mitral Valve Segmentation from Surgical Video Frames
This task focuses on extracting anatomical information from individual frames extracted from intraoperative surgical videos.
*   **Target:** Pixel-level segmentation of the mitral valve structures as seen from the surgeon's direct viewpoint.
*   **Methodology:** Although the data originates from video recordings, this task is defined as a frame-based segmentation problem. Participants should treat the provided frames as individual 2D images for training and inference.
*   **Clinical Focus:** This task enables the verification of leaflet motion and structural continuity during the actual intervention, providing real-time feedback within the surgical environment.
pages.content_zh:
# 核心任务

MVAA挑战赛旨在反映多个成像模态下的真实临床工作流程。该挑战赛结构包含三个主要分割任务。

### 参赛和模型提交要求

参赛者需要完成并提交全部三个任务的结果。官方最终排名将根据**最终排名**页面中描述的归一化最终得分确定；因此，仅提交一个或两个任务的结果将不足以获得最终排名。

但是，参赛者不需要使用单一的统一多模态模型。每个任务可以独立处理，参赛者可以为CT、3D TEE和手术视频帧分割任务分别训练和提交不同的模型。

### 任务1：心脏CT中的二尖瓣分割
该任务重点关注从三维心脏CT扫描中进行二尖瓣多类解剖结构的自动分割。
*   **目标：** 参赛者需要分割二尖瓣环以及前/后瓣叶。
*   **临床意义：** 高分辨率CT分割提供了精确的空间几何信息，用于术前规划，包括器械尺寸确定和修复策略选择，适用于TEER或瓣环成形术等介入治疗。

### 任务2：三维经食管超声心动图(3D TEE)中的二尖瓣分割
该任务涉及从容积3D TEE(超声)数据中进行瓣膜结构分割，其作为瓣膜功能的关键术中参考。
*   **目标：** 从3D超声容积数据中描绘瓣叶轮廓。
*   **技术重点：** 算法必须足够稳健以处理超声特有的伪影、声学噪声、信号丢失以及瓣叶与周围心脏组织间的模糊边界。

### 任务3：手术视频帧中的二尖瓣分割
该任务重点关注从术中手术视频中提取的单个帧中提取解剖学信息。
*   **目标：** 从外科医生直接视角看到的二尖瓣结构进行像素级分割。
*   **方法学：** 虽然数据源自视频记录，但该任务被定义为基于帧的分割问题。参赛者应将提供的帧作为单个2D图像进行训练和推理。
*   **临床重点：** 该任务能够在实际介入治疗中验证瓣叶运动和结构连续性，在手术环境中提供实时反馈。

pages.title: Dataset
pages.content:
# MVAA Challenge - Dataset System

## 1. Ethics Approval & Data License

### 1.1 Ethics Approval
All data is anonymized, with approval from the Medical Ethics Committee (No. KY-N-2022-048-01).

### 1.2 Data Usage Agreement & License
* **License:** CC BY-NC (Attribution-NonCommercial)
* No commercial use of the data is permitted; all usage must comply with the license terms.

## 2. Data Source

### 2.1 Acquisition Devices
* **Cardiac CT:** Siemens Healthineers, GE Healthcare, Philips Healthcare, and Canon Medical Systems.
* **3D TEE:** Philips Epiq cardiac ultrasound system.
* **Surgical Video:** Standard endoscopic video recorder (720p, 30fps).

### 2.2 Acquisition Centers
The dataset is collected from multiple clinical centers, including:
* Guangdong Provincial People’s Hospital
* The First Affiliated Hospital of Jinan University
* Dongguan Eastern Central Hospital

## 3. Dataset Scale & Partition

### 3.1 Task 1: Cardiac CT Segmentation
* **Training Set:** 1,067 images total (27 with ground-truth labels, 1,040 unlabeled for semi-supervised learning).
* **Validation Set:** 30 images (without labels).

### 3.2 Task 2: 3D TEE Segmentation
* **Training Set:** 105 images with ground-truth labels.
* **Validation Set:** 20 images (without labels).

### 3.3 Task 3: Surgical Frame Segmentation

* **Training Set:** 1,559 frames total.
    * **Labeled Data:** 180 frames (118 frames contain the mitral valve).
    * **Unlabeled Data:** 1,379 frames (for semi-supervised learning).
* **Validation Set:** 48 images (without labels, all containing mitral valve structures for scoring).

#### 3.3.1 Task 3 Label Note

Task 3 labels may include annotations beyond the mitral valve. Only the mitral valve label is used for training and evaluation. In this task, the mitral valve is the only target segmentation class.

Participants should use the `*_Label.nii.gz` file within each `*_Label.tar` archive as the source of ground-truth annotations, and refer to the category mapping table in the corresponding `*_Label.json` file for confirmation. Specifically, category ID `10` corresponds to the mitral valve.

The `*_Label.json` file is intended only for reading category names, colors, and metadata, and should not be used as the primary label source for training.

Some polygon annotations in the JSON files are incomplete or empty; therefore, generating training labels from `Polys.Shapes` is not recommended. Of the 180 labeled frames, 118 contain valid mitral valve annotations. Unlabeled frames may also include images without visible mitral valve structures.


## 4. Data Novelty
* **Multi-modal Data Resource:** The challenge includes cardiac CT, 3D TEE, and surgical video data collected from multiple clinical centers. In the current public release, these modalities are provided as independent datasets, and no formal CT-video pairing metadata or case mapping table is included.
* **Unpublished Data:** More than 140 newly collected, unpublished ultrasound images have been provided for validation and testing to ensure fair evaluation of generalization.

## 5. Inclusion & Exclusion Criteria

### 5.1 Inclusion Criteria
1. Standard clinical cardiac views suitable for mitral valve assessment.
2. Sufficient image quality for expert annotation of leaflets and annulus.
3. Availability of corresponding clinical measurement references.

### 5.2 Exclusion Criteria
1. Severe imaging artifacts or signal dropout hindering anatomical visibility.
2. Duplicated or corrupted data.
3. Cases with uncertain clinical reference measurements.

## 6. Annotation Characteristics

### 6.1 Annotation Method
* **Two-Stage Process:** Initial annotations by two trained medical experts followed by review and refinement by a board-certified radiologist with over 10 years of experience.
* **Semi-automated refinement:** For ultrasound data, an initial automatic segmentation was followed by manual review and modification by two annotators until agreement was reached.

### 6.2 Annotation Quality Control (QC)
* **Inter-observer Reliability:** Evaluated on a subset of 30 images using ICC and absolute error distributions.
* **Adjudication:** Senior clinical specialists resolved discrepancies to ensure the reliability of reference annotations.

## 7. Data Preprocessing
1. **Anonymization:** Removal of all patient-related information from metadata.
2. **Standardization:** CT and TEE data converted to NIfTI format; surgical video frames extracted as 2D images.
3. **Resampling:** Data resampled to a consistent resolution to ensure uniform slice-level annotation.

## 8. Main Annotation Error Sources
1. **Inter-Annotator Variability:** Differences in identifying subtle mitral valve boundaries in low-contrast cases.
2. **Annotation Ambiguity:** Inherent ambiguity of valve boundaries due to pathological alterations or imaging limitations.
3. **Technical Limitations:** Errors introduced by the resolution constraints of the annotation tools.
pages.content_zh:
# MVAA挑战赛 - 数据集系统

## 1. 伦理审批与数据许可

### 1.1 伦理审批
所有数据已匿名处理，获得医学伦理委员会批准（编号：KY-N-2022-048-01）。

### 1.2 数据使用协议与许可证
* **许可证：** CC BY-NC（署名-非商业性使用）
* 禁止对数据进行商业使用；所有使用必须符合许可证条款。

## 2. 数据来源

### 2.1 采集设备
* **心脏CT：** 西门子医疗、通用电气医疗、飞利浦医疗和佳能医疗系统。
* **3D TEE：** 飞利浦Epiq心脏超声系统。
* **手术视频：** 标准内窥镜视频录制器（720p，30fps）。

### 2.2 采集中心
数据集来自多个临床中心，包括：
* 广东省人民医院
* 暨南大学第一附属医院
* 东莞东部中央医院

## 3. 数据集规模与划分

### 3.1 任务1：心脏CT分割
* **训练集：** 共1,067张图像（27张带有标注标签，1,040张用于半监督学习的未标注数据）。
* **验证集：** 30张图像（无标签）。

### 3.2 任务2：3D TEE分割
* **训练集：** 105张带有标注标签的图像。
* **验证集：** 20张图像（无标签）。

### 3.3 任务3：手术帧分割

* **训练集：** 共1,559帧。
    * **标注数据：** 180帧（其中118帧包含二尖瓣）。
    * **未标注数据：** 1,379帧（用于半监督学习）。
* **验证集：** 48张图像（无标签，全部包含二尖瓣结构用于评分）。

#### 3.3.1 任务3标签说明

任务3标签可能包含二尖瓣之外的注释。仅二尖瓣标签用于训练和评估。在该任务中，二尖瓣是唯一的目标分割类别。

参与者应使用每个`*_Label.tar`压缩包内的`*_Label.nii.gz`文件作为真值注释的来源，并参考相应`*_Label.json`文件中的类别映射表进行确认。具体而言，类别ID `10` 对应二尖瓣。

`*_Label.json`文件仅供读取类别名称、颜色和元数据使用，不应作为训练标签的主要来源。

JSON文件中的某些多边形注释可能不完整或为空；因此不建议从`Polys.Shapes`生成训练标签。在180个标注帧中，118个包含有效的二尖瓣注释。未标注帧也可能包含不含可见二尖瓣结构的图像。

## 4. 数据新颖性
* **多模态数据资源：** 挑战赛包括来自多个临床中心的心脏CT、3D TEE和手术视频数据。在当前公开发布版本中，这些模态作为独立数据集提供，不包含正式的CT-视频配对元数据或病例映射表。
* **未发表数据：** 提供了超过140张新采集的未发表超声图像用于验证和测试，以确保泛化能力的公平评估。

## 5. 纳入与排除标准

### 5.1 纳入标准
1. 适合二尖瓣评估的标准临床心脏图像。
2. 图像质量足以进行专家标注瓣叶和瓣环。
3. 有相应的临床测量参考数据。

### 5.2 排除标准
1. 严重影像伪影或信号丧失，影响解剖结构的可见性。
2. 重复或损坏的数据。
3. 临床参考测量不确定的病例。

## 6. 注释特征

### 6.1 注释方法
* **两阶段流程：** 先由两名训练有素的医学专家进行初始注释，随后由具有10年以上经验的认证放射学医生进行审核和改进。
* **半自动化精化：** 对于超声数据，初始自动分割后由两名注释者进行手工审核和修改，直至达成一致。

### 6.2 注释质量控制

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation

## Final Test Evaluation Mode

In the final hidden-test phase, participants submit Docker image descriptors through CodaBench. A private organizer-side CodaBench worker forwards accepted descriptors to the MVAA GPU runner, which pulls each submitted image, runs inference on the hidden test set, computes official metrics, and returns the resulting scores to the CodaBench leaderboard.

Metrics are computed outside the public CodaBench environment on the organizer-side server. The leaderboard columns in this portal are the official hidden-test raw metrics returned by that runner. The official overall ranking is based on normalized metric scores as described on the **Final Ranking** page.

## Metrics

All tasks are evaluated using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff Distance (HD), and Average Surface Distance (ASD). Higher DSC is better; lower HD and ASD are better.

### Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)

DSC measures overlap between the predicted segmentation and the ground truth. It is computed as twice the intersection divided by the sum of the predicted and reference foreground sizes.

### Hausdorff Distance (HD)

HD measures the largest bidirectional surface discrepancy between the prediction and reference mask. Surfaces are extracted from binary masks and Euclidean distances are computed using image spacing when spacing metadata is available.

### Average Surface Distance (ASD)

ASD is the symmetric mean surface-to-surface distance between prediction and reference masks.

## Task-Specific Computation

### Task 1: CT Segmentation

- Foreground label: `1`
- Per-case metrics: DSC, HD, ASD on the binary foreground mask
- Final task score: mean across all Task 1 cases

### Task 2: TEE Segmentation

- Foreground labels: `1` and `2`
- Metrics are computed separately for each foreground class and averaged within each case
- Final task score: mean across all Task 2 cases

### Task 3: Video/Image Segmentation

- Prediction foreground: any positive pixel value
- Reference foreground: the case-specific `target_label`
- Final task score: mean across all Task 3 frames/cases

## Evaluation Notes

- HD and ASD use physical spacing when available; otherwise unit spacing is used.
- Missing or invalid predictions receive penalty metrics: `DSC = 0`, `HD = large penalty`, `ASD = large penalty`.
- If both prediction and reference are empty for an evaluated class, that class is treated as a perfect match: `DSC = 1`, `HD = 0`, `ASD = 0`.
- Prediction paths in JSON files must be relative paths under the corresponding task output folder. Absolute paths and `../` traversal are rejected.

## Leaderboard Columns

The final leaderboard reports:

- `Task1_DSC`, `Task1_HD`, `Task1_ASD`
- `Task2_DSC`, `Task2_HD`, `Task2_ASD`
- `Task3_DSC`, `Task3_HD`, `Task3_ASD`
- `Evaluation_Status`
- `Runtime_Seconds`

`Evaluation_Status = 1` means the organizer-side runner completed successfully. `Evaluation_Status = 0` means descriptor validation, image pulling, inference, or scoring failed; failed submissions receive penalty metrics.

## Participant Result Summary

After a successful final-test submission, participants will see the leaderboard values for the three mean metrics of each task. Per-case or per-image scores are not shown in the final hidden-test phase.

The detailed result summary follows this structure:

```text
MVAA Final Hidden-Test Evaluation
Status: done
Message: official hidden-test evaluation completed

Task-level mean metrics:
- Task 1 (CT): mean DSC = ..., mean HD = ..., mean ASD = ...
- Task 2 (TEE): mean DSC = ..., mean HD = ..., mean ASD = ...
- Task 3 (Video/Image): mean DSC = ..., mean HD = ..., mean ASD = ...

Evaluation_Status: 1
Runtime_Seconds: ...
```
pages.content_zh:
# 评估

## 最终测试评估模式

在最终隐藏测试阶段，参与者通过CodaBench提交Docker镜像描述符。组织方CodaBench工作线程将接受的描述符转发给MVAA GPU运行器，该运行器拉取每个提交的镜像，在隐藏测试集上运行推理，计算官方指标，并将结果得分返回给CodaBench排行榜。

指标在组织方服务器上的公共CodaBench环境外进行计算。此门户中排行榜列显示由该运行器返回的官方隐藏测试原始指标。官方总体排名基于**最终排名**页面中描述的标准化指标得分。

## 指标

所有任务使用骰子相似系数（DSC）、豪斯多夫距离（HD）和平均表面距离（ASD）进行评估。DSC越高越好；HD和ASD越低越好。

### 骰子相似系数（DSC）

DSC测量预测分割与真实标注之间的重叠程度。计算方式为交集的两倍除以预测和参考前景大小之和。

### 豪斯多夫距离（HD）

HD测量预测和参考掩模之间最大的双向表面偏差。表面从二值掩模中提取，当有间距元数据时使用图像间距计算欧几里得距离。

### 平均表面距离（ASD）

ASD是预测和参考掩模之间对称的表面间平均距离。

## 任务特定计算

### 任务1：CT分割

- 前景标签：`1`
- 按病例指标：二值前景掩模上的DSC、HD、ASD
- 最终任务得分：所有任务1病例的均值

### 任务2：TEE分割

- 前景标签：`1`和`2`
- 为每个前景类分别计算指标，在每个病例内进行平均
- 最终任务得分：所有任务2病例的均值

### 任务3：视频/图像分割

- 预测前景：任何正像素值
- 参考前景：病例特定的`target_label`
- 最终任务得分：所有任务3帧/病例的均值

## 评估说明

- 当可用时，HD和ASD使用物理间距；否则使用单位间距。
- 缺失或无效预测收到惩罚指标：`DSC = 0`、`HD = 大惩罚值`、`ASD = 大惩罚值`。
- 如果评估的某个类的预测和参考都为空，该类被视为完美匹配：`DSC = 1`、`HD = 0`、`ASD = 0`。
- JSON文件中的预测路径必须是对应任务输出文件夹下的相对路径。绝对路径和`../`遍历会被拒绝。

## 排行榜列

最终排行榜报告：

- `Task1_DSC`、`Task1_HD`、`Task1_ASD`
- `Task2_DSC`、`Task2_HD`、`Task2_ASD`
- `Task3_DSC`、`Task3_HD`、`Task3_ASD`
- `Evaluation_Status`
- `Runtime_Seconds`

`Evaluation_Status = 1`表示组织方运行器成功完成。`Evaluation_Status = 0`表示描述符验证、镜像拉取、推理或评分失败；失败的提交将收到惩罚指标。

## 参与者结果摘要

成功完成最终测试提交后，参与者将看到每个任务三个平均指标的排行榜值。在最终隐藏测试阶段不显示按病例或按图像的得分。

详细结果摘要遵循以下结构：

```text
MVAA最终隐藏测试评估
状态：完成
信息：官方隐藏测试评估已完成

任务级平均指标：
- 任务1（CT）：平均DSC = ...、平均HD = ...、平均ASD = ...
- 任务2（TEE）：平均DSC = ...、平均HD = ...、平均ASD = ...
- 任务3（视频/图像）：平均DSC = ...、平均HD = ...、平均ASD = ...

Evaluation_Status：1
Runtime_Seconds：...
```

pages.title: Final Ranking
pages.content:
# Final Score, Prizes, and Certificates


The official overall ranking will be based on normalized metric scores from the final hidden-test evaluation. The raw leaderboard metrics will remain visible for transparency, while the normalized score will be used for final ranking and award decisions.

Because Task 2 uses a public dataset, its three normalized metric scores will be assigned as 100 points for all eligible teams to avoid unfair advantage from public test-set information.

To be eligible for prize money, a team must satisfy the participation rules, rank in the overall top 10, and, barring exceptional circumstances approved by the organizers, must attend the onsite presentation.

In addition to the overall awards, the top three teams in Task 1 and the top three teams in Task 3 will receive additional task-specific certificates.
pages.content_zh:
# 最终成绩、奖项和证书

最终官方总体排名将基于最终隐藏测试评估中的标准化指标得分。原始排行榜指标将保持可见以确保透明度，而标准化得分将用于最终排名和奖项决策。

由于第2任务使用公开数据集，其三个标准化指标得分将为所有符合条件的团队分配100分，以避免公开测试集信息带来的不公平优势。

要获得奖金资格，团队必须满足参赛规则、总体排名前10，以及除组织者批准的特殊情况外，必须参加现场展示。

除总体奖项外，第1任务排名前三和第3任务排名前三的团队将获得额外的任务特定证书。

pages.title: Participation Rules
pages.content:
# MVAA Challenge - Participation Rules

## 1. Challenge Life Cycle

The final test stage uses hidden data and Docker-based evaluation. The official ranking is determined by running each accepted Docker submission on the hidden test set and applying the normalized final score described on the **Final Ranking** page.

## 2. Participation Policies

### 2.1 Algorithm Development

- Task 1 and Task 3 encourage semi-supervised learning using the released labeled and unlabeled data.
- Task 2 is a supervised 3D TEE segmentation task.
- Public external datasets and public pre-trained models are allowed.
- Private datasets, private annotations of public data, and hidden test data leakage are strictly prohibited.

### 2.2 Organizer Institute Participants

Members of the organizers' institutes may participate but are not eligible for awards and will not be listed in the official award ranking.

## 3. Final Docker Submission Rules

### 3.1 Submission Method

Participants must submit a `submission.zip` file containing a root-level `submission.json` with a Docker image reference.

Direct prediction-mask uploads are not used for final hidden-test ranking.

### 3.2 Docker Image Requirements

The Docker image must include:

- inference code;
- model weights;
- all runtime dependencies;
- a default entrypoint that runs inference automatically.

The Docker image must not require internet access during evaluation. Runtime network access may be restricted or disabled by the organizers.

### 3.3 Runtime Environment

The organizer-side runner will provide:

- `/input`: hidden test inputs, read-only;
- `/output`: prediction output directory, writable;
- one NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB GPU;
- runtime network access may be restricted or disabled.

### 3.4 Submission Limits

Each team may submit up to 15 times in total during the final test phase. Among them, at most 10 valid submissions are allowed for each team.

The additional 5 submission attempts are reserved for possible technical failures, such as descriptor-format errors, image-pulling failures, platform errors, or other unexpected submission issues. These failed or invalid attempts may be excluded from the valid-submission count at the organizers' discretion.

Among the 10 valid submissions, 3 additional valid attempts have been granted to all teams due to the update of the Task 3 HD/ASD evaluation rule.

The submission limit applies to the team as a whole, not to individual CodaBench accounts. Submissions made from different accounts belonging to the same team will be counted together. If members of the same team use multiple accounts to bypass the submission limit, the team may be disqualified.

This rule is intended to ensure fairness for smaller teams.

## 4. Award Policy

1. The official overall ranking is based on the normalized final score described on the **Final Ranking** page.
2. A total prize pool of 10,000 RMB will be awarded to eligible teams in the overall top 10 after score verification and rule-compliance checks.
3. To receive prize money, an eligible top-10 team must attend the onsite presentation unless exceptional circumstances are approved by the organizers.
4. In addition to the overall awards, the top three teams in Task 1 and the top three teams in Task 3 will receive additional task-specific certificates.
5. Outstanding teams may be encouraged to submit extended versions of their methods to a related journal special issue.
6. Eligible top teams may be invited to contribute to the challenge summary paper.

## 5. Result Announcement

Official final results will be announced after the organizers have completed hidden-test execution, score verification, and rule-compliance checks.

## 6. Publication Policy

Participating teams may publish their methods separately, while respecting challenge data usage rules and collective challenge contributions.

## 7. Code Availability Requirement

Algorithm code release through a public GitHub repository and the submission of a corresponding conference paper are prerequisites for award eligibility.
pages.content_zh:
# MVAA 挑战赛 - 参赛规则

## 1. 挑战赛生命周期

最终测试阶段使用隐藏数据和基于Docker的评估。官方排名通过在隐藏测试集上运行每个被接受的Docker提交，并应用**最终排名**页面所述的归一化最终分数来确定。

## 2. 参赛政策

### 2.1 算法开发

- 任务1和任务3鼓励使用发布的标注数据和未标注数据进行半监督学习。
- 任务2是一项有监督的3D TEE分割任务。
- 允许使用公开外部数据集和公开预训练模型。
- 严格禁止使用私有数据集、公开数据的私有标注以及隐藏测试数据泄露。

### 2.2 组织机构参与者

组织者所在机构的成员可以参赛，但无资格获得奖项，不会列入官方获奖排名。

## 3. 最终Docker提交规则

### 3.1 提交方式

参赛者必须提交一个`submission.zip`文件，其中包含根目录级别的`submission.json`和Docker镜像引用。

最终隐藏测试排名不使用直接上传预测掩码的方式。

### 3.2 Docker镜像要求

Docker镜像必须包含：

- 推理代码；
- 模型权重；
- 所有运行时依赖项；
- 自动运行推理的默认入口点。

Docker镜像在评估期间不得要求互联网访问。运行时网络访问可能受到组织者的限制或禁用。

### 3.3 运行时环境

组织者端的运行器将提供：

- `/input`：隐藏测试输入，只读；
- `/output`：预测输出目录，可写；
- 一块NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB GPU；
- 运行时网络访问可能受到限制或禁用。

### 3.4 提交限制

每个团队在最终测试阶段总共最多可提交10次。其中，每个团队最多允许7次有效提交。

额外的3次提交机会预留用于可能的技术故障，例如描述符格式错误、镜像拉取失败、平台错误或其他意外提交问题。这些失败或无效的提交可由组织者酌情从有效提交计数中排除。

提交限制适用于整个团队，而非个别CodaBench账户。来自同一团队不同账户的提交将累计计算。如果同一团队的成员使用多个账户绕过提交限制，该团队可能被取消资格。

该规则旨在确保较小团队的公平性。

## 4. 奖励政策

1. 官方总体排名基于**最终排名**页面所述的归一化最终分数。
2. 总奖金池为10,000元人民币，将奖励在分数验证和规则合规检查后排名前10的合格团队。
3. 符合条件的前10名团队若要获得奖金，必须参加现场报告，除非获得组织者的特殊批准。
4. 除总体奖项外，任务1前三名团队和任务3前三名团队将获得额外的任务特定证书。
5. 杰出团队可被鼓励向相关期刊特刊提交其方法的扩展版本。
6. 符合条件的前列团队可被邀请为挑战赛总结论文做贡献。

## 5. 结果公布

官方最终结果将在组织者完成隐藏测试执行、分数验证和规则合规检查后公布。

## 6. 出版政策

参赛团队可单独发表其方法，同时应遵守挑战赛数据使用规则和集体挑战赛贡献规范。

## 7. 代码可用性要求

通过公开GitHub仓库发布算法代码和提交相应的会议论文是获得奖项资格的前置条件。

pages.content:
﻿# MVAA Challenge - Technical Support

## 1. Platform Role

This CodaBench portal collects final Docker submission descriptors and returns official hidden-test scores. The descriptor is first validated by CodaBench, then a private organizer-side CodaBench worker forwards the Docker image reference to the MVAA GPU runner.

## 2. Final Evaluation Server

The official final-test runner uses a standardized GPU server:

```text
GPU: NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB
CUDA driver: 550.x / CUDA 12.4
Compute capability: sm_70
Runtime network inside participant container: disabled
```

Participant containers are run with `/input` mounted read-only and `/output` mounted writable.

## 3. Recommended Local Validation

Before submitting, participants should test their image locally:

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all \
  --network none \
  -v /path/to/test_input:/input:ro \
  -v /path/to/output:/output:rw \
  your-image:final
```

The container should exit with code `0` and write prediction JSON files and masks under `/output`.

## 4. Common Failure Reasons

- `submission.json` is not at the root of `submission.zip`.
- The `image` field is missing or contains whitespace/control characters.
- The Docker image is private and the organizers cannot pull it.
- The Docker image requires internet access at runtime.
- The container does not have an automatic entrypoint.
- The image is not compatible with NVIDIA V100 / `sm_70`.
- Prediction files are missing or paths in prediction JSON contain absolute paths or `../`.
- The container exceeds the configured runtime, memory, or disk limits.

## 5. Technical Contact

For technical issues regarding Docker submission, data integrity, or evaluation scripts, please contact:

- Technical Lead: [dbd2002@foxmail.com](mailto:dbd2002@foxmail.com)
- Challenge Contact: [dbd2002@foxmail.com](mailto:dbd2002@foxmail.com)

pages.title: Future Plans
pages.content:
# MVAA Challenge - Publication & Future Plans

The MVAA challenge has a comprehensive publication framework, with a focus on clinical relevance, methodological novelty, and long-term multimodal benchmark development.

## 1. Conference Proceedings Publication
* **Springer LNCS:** We will coordinate post-conference proceedings, enabling participating teams to publish detailed method descriptions in the **Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS)** volumes linked to the 1st MICCAI Workshop on Medical World Models (MWM).
* **Open Access:** This mechanism ensures that all successful technical contributions are publicly available and citeable within the MICCAI ecosystem.

## 2. Journal Special Issue Submission
* **Outstanding Contributions:** High-impact submissions will be invited to submit extended manuscripts to the **IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering (TBME)** Special Issue entitled: *“Digital Twins, Simulation-Based AI and Medical World Models.”*
* **Selection Criteria:** Evaluation goes beyond leaderboard ranking, focusing on methodological novelty, cross-modal generalization, and real-world clinical deployment potential for mitral valve analysis.

## 3. Challenge Summary Manuscripts
* **Journal-level Summary:** We will coordinate a comprehensive challenge summary manuscript to report and analyze MVAA outcomes.
* **Analysis:** Content will include a meta-analysis of all participating methods, key findings in multimodal segmentation, and research trends in structural heart disease analysis.
* **Purpose:** This paper serves as an authoritative reference for the community, informing future research directions in unified anatomical modeling.

## 4. Long-Term Future Plans
1. **Annual Repeated Event:** Maintain the challenge as an **annual event** with fixed MICCAI deadlines, continuously expanding the dataset with new multimodal clinical data.
2. **Integration with World Models:** Further integrate the benchmark with **medical world models and digital twin frameworks**, extending mitral valve analysis to longitudinal and predictive surgical modeling.
3. **Clinical Translation:** Promote the translation of top-performing algorithms into clinical tools for mitral valve repair, TEER, and annuloplasty, reducing operator dependence and improving intervention safety.
4. **Global Collaboration:** Establish a sustainable consortium for multimodal heart research, fostering ongoing collaboration between clinicians, sonographers, and AI researchers.

# MVAA挑战赛 - 发表计划与未来规划

MVAA挑战赛拥有全面的发表框架，重点关注临床相关性、方法学创新性和长期多模态基准的开发。

## 1. 会议论文集发表
* **Springer LNCS：** 我们将协调会后论文集，使参赛团队能够在与第一届MICCAI医学世界模型研讨会（MWM）相关的**Springer计算机科学讲义（LNCS）**卷中发表详细的方法描述。
* **开放获取：** 此机制确保所有成功的技术贡献在MICCAI生态系统内可公开获取且可引用。

## 2. 期刊特刊投稿
* **优秀贡献：** 高影响力的投稿将被邀请向**IEEE生物医学工程汇刊（TBME）**特刊提交扩展稿件，特刊主题为：*"数字孪生、基于仿真的人工智能和医学世界模型"*
* **遴选标准：** 评估超越排行榜排名，重点关注方法学创新性、跨模态泛化能力和二尖瓣分析的真实临床应用潜力。

## 3. 挑战赛总结论文
* **期刊级总结：** 我们将协调编写综合性挑战赛总结论文，以报告和分析MVAA的成果。
* **分析内容：** 包括所有参赛方法的荟萃分析、多模态分割的关键发现，以及结构性心脏病分析研究趋势。
* **目的：** 本论文作为业界权威参考资料，为统一解剖学建模的未来研究方向提供指导。

## 4. 长期未来规划
1. **年度持续赛事：** 将挑战赛作为**年度赛事**维持运营，遵循固定的MICCAI截止期限，持续扩展数据集并纳入新的多模态临床数据。
2. **与世界模型的融合：** 进一步将基准与**医学世界模型和数字孪生框架**整合，将二尖瓣分析扩展到纵向和预测性手术建模。
3. **临床转化：** 推进高性能算法向二尖瓣修复、经导管二尖瓣边缘对边缘修复（TEER）和环成形术等临床工具的转化，降低操作者依赖性并提高干预安全性。
4. **全球协作：** 建立可持续的多模态心脏研究联盟，促进临床医生、超声医学医生和AI研究人员之间的持续合作。

pages.content:
# Q&A

## What should I submit in the final test phase?

Submit `submission.zip` containing a root-level `submission.json` with your Docker image reference.

## Do I upload model weights separately?

No. Your Docker image must include all model weights and dependencies needed for inference.

## Will my Docker container have internet access?

Your image must not require internet access during hidden-test evaluation. Runtime network access may be restricted or disabled by the organizers.

## Where are the hidden test images mounted?

The hidden test inputs are mounted at `/input` inside your container.

## Where should predictions be written?

Write all prediction JSON files and masks under `/output`.

## Does the CodaBench leaderboard show final DSC/HD/ASD scores?

Yes. After descriptor validation, the private organizer-side worker runs the submitted image on the hidden test set and returns official Task1/Task2/Task3 DSC, HD, and ASD metrics to this leaderboard.

## Why might my row show Evaluation_Status = 0?

`Evaluation_Status = 0` means validation, image pulling, container execution, output checking, or scoring failed. Check the submission logs and the `Message` line in the detailed score output.

## Which GPU should my image support?

The official runner uses NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB. Your image must support compute capability `sm_70`.

## Will my Docker image reference be visible to other participants?

No. The Docker image reference is used for organizer-side evaluation and is not shown in the public leaderboard or detailed result page. If you need to protect code or weights, use a private registry and provide pull access to the organizers.
## Is there a reference baseline Docker image?

Yes. Participants may pull the public reference baseline image to inspect the expected Docker-based inference style:

```bash
docker pull db0725/mvaa-baseline-infer:final-20260626
```

This image is only a reference example. Participants may submit their own Docker images as long as they follow the required input/output contract.

## How many final-test submissions are allowed?

Each team may submit up to 15 times in total during the final test phase. Among them, at most 10 valid submissions are allowed for each team.

The additional 5 submission attempts are reserved for possible technical failures, such as descriptor-format errors, image-pulling failures, platform errors, or other unexpected submission issues. These failed or invalid attempts may be excluded from the valid-submission count at the organizers' discretion.

Among the 10 valid submissions, 3 additional valid attempts have been granted to all teams due to the update of the Task 3 HD/ASD evaluation rule.

The limit applies to the team as a whole, not to individual CodaBench accounts. If members of the same team use multiple accounts to bypass the submission limit, the team may be disqualified. This rule is intended to ensure fairness for smaller teams.

# 问答

## 最终测试阶段应该提交什么？

提交包含根目录级 `submission.json` 的 `submission.zip`，其中包含您的 Docker 镜像参考。

## 是否需要单独上传模型权重？

否。您的 Docker 镜像必须包含推理所需的所有模型权重和依赖项。

## Docker 容器是否具有互联网访问权限？

您的镜像不得在隐藏测试评估期间需要互联网访问。组织者可能会限制或禁用运行时网络访问。

## 隐藏测试图像安装在哪里？

隐藏测试输入安装在容器内的 `/input`。

## 预测结果应写入何处？

将所有预测 JSON 文件和掩码写入 `/output`。

## CodaBench 排行榜是否显示最终的 DSC/HD/ASD 分数？

是的。描述符验证后，私有组织者端工作程序在隐藏测试集上运行提交的镜像，并将官方 Task1/Task2/Task3 的 DSC、HD 和 ASD 指标返回到此排行榜。

## 为什么我的行可能显示 Evaluation_Status = 0？

`Evaluation_Status = 0` 表示验证、镜像拉取、容器执行、输出检查或评分失败。检查提交日志和详细评分输出中的 `Message` 行。

## 我的镜像应该支持哪个 GPU？

官方运行器使用 NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB。您的镜像必须支持计算能力 `sm_70`。

## 其他参赛者能否看到我的 Docker 镜像参考？

否。Docker 镜像参考仅用于组织者端评估，不会在公共排行榜或详细结果页面中显示。如果需要保护代码或权重，请使用私有注册表并向组织者提供拉取访问权限。

## 是否有参考基线 Docker 镜像？

是的。参赛者可以拉取公共参考基线镜像以查看预期的基于 Docker 的推理风格：

```bash
docker pull db0725/mvaa-baseline-infer:final-20260626
```

此镜像仅是参考示例。参赛者可以提交自己的 Docker 镜像，只要它们遵循所需的输入/输出约定。

## 最终测试阶段允许多少次提交？

每个团队在最终测试阶段总共可提交最多 10 次。其中，每个团队最多允许 7 次有效提交。

额外的 3 次提交尝试保留用于可能的技术故障，例如描述符格式错误、镜像拉取失败、平台错误或其他意外提交问题。这些失败或无效的尝试可能被组织者自行决定排除在有效提交计数之外。

该限制适用于整个团队，而不是单个 CodaBench 账户。如果同一团队的成员使用多个账户绕过提交限制，该团队可能被取消资格。此规则旨在确保较小团队的公平性。

二尖瓣评估在结构性心脏病的诊断、治疗规划和术中引导中起着核心作用。在临床实践中，医生依赖具有非常不同特征的多模态影像数据，包括用于术前几何结构的心脏CT、用于术中解剖参考的3D经食管超声心动图，以及用于直接手术观察的选定术中帧。然而，跨这些模态的手动分析仍然劳动密集且受观察者间变异性的影响。 MVAA挑战赛旨在通过提供跨多种影像模态和手术阶段的统一基准来推进自动化二尖瓣分析。鼓励参赛者开发稳健的分割和解剖分析方法，这些方法在异构数据源上保持一致，并支持临床意义的下游应用。 ## 挑战赛目标 开发用于跨CT、3D TEE和术中图像帧的多模态二尖瓣解剖分析的自动化方法，评估重点关注分割质量、结构一致性和临床相关性。 **具体目标：** - 建立涵盖术前、术中和手术影像数据的二尖瓣分析多模态基准。 - 评估算法在多样化影像特征和临床条件下的准确分割和解剖理解能力。 - 鼓励开发在模态间具有良好泛化性能同时保留二尖瓣连贯结构表示的模型。 - 促进AI研究人员、影像科学家和心脏介入临床专家之间的协作。 ## 资源 - **挑战赛网站:** https://mwm2026.github.io/mvaa - **数据集(训练与验证) - 链接1:** 任务1和任务2的完整数据，加上任务3的标注数据: https://drive.google.com/file/d/14WneBUBZ1X4p69tRdRzximNb0IsWuh2B/view?usp=sharing - **数据集(训练与验证) - 链接2:** 任务3的未标注数据: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1K4vFo-4pdL1_xt-8msO-32bc2aEdJ7wS/view?usp=sharing - **基线代码:** https://github.com/db0725/MVAA - **联系方式:** dbd2002@foxmail.com

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# Mitral Valve Anatomy Analysis Using Multimodal Imaging Data ## MICCAI 2026 Challenge - International Workshop on Medical World Models (MWM)
Mitral valve assessment plays a central role in the diagnosis, treatment planning, and intraoperative guidance of structural heart disease. In clinical practice, physicians rely on multimodal imaging data with very different characteristics, including cardiac CT for pre-procedural geometry, 3D transesophageal echocardiography for intraoperative anatomical reference, and selected intraoperative frames for direct procedural observation. However, manual analysis across these modalities remains labor-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability. The MVAA challenge aims to advance automated mitral valve analysis by providing a unified benchmark across multiple imaging modalities and surgical stages. Participants are encouraged to develop robust methods for segmentation and anatomy analysis that remain consistent across heterogeneous data sources and support clinically meaningful downstream use. ## Aim of the Challenge To develop automated methods for multimodal mitral valve anatomy analysis across CT, 3D TEE, and intraoperative image frames, with evaluation focused on segmentation quality, structural consistency, and clinical relevance. **Objectives:** - To establish a multimodal benchmark for mitral valve analysis spanning pre-operative, intraoperative, and procedural imaging data. - To evaluate algorithms for accurate segmentation and anatomy understanding under diverse image characteristics and clinical conditions. - To encourage models that generalize across modalities while preserving coherent structural representations of the mitral valve. - To promote collaboration between AI researchers, imaging scientists, and clinical experts in cardiac intervention. ## Resources - **Challenge website:** https://mwm2026.github.io/mvaa - **Dataset (Training & Validation) - Link 1:** Full data for Task 1 and Task 2, plus the labeled data for Task 3: https://drive.google.com/file/d/14WneBUBZ1X4p69tRdRzximNb0IsWuh2B/view?usp=sharing - **Dataset (Training & Validation) - Link 2:** Unlabeled data for Task 3: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1K4vFo-4pdL1_xt-8msO-32bc2aEdJ7wS/view?usp=sharing - **Baseline code:** https://github.com/db0725/MVAA - **Contact:** dbd2002@foxmail.com
pages.content_zh:
# 核心任务

MVAA挑战赛旨在反映跨多种成像模式的真实临床工作流程。该挑战赛分为三个主要分割任务。

### 参赛和模型提交要求

参赛者需要完成并提交全部三个任务的结果。最终排名将基于三个任务的综合性能确定；因此，仅提交一个或两个任务的结果不足以进行最终排名。

但是，参赛者无需使用单一的统一多模态模型。每个任务可以独立处理，参赛者可以为CT、3D TEE和手术视频帧分割任务分别训练并提交不同的模型。

### 任务1：心脏CT中的二尖瓣分割
该任务重点关注从3D心脏CT扫描中自动进行多类解剖分割。
*   **目标：** 参赛者需要分割二尖瓣环和前/后瓣叶。
*   **临床意义：** 高分辨率CT分割提供了术前规划所需的精确空间几何信息，包括装置尺寸确定和经导管二尖瓣边缘修复术（TEER）或环成形术等介入治疗的修复策略选择。

### 任务2：三维经食管超声心动图（3D TEE）中的二尖瓣分割
该任务解决从容积3D TEE（超声）数据中分割瓣膜结构的问题，这是术中瓣膜功能的关键参考。
*   **目标：** 从3D超声容积中描绘瓣叶。
*   **技术重点：** 算法必须足够稳健，能够处理超声特有的伪影、声学噪声、信号丢失以及瓣叶与周围心脏组织之间的模糊边界。

### 任务3：手术视频帧中的二尖瓣分割
该任务重点关注从术中手术视频提取的单帧中提取解剖信息。
*   **目标：** 从外科医生直视角度看到的二尖瓣结构的像素级分割。
*   **方法论：** 虽然数据源自视频录制，但该任务被定义为基于帧的分割问题。参赛者应在训练和推理中将提供的帧视为单独的2D图像。
*   **临床重点：** 该任务能够在实际介入治疗中验证瓣叶运动和结构连续性，在手术环境中提供实时反馈。

pages.content_zh:
# MVAA挑战 - 数据系统

## 1. 伦理批准与数据许可

### 1.1 伦理批准
所有数据已匿名处理，获得医学伦理委员会批准（编号：KY-N-2022-048-01）。

### 1.2 数据使用协议与许可
* **许可证：** CC BY-NC（署名-非商业性使用）
* 禁止对数据进行商业使用；所有使用方式必须符合许可证条款。

## 2. 数据来源

### 2.1 采集设备
* **心脏CT：** 西门子医疗、GE医疗、飞利浦医疗和佳能医疗系统。
* **3D经食管超声心动图（TEE）：** 飞利浦Epiq心脏超声系统。
* **手术视频：** 标准内镜视频录制器（720p，30fps）。

### 2.2 采集中心
数据来自多个临床中心，包括：
* 广东省人民医院
* 暨南大学第一附属医院
* 东莞东城中央医院

## 3. 数据集规模与分割

### 3.1 任务1：心脏CT分割
* **训练集：** 共1,067张图像（27张含标注，1,040张无标注用于半监督学习）。
* **验证集：** 30张图像（无标注）。

### 3.2 任务2：3D TEE分割
* **训练集：** 105张含标注的图像。
* **验证集：** 20张图像（无标注）。

### 3.3 任务3：手术帧分割

* **训练集：** 共1,559帧。
    * **标注数据：** 180帧（其中118帧包含二尖瓣）。
    * **无标注数据：** 1,379帧（用于半监督学习）。
* **验证集：** 48张图像（无标注，全部包含二尖瓣结构用于评分）。

#### 3.3.1 任务3标注说明

任务3的标注可能包括二尖瓣以外的解剖结构注释。仅二尖瓣标注用于训练和评估。在本任务中，二尖瓣是唯一的目标分割类别。

参赛者应使用每个`*_Label.tar`压缩包内的`*_Label.nii.gz`文件作为真实标注的来源，并参考相应`*_Label.json`文件中的类别映射表进行确认。具体而言，类别ID `10` 对应二尖瓣。

`*_Label.json`文件仅供查看类别名称、颜色和元数据之用，不应作为训练标注的主要来源。

JSON文件中的某些多边形注释可能不完整或为空；因此不建议从`Polys.Shapes`生成训练标注。180帧标注数据中，118帧包含有效的二尖瓣注释。无标注帧中也可能包含没有可见二尖瓣结构的图像。

## 4. 数据新颖性
* **多模态数据资源：** 本挑战包括来自多个临床中心的心脏CT、3D TEE和手术视频数据。在当前公开发布版本中，这些模态作为独立数据集提供，不包含正式的CT-视频配对元数据或病例映射表。
* **未发表数据：** 为确保泛化能力的公平评估，提供了140多张新采集的、未发表的超声图像用于验证和测试。

## 5. 纳入与排除标准

### 5.1 纳入标准
1. 适合二尖瓣评估的标准临床心脏切面。
2. 图像质量足以支持专家对瓣叶和瓣环进行标注。
3. 具有相应的临床测量参考值。

### 5.2 排除标准
1. 严重成像伪影或信号丢失，影响解剖结构可见性。
2. 重复或损坏的数据。
3. 临床参考测量值不确定的病例。

## 6. 标注特征

### 6.1 标注方法
* **两阶段流程：** 由两名经过培训的医学专家进行初始标注，随后由具有10年以上经验的获证放射科医生进行审查和完善。
* **半自动化完善：** 对于超声数据，初始自动分割之后由两名标注者进行手动审查和修改，直至达成一致意见。

### 6.2 标注质量

pages.title: Core Task
pages.content:
# Core Task

The MVAA challenge is designed to reflect the real-world clinical workflow across multiple imaging modalities. The challenge is structured into three primary segmentation tasks.

### Participation and Model Submission Requirements

Participants are required to complete and submit results for all three tasks. The final ranking will be determined based on the combined performance across the three tasks; therefore, submissions for only one or two tasks will not be sufficient for the final ranking.

However, participants are not required to use a single unified multimodal model. Each task may be addressed independently, and participants may train and submit separate models for the CT, 3D TEE, and surgical video frame segmentation tasks.

### Task 1: Mitral Valve Segmentation in Cardiac CT
This task focuses on the automated, multi-class anatomical segmentation of the mitral valve from 3D cardiac CT scans.
*   **Target:** Participants are required to segment the mitral annulus and the anterior/posterior leaflets.
*   **Clinical Significance:** High-resolution CT segmentation provides the precise spatial geometry necessary for pre-procedural planning, including device sizing and the selection of repair strategies for interventions like TEER or annuloplasty.

### Task 2: Mitral Valve Segmentation in 3D Transesophageal Echocardiography (3D TEE)
This task addresses the segmentation of valve structures from volumetric 3D TEE (ultrasound) data, which serves as the key intraoperative reference for valve function.
*   **Target:** Delineation of the valve leaflets from 3D ultrasound volumes.
*   **Technical Focus:** Algorithms must be robust enough to handle ultrasound-specific artifacts, acoustic noise, signal dropout, and ambiguous boundaries between the leaflets and surrounding cardiac tissues.

### Task 3: Mitral Valve Segmentation from Surgical Video Frames
This task focuses on extracting anatomical information from individual frames extracted from intraoperative surgical videos.
*   **Target:** Pixel-level segmentation of the mitral valve structures as seen from the surgeon's direct viewpoint.
*   **Methodology:** Although the data originates from video recordings, this task is defined as a frame-based segmentation problem. Participants should treat the provided frames as individual 2D images for training and inference.
*   **Clinical Focus:** This task enables the verification of leaflet motion and structural continuity during the actual intervention, providing real-time feedback within the surgical environment.

# 评估指标

本挑战赛中的所有任务均使用三个标准分割指标进行评估：Dice相似系数（DSC）、Hausdorff距离（HD）和平均表面距离（ASD）。这些指标衡量提交分割与参考标注之间的区域重叠和边界精度。

对于每个案例，预测结果与相应的真实标签进行比较。最终任务级结果通过对所有评估案例的案例级指标值进行平均得到。

## 1. 指标定义

### Dice相似系数（DSC）
Dice分数衡量预测分割与真实标签之间的重叠程度。
- **范围：** [0, 1]，其中1表示完美重叠。
- **定义：** DSC计算为两个掩模的交集的两倍除以其体积或面积之和。
- **解释：** DSC值越高表示分割重叠效果越好。

### Hausdorff距离（HD）
Hausdorff距离通过测量预测结果与真实标签之间的最大表面偏差来评估边界精度。
- **定义：** HD计算为预测掩模与参考掩模之间的双向表面到表面距离的最大值。
- **实现：** 从二值掩模中提取表面，当存在图像间距元数据时使用其进行欧几里得距离计算。
- **解释：** HD值越低表示边界对齐效果越好。

### 平均表面距离（ASD）
ASD衡量预测表面与真实标签表面之间的平均距离。
- **定义：** ASD计算为从预测表面到参考表面的距离与从参考表面到预测表面的距离的对称平均值。
- **实现：** 与HD相同，距离计算在可用时使用图像间距。
- **解释：** ASD值越低表示总体形状一致性越好。

## 2. 任务特定计算

### 任务1：CT分割
任务1作为3D分割任务进行评估。
- **前景定义：** 标签`1`
- **案例级计算：** 对每个案例的二值前景掩模计算DSC、HD和ASD。
- **最终任务结果：** 所有案例级值的平均值。

### 任务2：TEE分割
任务2作为3D多类别分割任务进行评估。
- **前景定义：** 标签`1`和`2`
- **案例级计算：** 分别为每个前景类别计算指标，并在每个案例内对类别级指标值进行平均。
- **最终任务结果：** 所有案例级值的平均值。

### 任务3：视频/图像分割
任务3作为2D分割任务进行评估。
- **前景定义：** 预测结果被视为二值前景掩模，并与真实标签中案例特定的`target_label`进行比较。
- **案例级计算：** 对每个案例或帧计算DSC、HD和ASD。
- **最终任务结果：** 所有案例级值的平均值。

## 3. 重要评估说明

- **间距感知型距离指标：** 当间距元数据可用时，HD和ASD使用物理间距进行计算；否则使用单位间距。
- **对称表面距离：** HD和ASD都在预测和参考表面之间双向计算。
- **缺失或无效预测：** 如果案例缺失或无法评估，将施加惩罚（`DSC = 0`，`HD = 大惩罚值`，`ASD = 大惩罚值`）。
- **空掩模处理：** 如果对于评估的类别预测和真实标签都为空，则将该案例视为完美匹配（`DSC = 1`，`HD = 0`，`ASD = 0`）。

## 4. 排名策略

官方评估程序包分别报告每个任务的三个指标：
- `Task1_DSC`、`Task1_HD`、`Task1_ASD`
- `Task2_DSC`、`Task2_HD`、`Task2_ASD`
- `Task3_DSC`、`Task3_HD`、`Task3_ASD`

# MVAA Challenge - Dataset System

## 1. Ethics Approval & Data License

### 1.1 Ethics Approval
All data is anonymized, with approval from the Medical Ethics Committee (No. KY-N-2022-048-01).

### 1.2 Data Usage Agreement & License
* **License:** CC BY-NC (Attribution-NonCommercial)
* No commercial use of the data is permitted; all usage must comply with the license terms.

## 2. Data Source

### 2.1 Acquisition Devices
* **Cardiac CT:** Siemens Healthineers, GE Healthcare, Philips Healthcare, and Canon Medical Systems.
* **3D TEE:** Philips Epiq cardiac ultrasound system.
* **Surgical Video:** Standard endoscopic video recorder (720p, 30fps).

### 2.2 Acquisition Centers
The dataset is collected from multiple clinical centers, including:
* Guangdong Provincial People’s Hospital
* The First Affiliated Hospital of Jinan University
* Dongguan Eastern Central Hospital

## 3. Dataset Scale & Partition

### 3.1 Task 1: Cardiac CT Segmentation
* **Training Set:** 1,067 images total (27 with ground-truth labels, 1,040 unlabeled for semi-supervised learning).
* **Validation Set:** 30 images (without labels).

### 3.2 Task 2: 3D TEE Segmentation
* **Training Set:** 105 images with ground-truth labels.
* **Validation Set:** 20 images (without labels).

### 3.3 Task 3: Surgical Frame Segmentation

* **Training Set:** 1,559 frames total.
    * **Labeled Data:** 180 frames (118 frames contain the mitral valve).
    * **Unlabeled Data:** 1,379 frames (for semi-supervised learning).
* **Validation Set:** 48 images (without labels, all containing mitral valve structures for scoring).

#### 3.3.1 Task 3 Label Note

Task 3 labels may include annotations beyond the mitral valve. Only the mitral valve label is used for training and evaluation. In this task, the mitral valve is the only target segmentation class.

Participants should use the `*_Label.nii.gz` file within each `*_Label.tar` archive as the source of ground-truth annotations, and refer to the category mapping table in the corresponding `*_Label.json` file for confirmation. Specifically, category ID `10` corresponds to the mitral valve.

The `*_Label.json` file is intended only for reading category names, colors, and metadata, and should not be used as the primary label source for training.

Some polygon annotations in the JSON files are incomplete or empty; therefore, generating training labels from `Polys.Shapes` is not recommended. Of the 180 labeled frames, 118 contain valid mitral valve annotations. Unlabeled frames may also include images without visible mitral valve structures.


## 4. Data Novelty
* **Multi-modal Data Resource:** The challenge includes cardiac CT, 3D TEE, and surgical video data collected from multiple clinical centers. In the current public release, these modalities are provided as independent datasets, and no formal CT-video pairing metadata or case mapping table is included.
* **Unpublished Data:** More than 140 newly collected, unpublished ultrasound images have been provided for validation and testing to ensure fair evaluation of generalization.

## 5. Inclusion & Exclusion Criteria

### 5.1 Inclusion Criteria
1. Standard clinical cardiac views suitable for mitral valve assessment.
2. Sufficient image quality for expert annotation of leaflets and annulus.
3. Availability of corresponding clinical measurement references.

### 5.2 Exclusion Criteria
1. Severe imaging artifacts or signal dropout hindering anatomical visibility.
2. Duplicated or corrupted data.
3. Cases with uncertain clinical reference measurements.

## 6. Annotation Characteristics

### 6.1 Annotation Method
* **Two-Stage Process:** Initial annotations by two trained medical experts followed by review and refinement by a board-certified radiologist with over 10 years of experience.
* **Semi-automated refinement:** For ultrasound data, an initial automatic segmentation was followed by manual review and modification by two annotators until agreement was reached.

### 6.2 Annotation Quality Control (QC)
* **Inter-observer Reliability:** Evaluated on a subset of 30 images using ICC and absolute error distributions.
* **Adjudication:** Senior clinical specialists resolved discrepancies to ensure the reliability of reference annotations.

## 7. Data Preprocessing
1. **Anonymization:** Removal of all patient-related information from metadata.
2. **Standardization:** CT and TEE data converted to NIfTI format; surgical video frames extracted as 2D images.
3. **Resampling:** Data resampled to a consistent resolution to ensure uniform slice-level annotation.

## 8. Main Annotation Error Sources
1. **Inter-Annotator Variability:** Differences in identifying subtle mitral valve boundaries in low-contrast cases.
2. **Annotation Ambiguity:** Inherent ambiguity of valve boundaries due to pathological alterations or imaging limitations.
3. **Technical Limitations:** Errors introduced by the resolution constraints of the annotation tools.

# MVAA 挑战赛 - 参赛规则

## 1. 挑战赛生命周期
* **公开征稿:** 挑战赛在初始会议投稿截止后开放新投稿，以鼓励持续改进和长期基准测试。

## 2. 参赛政策

### 2.1 算法开发
* **任务特定学习策略:**
    * **任务1和3(半监督):** 参赛者需要使用任务1(CT)和任务3(手术视频帧)中提供的无标注数据开发半监督方法。
    * **任务2(监督学习):** 由于任务2(3D TEE)提供的所有数据集均完全标注，参赛者应重点关注该赛道的监督学习方法。
* **外部数据:** 参赛者仅允许使用公开可得的外部数据集和公开发布的预训练模型。严格禁止对公开数据进行额外的私人标注或使用私有数据集。

### 2.2 组织机构成员参赛
* 组织方机构的成员可参加挑战赛，但**不具有获奖资格**，且**不会在官方排行榜上列出**。

## 3. 提交规则

### 3.1 提交方式
* **验证阶段:** 参赛者直接向CodaBench平台提交验证集的预测分割掩模，以获得即时反馈。
* **测试阶段:** 最终评估时，参赛者必须提供**Docker容器**。这确保了透明、可重复且公平的基准测试环境。

### 3.2 提交限制
* **验证阶段:** 在验证阶段，各队最多可提交**每天2次**，以防止过度拟合。
* **最终评估:** 仅使用最后成功的Docker提交用于隐藏测试集上的排名。

## 4. 奖励政策

1. **现金奖励:** 总奖金池为**10,000元人民币**，颁发给**前10名团队**(分配详情待公布)。
2. **证书:** 为表现最佳的团队和方法最具创新性的团队提供官方证书。
3. **MICCAI 2026演讲邀请:** 前10名团队将被邀请在MICCAI 2026研讨会进行口头报告。
4. **期刊邀请:** 优秀团队将被鼓励向相关期刊特刊投稿其方法的扩展版本。
5. **挑战赛总结文章:** 共同署名挑战赛总结论文，该论文将投稿至高影响力医学影像分析期刊。

## 5. 结果公布
* 组织方将公开公布表现最好的10种方法。
* 公布内容包括团队名称和基于官方评估指标的总体排名。

## 6. 发表政策
* 前10名团队中对研究有重大贡献的成员有资格成为总结论文的作者。
* 参赛团队可分别发表各自的结果，同时尊重挑战赛的集体努力。

## 7. 代码发布要求
* 算法代码发布(通过GitHub仓库)和提交对应会议论文是**获奖资格的先决条件**。

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation Metrics

All tasks in this challenge are evaluated using three standard segmentation metrics: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff Distance (HD), and Average Surface Distance (ASD). These metrics measure both region overlap and boundary accuracy between the submitted segmentation and the reference annotation.

For each case, the prediction is compared with the corresponding ground truth mask. Final task-level results are obtained by averaging case-level metric values across all evaluated cases.

## 1. Metrics Definitions

### Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
The Dice score measures the overlap between the predicted segmentation and the ground truth.
- **Range:** [0, 1], where 1 indicates perfect overlap.
- **Definition:** DSC is computed as twice the intersection of the two masks divided by the sum of their volumes or areas.
- **Interpretation:** A higher DSC indicates better segmentation overlap.

### Hausdorff Distance (HD)
The Hausdorff Distance evaluates boundary accuracy by measuring the largest surface discrepancy between the prediction and the ground truth.
- **Definition:** HD is computed as the maximum of the bidirectional surface-to-surface distances between the predicted mask and the reference mask.
- **Implementation:** Surfaces are extracted from binary masks, and Euclidean distances are computed using image spacing when spacing metadata is available.
- **Interpretation:** A lower HD indicates better boundary alignment.

### Average Surface Distance (ASD)
ASD measures the average distance between the predicted surface and the ground truth surface.
- **Definition:** ASD is computed as the symmetric mean of the distances from the predicted surface to the reference surface and from the reference surface to the predicted surface.
- **Implementation:** As with HD, distance computation uses image spacing when available.
- **Interpretation:** A lower ASD indicates better overall shape agreement.

## 2. Task-Specific Computation

### Task 1: CT Segmentation
Task 1 is evaluated as a 3D segmentation task.
- **Foreground definition:** label `1`
- **Per-case computation:** DSC, HD, and ASD are computed on the binary foreground mask for each case.
- **Final task result:** the mean of all case-level values.

### Task 2: TEE Segmentation
Task 2 is evaluated as a 3D multi-class segmentation task.
- **Foreground definition:** labels `1` and `2`
- **Per-case computation:** metrics are computed separately for each foreground class, and the class-wise metric values are averaged within each case.
- **Final task result:** the mean of all case-level values.

### Task 3: Video/Image Segmentation
Task 3 is evaluated as a 2D segmentation task.
- **Foreground definition:** the prediction is treated as a binary foreground mask, and it is compared against the case-specific `target_label` in the ground truth.
- **Per-case computation:** DSC, HD, and ASD are computed for each case or frame.
- **Final task result:** the mean of all case-level values.

## 3. Important Evaluation Notes

- **Spacing-aware distance metrics:** HD and ASD are computed with physical spacing when spacing metadata is available; otherwise, unit spacing is used.
- **Symmetric surface distance:** Both HD and ASD are computed bidirectionally between prediction and reference surfaces.
- **Missing or invalid predictions:** If a case is missing or cannot be evaluated, a penalty is assigned (`DSC = 0`, `HD = large penalty`, `ASD = large penalty`).
- **Empty-mask handling:** If both prediction and ground truth are empty for an evaluated class, the case is treated as a perfect match for that class (`DSC = 1`, `HD = 0`, `ASD = 0`).

## 4. Ranking Strategy

The official evaluation bundle reports the three metrics separately for each task:
- `Task1_DSC`, `Task1_HD`, `Task1_ASD`
- `Task2_DSC`, `Task2_HD`, `Task2_ASD`
- `Task3_DSC`, `Task3_HD`, `Task3_ASD`

No additional normalized composite score is computed inside the current evaluation bundle. Participants should therefore interpret performance jointly across overlap accuracy (DSC) and boundary accuracy (HD and ASD), where higher DSC and lower HD/ASD indicate better performance.

## 5. Submission Result Logs

After submitting, participants can inspect the detailed evaluation output in the competition logs.
- Open the `LOGS` tab of the submission.
- Go to `Prediction Logs`.
- Check `Ingestion stdout` to view the per-task evaluation results printed by the ingestion program.
