# MVAA Challenge - Participation Rules

## 1. Challenge Life Cycle
* **Open Call:** The challenge opens for new submissions after the initial conference submission deadline to encourage continuous improvement and long-term benchmarking.

## 2. Participation Policies

### 2.1 Algorithm Development
* **Task-Specific Learning Strategies:**
    * **Tasks 1 & 3 (Semi-supervised):** Participants are required to use the provided unlabeled data in Task 1 (CT) and Task 3 (Surgical Frames) to develop semi-supervised methods. 
    * **Task 2 (Supervised):** Since all datasets provided for Task 2 (3D TEE) are fully annotated, participants should focus on supervised learning methods for this track.
* **External Data:** Participants are allowed to use only publicly available external datasets and publicly released pre-trained models. Additional private annotations of public data or the use of private datasets are strictly prohibited.

### 2.2 Organizer Institute Participants
* Members of the organizers' institutes may participate in the challenge but are **not eligible for awards** and will **not be listed in the official leaderboard**.

## 3. Submission Rules

### 3.1 Submission Method
* **Validation Phase:** Participants submit their predicted segmentation masks for the validation set directly to the CodaBench platform to receive immediate feedback.
* **Testing Phase:** For the final evaluation, participants must provide a **Docker container**. This ensures a transparent, reproducible, and fair benchmarking environment.

### 3.2 Submission Limits
* **Validation Phase:** Teams may submit up to **5 submissions per day** during the validation phase to prevent overfitting.
* **Final Evaluation:** Only the final successful Docker submission will be used for the ranking on the hidden test set.

## 4. Award Policy

1. **Cash Awards:** A total prize pool of **10,000 RMB** will be awarded to the **top 10 teams** (distribution details to be announced).
2. **Certificates:** Official certificates will be provided to the top-performing teams and the team with the most innovative method.
3. **MICCAI 2026 Presentation:** The top 10 teams will be invited to give oral presentations at the MICCAI 2026 workshop.
4. **Journal Invitation:** Outstanding teams will be encouraged to submit extended versions of their methods to a related journal special issue.
5. **Challenge Compendium:** Co-authorship of the challenge summary paper, which will be submitted to a high-impact medical image analysis journal.

## 5. Result Announcement
* The top 10 performing methods will be publicly announced by the organizers.
* The announcement will include team names and overall rankings based on the official evaluation metrics.

## 6. Publication Policy
* Members of the top-10 teams who make significant contributions to the research qualify as authors of the summary paper.
* Participating teams are allowed to publish their own results separately, respecting the collective efforts of the challenge.

## 7. Code Availability Requirement
* Algorithm code release (via a GitHub repository) and the submission of a corresponding conference paper are **prerequisites for award eligibility**.

# Timeline

All deadlines are at **23:59 (UTC+8)** on the dates listed below. Please note that these dates are subject to minor adjustments depending on the official MICCAI 2026 schedule.

## Key Milestones

* **April 15, 2026:** Training Data Release
    - Participants can download the training datasets (labeled and unlabeled) to begin model development.

* **June 01, 2026:** Validation Data Release
    - The validation set (without labels) will be released. The CodaBench leaderboard will open for preliminary scoring.

* **July 01, 2026:** Test Phase / Final Evaluation Start
    - The hidden test set evaluation phase begins. Participants will be required to prepare their final models and Docker containers.

* **September 27 - October 01, 2026:** MICCAI 2026 Conference (France)
    - The official challenge workshop, final results presentation, and award ceremony will take place during the MICCAI 2026 conference in **France**.

Any changes to the timeline will be announced via the competition website and through emails sent to registered participants.

# MVAA 挑战赛 - 发表计划与未来规划

MVAA 挑战赛具有完整的发表框架，重点关注临床相关性、方法学创新性和长期多模态基准开发。

## 1. 会议论文集发表
* **Springer LNCS:** 我们将协调会后论文集，使参赛团队能够在与第一届 MICCAI 医学世界模型研讨会 (MWM) 相关的 **Springer 计算机科学讲义 (LNCS)** 卷中发表详细的方法描述。
* **开放获取:** 该机制确保所有成功的技术贡献在 MICCAI 生态系统中公开可用且可引用。

## 2. 期刊特刊投稿
* **优秀投稿:** 高影响力的投稿将被邀请向 **IEEE 生物医学工程汇刊 (TBME)** 特刊提交扩展稿件，特刊题目为：*"数字孪生、基于仿真的人工智能与医学世界模型。"*
* **遴选标准:** 评估超越排行榜排名，重点关注方法学创新性、跨模态泛化能力和二尖瓣分析的实际临床应用潜力。

## 3. 挑战赛总结论文
* **期刊级总结:** 我们将协调编写综合性挑战赛总结论文，报告和分析 MVAA 结果。
* **分析内容:** 包括所有参赛方法的荟萃分析、多模态分割的主要发现，以及结构性心脏病分析的研究趋势。
* **目的:** 该论文作为社区的权威参考资料，为统一解剖学建模的未来研究方向提供指导。

## 4. 长期未来规划
1. **年度重复举办:** 将挑战赛作为 **年度活动** 维持运营，与 MICCAI 固定截止日期相关联，持续扩展多模态临床数据集。
2. **与世界模型集成:** 进一步将基准与 **医学世界模型和数字孪生框架** 集成，将二尖瓣分析扩展至纵向和预测性手术建模。
3. **临床转化:** 推动表现最佳的算法转化为二尖瓣修复、经导管二尖瓣边缘对边缘修复 (TEER) 和瓣环成形术的临床工具，减少操作者依赖性，提高干预安全性。
4. **全球合作:** 建立多模态心脏研究可持续联盟，促进临床医生、超声医学工作者和人工智能研究人员之间的持续协作。

* A GitHub repository URL containing the complete source code is a **prerequisite for award eligibility**.

* **Only organizers** have access to the hidden test dataset labels during the challenge.

pages.title: Future Plans
pages.content:
# MVAA Challenge - Publication & Future Plans

The MVAA challenge has a comprehensive publication framework, with a focus on clinical relevance, methodological novelty, and long-term multimodal benchmark development.

## 1. Conference Proceedings Publication
* **Springer LNCS:** We will coordinate post-conference proceedings, enabling participating teams to publish detailed method descriptions in the **Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS)** volumes linked to the 1st MICCAI Workshop on Medical World Models (MWM).
* **Open Access:** This mechanism ensures that all successful technical contributions are publicly available and citeable within the MICCAI ecosystem.

## 2. Journal Special Issue Submission
* **Outstanding Contributions:** High-impact submissions will be invited to submit extended manuscripts to the **IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering (TBME)** Special Issue entitled: *“Digital Twins, Simulation-Based AI and Medical World Models.”*
* **Selection Criteria:** Evaluation goes beyond leaderboard ranking, focusing on methodological novelty, cross-modal generalization, and real-world clinical deployment potential for mitral valve analysis.

## 3. Challenge Summary Manuscripts
* **Journal-level Summary:** We will coordinate a comprehensive challenge summary manuscript to report and analyze MVAA outcomes.
* **Analysis:** Content will include a meta-analysis of all participating methods, key findings in multimodal segmentation, and research trends in structural heart disease analysis.
* **Purpose:** This paper serves as an authoritative reference for the community, informing future research directions in unified anatomical modeling.

## 4. Long-Term Future Plans
1. **Annual Repeated Event:** Maintain the challenge as an **annual event** with fixed MICCAI deadlines, continuously expanding the dataset with new multimodal clinical data.
2. **Integration with World Models:** Further integrate the benchmark with **medical world models and digital twin frameworks**, extending mitral valve analysis to longitudinal and predictive surgical modeling.
3. **Clinical Translation:** Promote the translation of top-performing algorithms into clinical tools for mitral valve repair, TEER, and annuloplasty, reducing operator dependence and improving intervention safety.
4. **Global Collaboration:** Establish a sustainable consortium for multimodal heart research, fostering ongoing collaboration between clinicians, sonographers, and AI researchers.

16944.title: ImageEval 2026 Task 2 - CRAI-Bench - Cultural Accuracy Evaluation for Arabic Text-to-Image Generation
16944.description: Evaluate whether AI-generated images faithfully represent Qatari and Arab cultural scenes using the CRAI framework.
16944.description_zh:
# 使用CRAI框架评估AI生成图像对卡塔尔和阿拉伯文化场景的真实性表现

## 文化准确性（Cultural Accuracy）
- **服饰表现**：评估传统服装（如阿拜亚、古特拉、阿拉伯头巾）的细节准确性
- **建筑风格**：验证伊斯兰建筑元素（如拱形、穹顶、书法装饰）是否正确呈现
- **宗教仪式**：检查礼拜场景、斋月相关元素的真实性
- **社会场景**：评估家庭聚会、市集、传统活动的文化真实性

## 代表性（Representation）
- **多样性**：确保呈现卡塔尔和阿拉伯世界的多元性，避免单一刻板印象
- **地理差异**：区分不同地区的文化特征（城市、沙漠、海滨）
- **代际表现**：反映传统与现代元素的融合
- **性别与身份**：公平准确地呈现不同群体

## 人工制品与物质文化（Artifacts）
- **传统手工艺**：阿拉伯书法、陶艺、纺织品的准确性
- **日常用品**：咖啡器具、香炉等文化象征物
- **装饰元素**：几何纹样、穆斯林花纹设计的准确性
- **食文化**：传统美食呈现的真实性

## 背景与语境（Context）
- **历史准确性**：时代背景的正确性
- **社会背景**：活动场景的合理性与适切性
- **语言符号**：阿拉伯书写的准确性
- **文化敏感性**：尊重宗教和社会禁忌

pages.title: overview
pages.content:
ImageEval2026 Subtask 2: CRAI-Bench: Cultural Accuracy Evaluation for Arabic Text-to-Image Generation

CRAI-Bench evaluates whether AI-generated images faithfully represent Qatari and Arab cultural scenes. Given a reference image, a caption, and an AI-generated image produced from that caption, participants predict CRAI scores across five cultural accuracy dimensions.

CRAI Formula

CRAI = 0.30 × CEA + 0.20 × CC + 0.20 × CS + 0.20 × CI − 0.10 × HP

Score Interpretation

  • 0.85 – 1.00: Highly accurate
  • 0.70 – 0.84: Mostly accurate
  • 0.50 – 0.69: Moderately accurate
  • 0.30 – 0.49: Weak
  • Below 0.30: Poor or misleading

Contact

imageeval2026@gmail.com
pages.content_zh:
ImageEval2026 子任务2：CRAI-Bench：阿拉伯文本转图像生成的文化准确性评估

CRAI-Bench评估AI生成的图像是否真实代表卡塔尔和阿拉伯文化场景。给定参考图像、标题和从该标题生成的AI生成图像，参与者需预测五个文化准确性维度的CRAI分数。

CRAI公式

CRAI = 0.30 × CEA + 0.20 × CC + 0.20 × CS + 0.20 × CI − 0.10 × HP

分数解释

  • 0.85 – 1.00：高度准确
  • 0.70 – 0.84：基本准确
  • 0.50 – 0.69：中等准确
  • 0.30 – 0.49：较弱
  • 低于0.30：较差或误导性

联系方式

imageeval2026@gmail.com

pages.title: evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation

Primary metric: Spearman correlation between predicted and gold CRAI_composite scores. Higher is better.

Secondary metric: MAE on CRAI_composite. Lower is better. Used as tiebreaker.

Per-dimension scores (CEA, CC, CS, CI, HP) are reported on the leaderboard for diagnostic purposes but do not affect ranking.

Organizer Baselines

SystemSpearmanMAE
Mean baselineN/A0.3450
GPT-4 via OpenRouter0.62500.2248

Submission Format

⚠️ Important: Submit a zip file only containing predictions.tsv with these tab-separated columns:

id    CRAI_CEA    CRAI_CC    CRAI_CS    CRAI_CI    CRAI_HP    CRAI_composite

Rules:

  • All scores must be floats in [0.0, 1.0]
  • Header row is required
  • All instances must be present
  • CRAI_composite must equal 0.30×CEA + 0.20×CC + 0.20×CS + 0.20×CI − 0.10×HP
pages.content_zh:
评估

主要指标：预测和黄金标准 CRAI_composite 分数之间的斯皮尔曼相关系数。越高越好。

次要指标：CRAI_composite 的平均绝对误差 (MAE)。越低越好。用作平局打破器。

各维度分数（CEA、CC、CS、CI、HP）在排行榜上报告，用于诊断目的，但不影响排名。

组织者基准

系统斯皮尔曼平均绝对误差

GPT-4（通过 OpenRouter）0.62500.2248

提交格式

id    CRAI_CEA    CRAI_CC    CRAI_CS    CRAI_CI    CRAI_HP    CRAI_composite

规则：

  • 所有分数必须是 [0.0, 1.0] 范围内的浮点数

# How to participate

ArGuard 2026 — Task 1 / Track A · **Subtask A2: Fine-grained category prediction (multi-label)**.

## Who can join
You can take part as an individual or as a team. A person can participate in multiple shared tasks within ArGuard 2026 — see the full list at the [task website](https://araieval.gitlab.io/ArGuard2026/).

pages.title: Dataset
pages.content:
# Dataset

ArGuard Task 1 — Track A is built around an Arabic multimodal meme dataset: each instance is an image with overlaid Arabic text (OCR-extracted). Memes are manually annotated with both a binary label and one or more **fine-grained** sub-types.

For **Subtask A2**, each meme is tagged with zero or more labels from a **unified 10-class active vocabulary**:

- Hateful sub-types (7 active): `Contempt`, `Dehumanization`, `Exclusion`, `Incitement`, `Inferiority`, `Mocking`, `Slurs`
- Non-hateful sub-types (2): `Humor`, `Sarcasm`
- Shared (1): `Other`

The full annotation taxonomy also includes 5 zero-support hateful classes — `Extremism`, `Historical`, `Insults`, `Stereotyping`, `Threat` — which are accepted by the format checker but **not** scored (they have no positive support in the released data).

## Get the data
The official splits live on the Hugging Face Hub at [`QCRI/ArGuard-Task1`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/QCRI/ArGuard-Task1). Download them with the helper script from the starter kit:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/araieval/ArGuard-2026-tasks.git
cd ArGuard-2026-tasks/task1
pip install -r requirements.txt
python data/download_data.py
```

## Splits

| Split        | Records | Labels   | Phase                    | Purpose                                    |
|--------------|--------:|----------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| `train`      |   3,500 | full     | development              | model training                             |
| `dev`        |     500 | full     | development              | hyperparameter selection, local evaluation |
| `dev_test`   |     500 | **none** | development (leaderboard)| submission target for the dev-phase leaderboard |
| `test`       |     500 | full     | final evaluation         | blind ranking (triple-annotated gold)      |

The `dev_test` split is released with labels stripped — that is the file you submit predictions for during the development phase.

## Record schema (after `download_data.py`)
```json
{
    "id": "f9a8…b1.jpg",
    "image_path": "img/f9a8…b1.jpg",
    "text": "OCR-extracted Arabic text…",
    "label": "Hateful" | "Not Hateful" | null,
    "fine_grained_label": ["Mocking", "Incitement"],
    "annotations": []
}
```

## Licence
The dataset is released under **CC BY-NC 4.0** (non-commercial research use only).

## Resources
- Starter kit: <https://github.com/araieval/ArGuard-2026-tasks>
- Task website: <https://araieval.gitlab.io/ArGuard2026/>

# 数据集

ArGuard Task 1 — Track A 基于阿拉伯语多模态表情包数据集构建：每个实例包含一张带有叠加阿拉伯文本的图像（通过OCR提取）。表情包使用二元标签和一个或多个**细粒度**子类型进行人工标注。

对于**子任务A2**，每个表情包从**统一的10类活跃词汇**中标记零个或多个标签：

- 仇恨子类型（7个活跃）：`轻蔑`、`非人化`、`排斥`、`煽动`、`贬低`、`嘲弄`、`辱骂`
- 非仇恨子类型（2个）：`幽默`、`讽刺`
- 共享（1个）：`其他`

完整注解分类法还包括5个零支持仇恨类别——`极端主义`、`历史性`、`侮辱`、`刻板印象`、`威胁`——这些类别被格式检查器接受，但**不计分**（在发布的数据中无正例支持）。

## 获取数据

```bash
git clone https://github.com/araieval/ArGuard-2026-tasks.git
cd ArGuard-2026-tasks/task1
pip install -r requirements.txt
python data/download_data.py
```

## 数据分割

| 分割          | 记录数 | 标签     | 阶段          | 目的                           |
|--------------|------:|----------|----------------|--------------------------------|
| `train`      | 3,500 | 完整     | 开发阶段      | 模型训练                       |
| `dev`        |   500 | 完整     | 开发阶段      | 超参数选择、本地评估           |
| `dev_test`   |   500 | **无**   | 开发阶段（排行榜）| 开发阶段排行榜的提交目标 |
| `test`       |   500 | 完整     | 最终评估      | 盲测排名（三重标注黄金标准） |

`dev_test`分割的标签已移除——这是您在开发阶段向排行榜提交预测的文件。

## 记录模式（`download_data.py`后）
```json
{
    "id": "f9a8…b1.jpg",
    "image_path": "img/f9a8…b1.jpg",
    "text": "OCR提取的阿拉伯文本…",
    "label": "仇恨" | "非仇恨" | null,
    "fine_grained_label": ["嘲弄", "煽动"],
    "annotations": []

pages.title: Dataset
pages.content:
# Dataset

ArGuard Task 1 — Track A is built around an Arabic multimodal meme dataset: each instance is an image with overlaid Arabic text (OCR-extracted). Memes are manually annotated for hatefulness.

For **Subtask A1**, every meme has a single binary label from {`Hateful`, `Not Hateful`}.

## Get the data
The official splits live on the Hugging Face Hub at [`QCRI/ArGuard-Task1`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/QCRI/ArGuard-Task1). Download them with the helper script from the starter kit:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/araieval/ArGuard-2026-tasks.git
cd ArGuard-2026-tasks/task1
pip install -r requirements.txt
python data/download_data.py
```

## Splits

| Split        | Records | Labels   | Phase                    | Purpose                                    |
|--------------|--------:|----------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| `train`      |   3,500 | full     | development              | model training                             |
| `dev`        |     500 | full     | development              | hyperparameter selection, local evaluation |
| `dev_test`   |     500 | **none** | development (leaderboard)| submission target for the dev-phase leaderboard |
| `test`       |     500 | full     | final evaluation         | blind ranking (triple-annotated gold)      |

The `dev_test` split is released with labels stripped — that is the file you submit predictions for during the development phase.

## Record schema (after `download_data.py`)
```json
{
    "id": "f9a8…b1.jpg",
    "image_path": "img/f9a8…b1.jpg",
    "text": "OCR-extracted Arabic text…",
    "label": "Hateful" | "Not Hateful" | null,
    "fine_grained_label": ["Mocking", "Incitement"],
    "annotations": []
}
```

## Licence
The dataset is released under **CC BY-NC 4.0** (non-commercial research use only).

## Resources
- Starter kit: <https://github.com/araieval/ArGuard-2026-tasks>
- Task website: <https://araieval.gitlab.io/ArGuard2026/>

# Dataset

All splits live on the Hugging Face Hub — **[QCRI/AynVQA-ArabicNLP26](https://huggingface.co/datasets/QCRI/AynVQA-ArabicNLP26)** — as config
`task1a_msa`. This competition scores **devtest** (development phase) and **test**
(final phase).

```python
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("QCRI/AynVQA-ArabicNLP26", "task1a_msa", split="devtest")
```

## Splits

| split | labels | items | phase | purpose |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `train`   | yes | 3000 | development | training / fine-tuning |
| `dev`     | yes | 500  | development | local validation |
| `devtest` | no  | 500  | development (leaderboard) | submission target, dev phase |
| `test`    | no  | 1000 | final evaluation | blind ranking (human-recorded audio) |

- **Language:** MSA.
- Media (images / audio) are referenced by **relative path** keyed on `id`.
- 🔊 Dev-phase audio is synthetically generated (voice cloning); the final **test** audio is human-recorded — expect a recording-condition shift.

CC BY-NC 4.0 — non-commercial research use only.

pages.title: overview
pages.content:
Welcome to the WSLP@EMNLP-2026 Shared Task: Sign Language Translation (SLT)

Pushing the Boundaries of Indian Sign Language Understanding through Machine Translation

Registration

To participate in this shared task, please visit the "Participate" tab and create an account on Codabench using a valid institutional or personal email address. Participation is open to both individuals and teams.

Once registered, navigate to your Settings tab and ensure all required details are correctly filled out. Please use a consistent and identifiable team name or individual name across all submissions.

Overview

Sign languages like Indian Sign Language (ISL) are rich, expressive, and visual languages that require sophisticated modeling for understanding and translation. The goal of this shared task is to develop systems capable of translating ISL video or pose-based input into coherent, grammatically correct English sentences.

To support this, we provide a large-scale dataset — iSign — which contains over 118,000 video-sentence pairs in Indian Sign Language. Participants are required to train models that accurately translate ISL inputs into fluent English output.

Phases

The competition will proceed in two distinct phases:

  • Phase 1: Training & Validation – Participants will use the provided training and validation datasets to develop and fine-tune their models.
  • Phase 2: Testing – A held-out test set will be released. Participants will submit predictions to evaluate model performance on unseen data.

Task Description

  • Input: ISL video or extracted pose sequence
  • Output: English sentence translation
  • Dataset: iSign
  • Evaluation Metrics: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, and chrF++

Submission Guidelines

Each submission must be a ZIP archive named submission.zip and should contain the following file:

  1. answer.csv – A CSV file with two columns:
    • Column 1: Unique ID (as provided in the test/validation data)(uid)
    • Column 2: English sentence predicted by your model (text)
    Important: Ensure the order and IDs and column name (uid, text) exactly match those in the reference files. Any mismatch may lead to errors in scoring or disqualification.

Sample submission files can be downloaded from this link.

To upload your submission, go to the "Submit / View Results" tab and upload your submission.zip file. Participants are allowed multiple submissions per day, subject to platform limits.

Results and Leaderboard

Evaluation results will be displayed on the "Results" tab. Teams will be ranked based on a combination of BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, and chrF++ scores. Top-performing systems will be highlighted and recognized at the WSLP 2025 Workshop.

Acknowledgements

This shared task is part of the Workshop on Sign Language Processing (WSLP 2026), co-located with EMNLP 2026, hosted at October 29th Budapest, Hungary.

We sincerely thank all participants, organizers, dataset contributors, and the broader research community for their continued support in advancing sign language technologies.

To stay updated and connect with other participants, join our Discord server

  • Shared Task
  • Workshop
  • Shared Task Webpage
pages.content_zh:
# 欢迎参加WSLP@EMNLP-2026共享任务：手语翻译（SLT）

#### 通过机器翻译推进印度手语理解的边界

## 注册

要参加此共享任务，请访问"参与"选项卡，并使用有效的机构或个人电子邮件地址在Codabench上创建帐户。
个人和团队均可参与。

注册后，导航至您的**设置**选项卡，确保所有必需的详细信息正确填写。
请在所有提交中使用一致且可识别的**团队名称或个人名称**。

## 概述

印度手语（ISL）等手语是丰富、富有表现力且视觉化的语言，需要复杂的建模来理解和翻译。
此共享任务的目标是开发能够将ISL视频或基于姿态的输入翻译成连贯、语法正确的英文句子的系统。

为支持这一目标，我们提供了一个大规模数据集——**iSign**——包含超过118,000个印度手语视频-句子对。
参与者需要训练模型，将ISL输入准确翻译成流利的英文输出。

## 阶段

竞赛将分为两个不同的阶段进行：

- **第1阶段：训练与验证** – 参与者将使用提供的训练和验证数据集来开发和微调模型。
- **第2阶段：测试** – 将发布一个保留的测试集。参与者将提交预测结果以评估模型在未见数据上的性能。

### 任务描述

- **输入：** ISL视频或提取的姿态序列
- **输出：** 英文句子翻译
- **数据集：** iSign
- **评估指标：** BLEU-4、ROUGE-L和chrF++

## 提交指南

每次提交必须是名为`submission.zip`的ZIP存档，应包含以下文件：

1. `answer.csv` – 一个包含两列的CSV文件：
   - **第1列：** 唯一ID（如测试/验证数据中所提供）(uid)
   - **第2列：** 您的模型预测的英文句子(text)

   **重要：** 确保顺序、ID和列名(uid, text)与参考文件中的完全匹配。任何不匹配可能导致评分错误或取消资格。

示例提交文件可从[此链接](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Exploration-Lab/WSLP-AACL-2025/blob/main/Shared_task_MT/sample_submission.csv)下载。

要上传您的提交，请转至"提交/查看结果"选项卡并上传您的`submission.zip`文件。
参与者每天可进行多次提交，但需遵守平台限制。

## 结果和排行榜

评估结果将显示在"结果"选项卡中。团队将根据BLEU-4、ROUGE-L和chrF++得分的组合进行排名。
表现最佳的系统将在WSLP 2025研讨会中突出展示和表彰。

## 致谢

此共享任务是**手语处理研讨会（WSLP 2026）**的一部分，与**EMNLP 2026**共同举办，地点为**2026年10月29日，匈牙利布达佩斯**。

我们衷心感谢所有参与者、组织者和数据集

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
Welcome to the WSLP@EMNLP 2026 Shared Task: Isolated Sign Language Recognition (ISLR)

Advancing Indian Sign Language Understanding through Isolated Sign Recognition

Registration

To participate in this shared task, please navigate to the "Participate" tab and create a Codabench account using a valid institutional email address or personal email id.

Please ensure that your team name/user name is clearly identifiable and used consistently throughout your submissions.

Overview

Sign languages, such as Indian Sign Language (ISL), are rich and complex visual languages. This shared task invites participants to tackle the challenge of recognizing isolated ISL signs (words or glosses) from short video clips. The goal is to build systems that can accurately identify individual signs, which is crucial for applications like dictionary building, lookup tools, and annotation.

Participants are required to build models that can classify an input video clip to its corresponding word label.

Phases

This competition consists of two distinct phases:

     
  • Phase 1: Training & Validation – Participants will develop and validate their models using a training set and a corresponding validation set.
    •  
  • Phase 2: Testing – A held-out test set will be released. Participants will submit predictions to evaluate their models' generalization capabilities.

Task Details:

     
  • Input: ISL video clip or pose sequence
    •  
  • Output: Word label (gloss)
    •  
  • Metrics: Top-1, Top-5, Top-10 Accuracy

Submission Guidelines

Each submission must be a ZIP archive containing the following file:

     
  1. answer.csv – A comma-separated file with columns:    
           
    • Column 1: uid (as provided in the validation/test files, representing the unique video identifier)
    • Column 2: pred1 (the predicted word label/gloss for the corresponding uid)
    • Column 3: pred2 (the predicted word label/gloss for the corresponding uid)
    • Column 4: pred3 (the predicted word label/gloss for the corresponding uid)
    • Column 5: pred4 (the predicted word label/gloss for the corresponding uid)
    • ....
    • ....
    • ....
    • Column 11: pred10 (the predicted word label/gloss for the corresponding uid)
      •    
        Note: Ensure that the uid and their order exactly match those in the original reference file. Mismatches may result in incorrect scoring or disqualification. For Top-K accuracy beyond Top-1, your submission file would need to include multiple predictions per uid.  

For reference, sample submission files is provided. "Sample submission file"

To submit your results, go to the "Submit Results" tab and upload your submission.zip file. You may make multiple submissions per day during the competition phases, subject to limits.

Results and Leaderboard

Results will be displayed on the "Results" tab. Teams will be ranked primarily based on Accuracy, with Top-K Accuracy (where K = 1, 5, 10) as a secondary metric. The top-performing teams will be highlighted and recognized at the WSLP 2025 event.

Acknowledgements

This shared task is part of the Workshop on Sign Language Processing (WSLP 2025), co-located with EMNLP 2026 at Budapest, Hungary. We thank all participants, contributors, and the broader research community for supporting this initiative.

To stay updated and connect with other participants, join our Discord server

  • Shared Task Webpage

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation Criteria

Your submissions will be evaluated based on Top-1 Accuracy, Top-5 Accuracy, and Top-10 Accuracy.

  • Top-1 Accuracy: Measures the percentage of test samples where the correct word label is the highest-ranked prediction.
  • Top-5 Accuracy: Measures the percentage of test samples where the correct word label appears within the top 5 ranked predictions.
  • Top-10 Accuracy: Measures the percentage of test samples where the correct word label appears within the top 10 ranked predictions.

These metrics capture both strict recognition performance (Top-1) and more flexible settings (Top-5, Top-10) where the system can return multiple likely candidates.
pages.content_zh:
评估标准

您的提交将基于Top-1 准确率、Top-5 准确率和Top-10 准确率进行评估。

  • Top-1 准确率：衡量正确词标签是排名最高预测的测试样本百分比。
  • Top-5 准确率：衡量正确词标签出现在前5个排名预测中的测试样本百分比。
  • Top-10 准确率：衡量正确词标签出现在前10个排名预测中的测试样本百分比。

这些指标既能捕捉严格的识别性能（Top-1），也能评估更灵活的设置（Top-5、Top-10），其中系统可以返回多个可能的候选项。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
Welcome to the WSLP@EMNLP-2026 Shared Task: Word\Sign Presence Prediction

Advancing Indian Sign Language Understanding through Sign Spotting

Registration

To participate in this shared task, please visit the "Participate" tab and create a Codabench account using a valid institutional or personal email address. Participation is open to both individuals and teams.

After registration, navigate to your Settings and fill in all the required details.

Please ensure that your team name (or individual name) is clearly identifiable and used consistently across all submissions.

Overview

Indian Sign Language (ISL) is a rich and expressive visual language. In this shared task, participants are challenged to predict whether a specific word (gloss) is present within a given ISL sentence video — a task commonly known as sign spotting.

This task is crucial for real-world applications such as query-based sign language video retrieval and semantic search. It represents a step forward in building models that understand continuous signing in a structured and meaningful way.

We provide a dedicated dataset — the Word\Sign Presence Dataset — containing 1,543 (video, word) query pairs. Your goal is to build a model that can accurately predict whether a queried word is signed in a given ISL sentence video.

Phases

The competition consists of two distinct phases:

  • Phase 1: Training & Validation – Participants will train and validate their models using the provided datasets.
  • Phase 2: Testing – A held-out test set will be released. Participants will submit predictions to evaluate the generalization of their models.

Task Details

  • Input: ISL sentence video or corresponding pose sequence, and a query word
  • Output: Binary prediction indicating the presence of the word (1 = Present, 0 = Not Present)
  • Dataset: Word Presence Dataset
  • Evaluation Metrics: Accuracy, Macro Precision, Macro Recall, Macro F1-Score

Submission Guidelines

Each submission must be a ZIP archive named submission.zip, containing the following file:

  1. answer.csv – A comma-separated file with the following three columns:
    • Column 1: sentence_id – ID of the input ISL sentence video
    • Column 2: query_id – ID of the queried word
    • Column 3: is_present – Your model’s binary prediction (1 for Present, 0 for Not Present)
    Note: Ensure that all (sentence_id, query_id) pairs appear in the exact same order as in the reference file. Mismatches may lead to invalid scoring or disqualification. Make sure columns name in the answer.csv files are (sentence_is, query_id, is_present).

Sample submission files is made available along with the dataset to guide your formatting. Sample Submission file

To submit your predictions, visit the "Submission" tab and upload your submission.zip file. Participants may make multiple submissions per day, subject to platform-imposed limits.

Results and Leaderboard

Leaderboard results will be displayed under the "Results" tab. Final rankings will be based primarily on the F1-Score for the positive class (i.e., correct prediction of presence), with Accuracy, Precision, and Recall (all macro-averaged) serving as secondary metrics.

Top-performing teams will be recognized and invited to present their approaches at the WSLP@EMNLP-2026 event.

Acknowledgements

This shared task is part of the Workshop on Sign Language Processing (WSLP@EMNLP-2026), co-located with EMNLP 2026 at Budapest, Hungary.

We sincerely thank all participants, organizers, collaborators, and the broader research community for their continued efforts in advancing the field of sign language technology.

To stay updated and connect with other participants, join our Discord server

  • Discord : Shared Task
  • Discord : Workshop
  • Shared Task Webpage
pages.content_zh: # 欢迎来到WSLP@EMNLP-2026共享任务：词/手语存在预测 ## 通过手语识别推进印度手语理解 ## 注册 要参加此共享任务，请访问"参与"选项卡，并使用有效的机构或个人电子邮件地址创建Codabench账户。 个人和团队都可以参加。 注册后，导航到您的**设置**并填入所有必需信息。 请确保您的**团队名称**（或个人名称）清晰可辨，并在所有提交中保持一致。 ## 概述 印度手语（ISL）是一种丰富而富有表现力的视觉语言。在此共享任务中，参与者需要预测特定词汇（标记）是否出现在给定的ISL句子视频中——这个任务通常被称为**手语识别**。 此任务对于实际应用至关重要，例如基于查询的手语视频检索和语义搜索。这代表了在构建以结构化和有意义的方式理解连续手语的模型方面的进步。 我们提供了一个专用数据集——**词/手语存在数据集**——包含1,543个（视频、词汇）查询对。您的目标是构建一个模型，能够准确预测查询的词汇是否在给定的ISL句子视频中被手语表达。 ## 阶段 竞赛包括两个不同的阶段： - **阶段1：训练与验证** – 参与者将使用提供的数据集训练和验证其模型。 - **阶段2：测试** – 将发布保留的测试集。参与者将提交预测以评估其模型的泛化能力。 ## 任务详情 - **输入：** ISL句子视频或对应的姿态序列，以及一个查询词汇 - **输出：** 表示词汇存在的二元预测（1 = 存在，0 = 不存在） - **数据集：** 词汇存在数据集 - **评估指标：** 准确率、宏平均精准率、宏平均召回率、宏平均F1分数 ## 提交指南 每次提交必须是名为`submission.zip`的ZIP压缩包，包含以下文件： 1. `answer.csv` – 逗号分隔的文件，包含以下三列： - **第1列：** `sentence_id` – 输入ISL句子视频的ID - **第2列：** `query_id` – 查询词汇的ID - **第3列：** `is_present` – 您模型的二元预测（`1`表示存在，`0`表示不存在） **注意：** 确保所有`(sentence_id, query_id)`对与参考文件的顺序完全相同。不匹配可能导致无效计分或被取消资格。请确保answer.csv文件中的列名为(sentence_id, query_id, is_present)。 样本提交文件已随数据集提供，用以指导您的格式设置。样本提交文件 要提交您的预测，请访问"提交"选项卡并上传您的`submission.zip`文件。参与者每天可进行多次提交，需遵守平台限制。 ## 结果和排行榜 排行榜结果将显示在排行榜选项卡下。

# 超声生物测量基础模型 (FU_Biometry) - 基本信息

所有时间节点均为2026年，最终结果公布时间以MICCAI 2026官方截止日期为准。

准确可靠的超声测量对于产前、儿科和成人临床诊断和决策至关重要。目前的手动和半自动方法耗时长、依赖操作者，且观察者间和观察者内变异性高。自动化和通用系统可将测量时间减少50%-80%，提高临床工作流效率。

pages.title: Docker Submission Guide
pages.content:
# FU Biometry Final Test — Participant Docker Submission Guide

> **GPU**：NVIDIA RTX 3080 10GB | **CUDA Runtime**：12.1 | **Inference Timeout**：6 hours | **Network**：Container is fully offline

---

## Quick Start (3 Steps)

```bash
# 1. Prepare local submission folder and package it
mkdir -p submission
echo '{"image": "your-dockerhub-username/image-name:v1.0"}' > submission/submission.json

# You MUST zip the submission folder itself
zip -r submission.zip submission/

# 2. Build and push the image
docker build -t your-dockerhub-username/image-name:v1.0 .
docker push your-dockerhub-username/image-name:v1.0

# 3. Upload submission.zip on Codabench
```

---

## 1. Submission Format

You MUST create a `submission/` folder, place `submission.json` inside it, then zip the folder itself.

Local structure before packaging:

```text
submission/
└── submission.json
```

The uploaded `submission.zip` must preserve this directory:

```
submission.zip
└── submission/
    └── submission.json   ← { "image": "dockerhub-username/image-name:tag" }
```

> Note: Do NOT zip only the files inside `submission/`. The ZIP must contain `submission/submission.json`; otherwise Codabench cannot locate the descriptor file according to this competition's submission structure.

Verify before uploading:

```bash
unzip -l submission.zip
```

Correct output should include:

```text
submission/
submission/submission.json
```

```json
{
  "image": "lijiake/fu-biometry:v2.1"
}
```

> **Strongly recommended: use a public image with an immutable new tag (e.g. `v1.0.1`). Do not repeatedly overwrite `latest`.**  
> If you must use a private repository, please contact the organizers first to confirm that the evaluation server has logged into a Docker Hub account with pull access, then follow these steps:
>
> 1. Log in to [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com)
> 2. Go to your repository → **Settings** → **Collaborators**
> 3. Add the following account with **Read & Write** permission:
>
>    ```
>    lijiake
>    ```
>
> 4. Click **Add** to complete authorization
>
> **Do NOT send Docker Hub passwords or access tokens.**
>
> After authorization, you may push new tags or digests to the same private repository within the allowed submission quota and resubmit the corresponding image reference on Codabench. As long as the organizer's account retains read/pull access to your repository, no further permission changes are needed.

---

## 2. Code Specification (Core)

### 2.1 File Structure

Organize your code under the Docker build directory:

```
your-project/
├── Dockerfile              ← Image definition
├── requirements.txt        ← Python dependencies
├── predict.py              ← Container entry script (provided by organizers, **DO NOT MODIFY**)
├── model.py                ← ⭐ Model inference code, must include class Model
├── model_factory.py        ← Network architecture (can be split or merged into model.py)
├── best_model.pth          ← Model weights (must be inside the image!)
└── ...                     ← Other files
```

### 2.2 Mandatory Rules

| # | Rule | Description |
|---|------|-------------|
| 1 | **predict.py is the entry script; DO NOT MODIFY** | Organizer-provided container entry; responsible for data preparation and calling model.py (**this is a script file, NOT the method inside model**). |
| 2 | **model.py MUST contain class Model** | model.py must also implement the `predict()` **method** (inference logic). |
| 3 | **All weights packaged inside the image** | The container is fully offline; no runtime downloads of any files. |
| 4 | **ENTRYPOINT is fixed** | `ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "/app/predict.py"]` |
| 5 | **Output file is fixed** | `/output/regression_predictions.json` |
| 6 | **Image is linux/amd64** | Mac M series requires `docker build --platform linux/amd64` |

> 📌 **Summary**: `predict.py` (the script) handles environment setup → calls `model.Model.predict()` (the method) to run inference. Both are named `predict`, but they reside in different files and serve different roles.

### 2.3 model.py Inference Method

`model.py` **internal implementation is completely free** (PyTorch / ONNX / TensorRT all accepted), but it MUST contain the `Model` class with a `predict()` **method**:

```python
class Model:
    def __init__(self):
        """
        Initialization phase: load model weights.
        Called once automatically after container starts.
        """
        pass

    def predict(self, data_root: str, output_dir: str, batch_size: int = 8):
        """
        Args:
            data_root  : data root directory (see structure below)
            output_dir : output directory = /output; must write predictions.json here
            batch_size : inference batch size (entry script passes 8; adjust in implementation based on VRAM)
        """
        pass
```

### 2.4 Data Layout

Once the platform launches your image, `predict.py` automatically prepares the following structure and passes it as `data_root`:

```
{data_root}/
├── images/
│   ├── A4C/                   → symlink to /input/A4C_test
│   ├── AOP/                   → symlink to /input/AOP_test
│   ├── ...(9 task directories in total)
│   └── fetal_femur/           → symlink to /input/fetal_femur_test
├── csv/
│   └── test_metadata.csv      ← Test set metadata
└── best_model.pth             ← Weight file you packaged into the image
```

**`test_metadata.csv` format**：

```csv
image_path,task_name,task_id,num_classes,height,width
A4C/0021.png,Regression,A4C,16,600,800
FA/0189.png,Regression,FA,4,768,1024
...
```

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `image_path` | Relative image path, e.g. `A4C/0021.png`; read by joining to `{data_root}/images/` |
| `task_id` | A4C / AOP / FA / FUGC / HC / IVC / PLAX / PSAX / fetal_femur |
| `num_classes` | Number of landmarks for this task |
| `height` / `width` | Image dimensions |

### 2.5 Entry Script predict.py (provided by organizers; DO NOT MODIFY)

> ⚠️ **This is the Docker entry script, NOT the predict() method inside model.py.** `predict.py` prepares the data directory and calls your `model.Model.predict()` method.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Docker entry — provided by organizers, DO NOT MODIFY."""

import os
import shutil
import sys

INPUT_DIR  = os.environ["GU_INPUT_DIR"]
OUTPUT_DIR = os.environ["GU_OUTPUT_DIR"]
WORK_DIR   = "/work"
os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

def prepare_images():
    """Map platform directories (e.g. A4C_test) to metadata paths (e.g. A4C)."""
    images_dir = os.path.join(WORK_DIR, "images")
    os.makedirs(images_dir, exist_ok=True)

    for name in os.listdir(INPUT_DIR):
        source = os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, name)
        if not os.path.isdir(source):
            continue
        task_name = name[:-5] if name.endswith("_test") else name
        target = os.path.join(images_dir, task_name)
        if not os.path.lexists(target):
            os.symlink(source, target)

os.makedirs(os.path.join(WORK_DIR, "csv"), exist_ok=True)
prepare_images()

shutil.copy2(
    os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "test_metadata.csv"),
    os.path.join(WORK_DIR, "csv", "test_metadata.csv"),
)

# Copy weights from /app/ to working directory
shutil.copy2("/app/best_model.pth", os.path.join(WORK_DIR, "best_model.pth"))
os.chdir(WORK_DIR)

# Import your Model
sys.path.insert(0, "/app")
from model import Model

model = Model()
model.predict(data_root=WORK_DIR, output_dir=OUTPUT_DIR, batch_size=8)

print("Done!", flush=True)
```

> ⚠️ **Critical constraint**: The container is fully offline (`--network none`). All model weights and pretrained parameters must be COPY'd into the image at build time.

---

## 3. Output Format

`Model.predict()` MUST generate **a single file** `regression_predictions.json` inside `output_dir`:

```json
[
  {
    "image_path": "A4C/0021.png",
    "task_id": "A4C",
    "predicted_points_pixels": [411.0, 235.0, 345.0, 372.0, ...]
  },
  {
    "image_path": "FA/0189.png",
    "task_id": "FA",
    "predicted_points_pixels": [506.0, 154.0, 506.0, 552.0, 716.0, 353.0, 296.0, 353.0]
  }
]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `image_path` | string | Exactly as it appears in `test_metadata.csv` |
| `task_id` | string | One of the 9 tasks |
| `predicted_points_pixels` | float[] | Flat coordinates `[x1,y1,x2,y2,...]`, length = num_classes × 2 |

Code example:

```python
import json, os

def save_predictions(predictions, output_dir):
    path = os.path.join(output_dir, "regression_predictions.json")
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(predictions, f)
    print(f"Saved {len(predictions)} predictions to {path}")

# Call at the end of the predict() method
# save_predictions(all_predictions, output_dir)
```

---

## 4. Dockerfile Template

```dockerfile
FROM pytorch/pytorch:2.3.1-cuda12.1-cudnn8-runtime

WORKDIR /app

# System dependencies (required by OpenCV / albumentations etc.)
RUN apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends \
    libgl1-mesa-glx libglib2.0-0 libsm6 libxrender1 libxext6 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Python dependencies
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Pretrained weights (if any) — MUST be downloaded and COPY'd into the image beforehand!
COPY dinov2_vit_small.pth /app/dinov2_vit_small.pth

# Model code + weights
COPY model.py model_factory.py utils.py predict.py /app/
COPY best_model.pth /app/best_model.pth

ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "/app/predict.py"]
```

---

## 5. Local Self-Check (Mandatory Before Submission)

Use the following commands to simulate the platform runtime environment:

```bash
# Prepare test set (simulate with validation set)
mkdir -p /tmp/test_local /tmp/test_output
cp -r /path/to/validation_data/* /tmp/test_local/
cp /path/to/test_metadata.csv /tmp/test_local/

# Run the image
docker run --rm --gpus all \
  --network none \
  --memory 7g --cpus 4 --shm-size 2g \
  -v /tmp/test_local:/input:ro \
  -v /tmp/test_output:/output:rw \
  -e GU_INPUT_DIR=/input \
  -e GU_OUTPUT_DIR=/output \
  your-image-name:v1.0

# Check output
cat /tmp/test_output/regression_predictions.json | python3 -c "
import json, sys
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
print(f'{len(data)} predictions')
print(f'Tasks: {set(p[\"task_id\"] for p in data)}')
"
```

---

## 6. Checklist (Verify Item by Item Before Submission)

- [ ] ZIP retains the `submission/` directory; descriptor path is `submission/submission.json`
- [ ] `submission.json` format is correct `{"image": "xxx/yyy:tag"}`, image is pushed to Docker Hub and set to **Public**
- [ ] Project directory includes `predict.py` (organizer-provided entry script; no modifications made)
- [ ] `model.py` contains `class Model` with a `predict()` **method** (inference logic) implemented
- [ ] `predict()` outputs to `/output/regression_predictions.json` with exactly correct field names and format
- [ ] All model weights and pretrained parameters have been COPY'd into the image (runtime is **fully offline**)
- [ ] Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT is `["python3", "/app/predict.py"]`
- [ ] Local test with `--network none` passes, exit code is 0
- [ ] Image is `linux/amd64` (Mac M series: `docker build --platform linux/amd64`)

---

## 7. Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| `Cannot find submission.json` | ZIP doesn't preserve the required `submission/` directory, or filename is incorrect | Use `zip -r submission.zip submission/`; verify with `unzip -l submission.zip` that `submission/submission.json` exists |
| `FileNotFoundError: /input/...` | Hardcoded paths | Use `os.environ["GU_INPUT_DIR"]` instead of hardcoding `/input` |
| Image too large to pull | Base image too heavy | Use `-runtime` (not `-devel`), clean apt cache |
| Model downloaded at runtime | Code uses `pretrained=True` | Change to `pretrained=False`, COPY weights into the image |
| `--network none` test fails | Code accesses HuggingFace etc. | Download all resources at build time |
| `CUDA out of memory` | Batch size, model ensemble count, or input dimensions too large | Total GPU VRAM is 10 GB; entry passes 8, reduce actual batch inside `Model.predict()` if needed |
| Exit code non-zero but no error message | ENTRYPOINT not set correctly | Run locally first, then add --network none to verify |

---

## 8. Hardware & Constraints

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| GPU | NVIDIA RTX 3080 (10 GB VRAM) |
| CUDA | 12.1 |
| GPU VRAM | 10 GB |
| Container memory limit | 7 GB |
| CPU cores | 4 |
| Shared memory | 2 GB (--shm-size 2g) |
| Runtime limit | 6 hours |
| Network | **Fully offline** (`--network none` + `--cap-drop ALL`) |
| Filesystem | `/input` read-only, `/output` writable |

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# Foundation Model for Ultrasound Biometry (FU_Biometry) - Basic Information

All time nodes are for 2026, with the final result announcement subject to MICCAI 2026 official deadlines.

Accurate and reliable ultrasound measurement is essential for clinical diagnosis and decision-making in prenatal, pediatric, and adult care. Current manual and semi-automated methods are time-consuming, operator-dependent, and suffer from high inter- and intra-observer variability. Automated and generalizable systems can reduce measurement time by 50%–80% and improve clinical workflow efficiency.

Despite advances from previous challenges (PSFHS 2023, IUGC 2024/2025, FUGC 2025, FM_UIA 2026), task-specific deep learning models lack robustness and generalization across diverse scanners, protocols, anatomies, and clinical settings.
This challenge establishes a large-scale unified benchmark for ultrasound biometry, covering prenatal, intrapartum, and adult cardiac ultrasound with over 20 clinical parameters. It promotes generalizable, multi-task, cross-domain models with improved efficiency, measurement consistency, and real-world clinical utility.

# Challenge Objectives
To develop automated, generalizable ultrasound biometry methods robust to devices, centers, and populations, with clinically validated end-to-end evaluation.

# Aim of the Challenge
1.Provide a large multi-center, multi-device dataset with expert annotations for training and validation.

2.Evaluate anatomical landmark detection and over 20 clinical biometric measurements.

3.Assess key clinical biomarkers derived from automated measurements.

4.Foster collaboration between AI researchers and clinical imaging experts.

5.Advance reliable fully automatic ultrasound quantification using landmark error and clinical measurement error.

# Resources
Participants can get the baseline the following channel：

https://github.com/lijiake2408/Foundation-Model-for-Ultrasound-Biometry

Training set: Released with full annotations for model development.
Validation set: Raw images distributed to participants. Upload your predictions in submission.zip to the platform for scoring.
Test set: Hosted by the organizers. Your Docker image will be run on this data during the final phase.

pages.content_zh:
# FU_Biometry Challenge - 评估方法

## 1. 评估目标（无优先级顺序）
- 在以下属性中优化算法性能：
  - 准确性
  - 复杂性
  - 硬件需求
  - 运行时间
  - 鲁棒性
  - 灵敏度
  - 特异性

## 2. 核心评估指标
两个指标具有**相等的50%权重**，均用于最终排名：

### 2.1 平均径向误差（MRE）
- **目的**：测量地标定位准确性。
- **计算**：对于具有K个所需地标的情况（预测值{p_k}，参考值{g_k}）：
  \[MRE =(1 / K) \sum_{k=1}^{K}|| p_k-g_k||_2\]
- **单位**：像素；如果有像素间距可用，转换为毫米（mm）。
- **注意**：仅针对每张图像的适用地标子集计算。

### 2.2 超声参数预测差异
- **目的**：测量临床衍生参数的准确性。
- **计算**：平均绝对误差（MAE）|ŷ_j − y_j|（ŷ_j = 预测参数，y_j = 手动测量），以原始物理单位（mm/度）表示。
- **归一化**：使用临床定义的容差范围或四分位数间距（IQR）对每个参数进行归一化，以防止大范围参数主导评估。
- **报告**：为透明起见，发布原始误差和归一化误差。

## 3. 排名计算方法

### 3.1 分数汇总
- 最终分数 = **50%归一化MRE + 50%归一化参数误差**（等权重以平衡几何精度和临床测量可靠性）。

### 3.2 排名框架（ChallengeR风格的排名后聚合）
1. 在4个预定义数据域中进行域平衡加权（避免单一采集源的主导地位）。
2. 双排行榜：**整体排名** + **域分层排名**（为了透明性）。
3. 平局破除规则：测量准确性更高（归一化参数误差更低）优先（临床相关性更高）。

### 3.3 缺失结果处理
- 缺少测试用例结果的提交通过为相应指标分配所有有效提交中的**最差性能分数**而受到处罚。

## 4. 统计分析

### 4.1 软件工具
- R语言；Python库（SciPy、Pandas）（在科学研究中被广泛接受）。

### 4.2 缺失数据处理
- 不进行多重填补；缺失输出受到处罚（最终结果无缺失值）。
- 报告所有指标的自助法95%置信区间（CI），采用1,000次重新取样。

### 4.3 性能精度评估
- **百分位自助法95%置信区间（1,000次重新取样）**用于测试集上的所有算法性能估计。

### 4.4 性能变异性评估
- 跨测试用例：通过标准差（SD）、四分位数间距（IQR）、箱线图/小提琴图和显式异常值报告，报告逐案例指标分布。
- 排名变异性：使用**自助法**评估（非参数，假设最少）。

### 4.5 统计显著性检验
- **配对Wilcoxon符号秩检验**用于算法性能的成对比较（非参数，适应非正态指标分布）。
- 多重比较修正（Holm或Benjamini-Hochberg）以避免假阳性。
- 效应量（例如Cliff's delta）与p值一起报告，用于临床解释。
- 域/设备分层分析以背景化跨域泛化。

### 4.6 数据假设验证
- 所有统计方法的预验证测试：
  1. Shapiro-Wilk检验：评估数据正态性。
  2. Levene检验：评估方差齐性。

## 5. 进一步分析
1. 由排名前列团队算法构建的**集成模型**的性能验证。
2. 算法间变异性、提交方法的常见偏差/问题分析。
3. 不同数据域/设备间排名变异性的深入分析。

# FU_Biometry Challenge - 参赛规则

## 1. 挑战赛生命周期
- 重复举办的赛事，具有固定的年度学术会议投稿截止日期

## 2. 参赛政策
### 2.1 算法开发
- 参赛者必须使用所有未标注数据开发半监督学习方法。
- 仅允许使用公开可用的外部数据集和预训练模型进行训练；禁止对公开数据进行额外的私有标注。

### 2.2 组织机构参赛者
- 可以参加挑战赛，但**不具备获奖资格**且**不在排行榜中列示**。

## 3. 投稿规则
### 3.1 投稿方式
- 测试阶段：每支队伍仅可提交**一个成功的Docker容器**（防止在隐藏测试集上反复调优）。
- 严格区分公开验证排行榜与私密最终测试评估；最终排名仅基于未见数据集。
- 排名靠前的投稿需接受人工审核验证（Docker可执行性、方法描述、规则合规性）。

### 3.2 验证阶段投稿
- 队伍在验证阶段总共可投稿**最多10次**，每天不超过**2次**。
- 验证阶段得分仅用于基本检查（完整性和格式），不用于排名或对比评估。

## 4. 奖励政策
1. 为排名靠前的队伍、最具创新方法的队伍以及方法描述最严谨的队伍颁发证书和现金奖励。
2. **排名前10的队伍**受邀在MICCAI 2026做口头报告，并鼓励向IEEE生物医学工程汇刊（TBME）特刊投稿扩展论文。
3. 作为挑战赛汇编论文的共同作者，该论文将投稿至顶级期刊（MedIA/TMI）。

## 5. 结果公布
- 组织方公布**表现最佳的前10种方法**。
- 公布内容包括队伍名称及基于官方评估指标的总体排名。

## 6. 发表政策
### 6.1 作者资格
- 对研究构想、设计、实施或解释做出重要贡献的前10名队伍成员符合作者资格。

### 6.2 独立发表
- 参赛队伍可单独发表结果，并应尊重挑战赛的集体努力。

### 6.3 禁发期
- 组织方首先发表全面的挑战赛论文；建议各队伍在此期间避免独立发表完整研究成果。

## 7. 代码可用性要求
- 算法代码发布（通过GitHub仓库）和相应的学术会议论文投稿是**获奖资格的先决条件**以及进一步数据使用的必要条件。

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# FU_Biometry Challenge - Evaluation Methods

## 1. Assessment Aims (No Priority Order)
- Optimize algorithm performance in the following properties:
  - Accuracy
  - Complexity
  - Hardware requirements
  - Runtime
  - Robustness
  - Sensitivity
  - Specificity

## 2. Core Evaluation Metrics
Two metrics with **equal 50% weighting**, both used for final ranking:
### 2.1 Mean Radial Error (MRE)
- **Purpose**: Measure landmark localization accuracy.
- **Calculation**: For a case with K required landmarks (predictions {p_k}, references {g_k}):
  \[MRE =(1 / K) \sum_{k=1}^{K}|| p_k-g_k||_2\]
- **Unit**: Pixels; converted to millimeters (mm) if pixel spacing is available.
- **Note**: Only computed for the applicable subset of landmarks for each image.

### 2.2 Ultrasound Parameter Prediction Difference
- **Purpose**: Measure the accuracy of clinically derived parameters.
- **Calculation**: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) |ŷ_j − y_j| (ŷ_j = predicted parameter, y_j = manual measurement) in native physical units (mm/degrees).
- **Normalization**: Each parameter is normalized using clinically defined tolerance ranges or interquartile range (IQR) to prevent large-range parameters from dominating evaluation.
- **Reporting**: Both raw and normalized errors are published for transparency.

## 3. Ranking Calculation Method
### 3.1 Score Aggregation
- Final score = **50% normalized MRE + 50% normalized parameter error** (equal weighting to balance geometric accuracy and clinical measurement reliability).

### 3.2 Ranking Framework (ChallengeR-style rank-then-aggregate)
1. Domain-balanced weighting across 4 predefined data domains (avoid dominance of a single acquisition source).
2. Dual leaderboards: **overall ranking** + **domain-stratified ranking** (for transparency).
3. Tie-breaking rule: Superior measurement accuracy (lower normalized parameter error) takes priority (higher clinical relevance).

### 3.3 Missing Result Handling
- Submissions with missing test case results are penalized by assigning the **worst performance score** for the corresponding metric among all valid submissions.

## 4. Statistical Analyses
### 4.1 Software Tools
- R language; Python libraries (SciPy, Pandas) (widely accepted in scientific research).

### 4.2 Missing Data Handling
- No multiple imputation; missing outputs are penalized (final results have no missing values).
- Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) with 1,000 resamples are reported for all metrics.

### 4.3 Performance Precision Assessment
- **Percentile bootstrap 95% CIs (1,000 resamples)** on the test set for all algorithm performance estimates.

### 4.4 Performance Variability Assessment
- Across test cases: Per-case metric distributions reported via standard deviation (SD), interquartile range (IQR), boxplots/violin plots, and explicit outlier reporting.
- Ranking variability: Assessed using the **bootstrap method** (nonparametric, minimal assumptions).

### 4.5 Statistical Significance Test
- **Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test** for pairwise algorithm performance comparisons (nonparametric, adapted for non-normal metric distributions).
- Multiple-comparison correction (Holm or Benjamini–Hochberg) to avoid false positives.
- Effect sizes (e.g., Cliff’s delta) reported alongside p-values for clinical interpretability.
- Domain/device-stratified analyses to contextualize cross-domain generalization.

### 4.6 Data Assumption Validation
- Pre-validation tests for all statistical methods:
  1. Shapiro-Wilk test: Assess data normality.
  2. Levene's test: Evaluate variance homogeneity.

## 5. Further Analyses
1. Performance verification of **ensemble models** built from the top-ranked teams’ algorithms.
2. Analysis of inter-algorithm variability, common biases/problems of submitted methods.
3. In-depth analysis of ranking variability across different data domains/devices.

pages.content:
# FU_Biometry Challenge - Participation Rules

## 1. Challenge Life Cycle
- Repeated event with annual fixed conference submission deadline

## 2. Participation Policies
### 2.1 Algorithm Development
- Participants must use all unlabeled data to develop semi-supervised methods.
- Only publicly available external datasets and pre-trained models are allowed for training; additional private annotations of public data are prohibited.

### 2.2 Organizer Institute Participants
- May participate in the challenge but are **not eligible for awards** and **not listed in the leaderboard**.

## 3. Submission Rules
### 3.1 Submission Method
- Testing phase: Only **one successful Docker container submission** per team (prevent repeated tuning on hidden test set).
- Strict separation between public validation leaderboard and private final test evaluation; final rankings based solely on unseen test set.
- Top-ranked submissions undergo manual verification (Docker executability, method descriptions, rule compliance).

### 3.2 Validation Phase Submission
- Teams may submit up to **10 times in total**, with no more than **2 submissions per day**.
- Validation scores serve only as sanity checks (completeness and format), not for ranking or comparative evaluation.

## 4. Award Policy
1. Certificates and cash awards for top teams, the most innovative method team, and teams with the most careful method description.
2. **Top 10 teams** are invited to give oral presentations at MICCAI 2026 and encouraged to submit extended manuscripts to the IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering (TBME) Special Issue.
3. Co-authorship of the challenge compendium paper to be submitted to top journals (MedIA/TMI).

## 5. Result Announcement
- The **top 10 performing methods** are publicly announced by organizers.
- Announcement includes team names and overall ranking based on official evaluation metrics.

## 6. Publication Policy
### 6.1 Authorship Qualification
- Members of top-10 teams who made significant contributions to research conceptualization, design, execution or interpretation qualify as authors.

### 6.2 Independent Publication
- Participating teams may publish results separately, with respect for the challenge’s collective efforts.

### 6.3 Embargo Period
- Organizers publish a comprehensive challenge paper first; individual teams are encouraged to refrain from publishing complete findings independently during this period.

## 7. Code Availability Requirement
- Algorithm code release (via GitHub repository) and corresponding conference paper submission are **prerequisites for award eligibility** and further data usage.

16048.title: UCF UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge — V2X-Real Track — ECCV Workshop 2026
16048.description: Synthesize LiDAR data targeting V2X-Real's infrastructure-centric distribution; train on synthetic, evaluate on real V2X-Real-IC.
16048.description_zh: 合成LiDAR数据，针对V2X-Real的基础设施中心分布；在合成数据上训练，在真实V2X-Real-IC上评估。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge — V2X-Real Track

Muhammad Shahbaz  ·  Shaurya Agarwal

A challenge track of the 6th DriveX Workshop @ ECCV 2026 — drivex-workshop.github.io/eccv2026.

Roadside LiDAR perception for intelligent transportation systems is bottlenecked by the cost and rarity of large, well-annotated real datasets. This challenge asks: can synthetic LiDAR data be made realistic enough that a deep learning model trained on it generalizes to real LiDAR frames?

Towards that, this challenge asks participants to generate their own synthetic LiDAR data targeting the V2X-Real distribution, train an object detector on that data, and submit detections on real held-out frames. We score on (1) how distributionally close their synthetic frames are to real ones, and (2) how well the sim-only detector performs on real frames.

Reference resources for participants

To support participants who would like a documented starting point, we make publicly available a complete reference pipeline covering synthesis methodology, empirical analysis, ready-to-use synthetic datasets, and an open-source LiDAR data processing and visualization software. These materials are offered as orientation, not as requirements.

The synthesis pipeline is described in UrbanTwin: Building High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Sim2Real LiDAR Perception and Evaluation (arXiv preprint), with a deeper empirical analysis including the distributional realism metrics adopted by this challenge in High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Bridging the Sim2Real Gap in LiDAR-Based ITS Perception (IEEE T-ITS, 2026).

The synthetic LiDAR datasets generated with that pipeline are released in UrbanTwin: Synthetic Roadside LiDAR Datasets (IEEE OJ-ITS, 2026) and are available for download at Harvard Dataverse. Each dataset contains 10K frames annotated across six object categories for detection, tracking, and segmentation tasks, and is directly compatible with the multi-class evaluation used here; empirical analysis in papers include both the distributional realism metrics and single-class 3D object detection study as proof-of-concept. For end-to-end LiDAR processing we also provide our LiGuard Framework (IEEE T-IV, 2026) with short, more software focused read on The Journal of Open Source Software.

What you will do

  1. Download the public real V2X-Real dataset and the released detection-test point clouds (50 real frames, no labels).
  2. Generate synthetic LiDAR frames using any approach you like — simulation (CARLA, LGSVL, custom), generative models (diffusion, GANs, flow-based), hybrid pipelines, or anything else.
  3. Train a 3D object detector (any architecture) on only your synthetic data.
  4. Submit:
    • 50 of your synthetic LiDAR frames,
    • your detector's predictions on the 50 released test point clouds,
    • and a signed honor declaration.

Scoring at a glance

Combined score = 0.6 × normalized 3D mAP + 0.4 × normalized realism, where 3D mAP is averaged across the 3 object categories defined for this track (vehicle, pedestrian, truck) and realism averages normalized Chamfer Distance, MMD, EMD, and Fréchet Point-cloud Distance. See the Evaluation tab for the formulae.

Phases

(line 49). New block:

Prizes

Per track:

  • 1st place: USD 500
  • 2nd place: USD 300
  • 3rd place: USD 200

Sponsor(s) will be announced before the Development phase opens.

Phases

  • Development — public leaderboard, up to 5 submissions/day per participant, 100 total. Use this to iterate.
  • Final — private leaderboard until close, 5 total submissions per participant. The final-phase ranking determines the winners.

Baselines

Reference numbers are listed in the Data tab.
pages.content_zh: # UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR挑战赛 — V2X-Real赛道 *6th DriveX Workshop @ ECCV 2026的挑战赛道 — drivex-workshop.github.io/eccv2026。* 路侧LiDAR感知在智能交通系统中的发展受到了大规模、高质量标注真实数据成本高昂且稀缺的限制。本挑战赛提出问题：合成LiDAR数据是否能够足够逼真，使得在其上训练的深度学习模型能够泛化到真实LiDAR帧？ 为此，本挑战赛要求参赛者生成自己的合成LiDAR数据以匹配**V2X-Real**分布，在该数据上训练目标检测器，并提交对真实保留测试集帧的检测结果。评分基于：(1)其合成帧与真实帧的分布接近程度，以及(2)仅在合成数据上训练的检测器在真实帧上的性能。 ## 参赛者参考资源 为支持需要有据可查的起点的参赛者，我们公开提供了一整套完整参考管道，涵盖合成方法论、实证分析、即用型合成数据集，以及开源LiDAR数据处理和可视化软件。这些资料作为参考方向提供，不作为强制要求。 合成管道详见UrbanTwin: Building High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Sim2Real LiDAR Perception and Evaluation（arXiv预印本），更深入的实证分析包括本挑战赛采用的分布真实性指标详见High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Bridging the Sim2Real Gap in LiDAR-Based ITS Perception（IEEE T-ITS，2026）。 使用该管道生成的合成LiDAR数据集发布在UrbanTwin: Synthetic Roadside LiDAR Datasets（IEEE OJ-ITS，2026），可在Harvard Dataverse下载。每个数据集包含**10K帧**，标注涵盖**六个物体类别**，支持**检测、跟踪和分割任务**，与本挑战赛采用的多类别评估直接兼容；论文中的实证分析包括分布真实性指标和单类别3D物体检测概念验证研究。对于端到端LiDAR处理，我们还提供LiGuard框架（IEEE T-IV，2026），以及更简洁的软件相关阅读《开源软件期刊》。 ## 你将要做的事 1. 下载公开的真实**V2X-Real**数据集和已发布的检测测试点云（50个真实帧，无标签）。 2. 使用任何方法生成合成LiDAR帧——模拟（CARLA、LGSVL、自定义）、生成模型（扩散、GAN、基于流的模型）、混合管道或其他任何方法。 3. **仅在你的合成数据**上训练3D物体检测器（任何架构）。 4. 提交： - 50个你的合成LiDAR帧 - 你的检测器对50个已发布测试点云的预测结果 - 一份签署的诚信声明 ## 评分概览 综合得分 = `0.6 × 归一化3D mAP` + `0.4 × 归一化真实性`，其中3D mAP在本赛道定义的**3个**物体类别（*车辆、行人、卡车*）上求平均，真实性对归一化倒角距离、最大均值差异、地球移动距离和Fréchet点云距离求平均

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation Protocol

Two scores are computed and combined into a single Combined score that determines leaderboard rank.

1. Distributional realism

Aggregation:

  1. Concatenate the 50 submitted synthetic frames into one set S_syn; concatenate the 50 held-out real reference frames into S_real.
  2. Mask both to the point-cloud range [-40, -40, -8, 40, 40, 2].
  3. Subsample uniformly at random to N = 10,000 points per side, with seed 1234 (identical seed used by the local evaluator in the starter kit).
  4. Compute one CD, MMD, EMD, and FPD across the entire 10,000-point sets.

1a. Chamfer Distance (CD)

CD(P, Q) = (1/|P|) Σ_{p ∈ P} min_{q ∈ Q} ||p - q||²
         + (1/|Q|) Σ_{q ∈ Q} min_{p ∈ P} ||p - q||²

Squared-L2 nearest-neighbor cost; symmetric. Lower is better.

1b. Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD)

MMD²(X, Y) = E[k(x, x')] + E[k(y, y')] - 2 E[k(x, y)],   k(a, b) = exp(-γ ||a - b||²)

Unbiased estimator (off-diagonal). Bandwidth γ is set by the median heuristic on a 1 000-point joint subsample (γ = 1 / (2 · median ||x - y||²)) so the kernel does not saturate at LiDAR spatial scales. Lower is better.

1c. Earth Mover's Distance (EMD)

EMD(X, Y) = √ ( min_{T ∈ Π(X, Y)} Σ_{i,j} T_{ij} · ||x_i - y_j|| )

Wasserstein-1 with Euclidean ground cost, solved exactly by the network simplex (POT's ot.emd2). Reported in metres. Lower is better.

1d. Fréchet Point-cloud Distance (FPD)

FPD = ||μ_X - μ_Y||² + Tr(Σ_X + Σ_Y - 2 (Σ_X · Σ_Y)^{1/2})

FID-style: fits a 3-variate Gaussian to each set's points, computes the 2-Wasserstein between Gaussians. Lower is better.

2. 3D Object Detection

Participants submit detections (predictions.json) on 50 real LiDAR frames whose ground truth is held out. We compute average precision over the 3 object categories defined for this track (vehicle, pedestrian, truck), at IoU thresholds 0.5 (primary) and 0.7 (secondary). Per-class AP is reported, and mean AP across classes (mAP) is the leaderboard's detection score; classes with zero ground-truth instances in the held-out set are excluded from the mean. Both KITTI 11-point and 40-point interpolated AP are reported; the 40-point form is the leaderboard primary.

Ground-truth and predicted boxes use the OpenPCDet 7-DoF format [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading]. IoU is computed as 3D intersection-over-union between two oriented BEV rectangles times the Z overlap. The KITTI truncation/occlusion/min-height difficulty filter is not applied because those depend on 2D bounding-box annotations that are not natural for roadside LiDAR datasets.

The valid class strings for this track are listed in config.json (shipped in reference_data/) and in submission_format.md in the starter kit. Any prediction with an unrecognized class label is discarded.

3. Combined score

Each component is min-max normalized into [0, 1] using a per-track normalization range:

score_realism   = mean( norm(CD), norm(MMD), norm(EMD), norm(FPD) )    (lower-is-better → 1 - clip)
score_detection = norm( AP_3d @ IoU 0.5 )                               (higher-is-better → clip)
score_combined  = 0.6 · score_detection + 0.4 · score_realism

Normalization endpoints are public in config.json (shipped in reference_data/), so the local evaluator and the server compute identical scores.

Reproducibility

  • Realism is dataset-level — frame ordering does not matter. Submit the 50 synthetic frames in any consistent naming.
  • Subsampling RNG seed: 1234 (same on server and starting kit).
  • The exact scoring program shipped to the Codabench worker is included in the starting kit.
pages.content_zh:
# 评估协议

计算两个分数并将其合并为单一的综合分数，该分数决定排行榜排名。

1. 分布真实性

聚合：

  1. 将50帧提交的合成帧连接成一个集合S_syn；将50帧保留的真实参考帧连接成S_real。
  2. 将两者掩码到点云范围[-40, -40, -8, 40, 40, 2]。
  3. 以均匀随机方式以每侧N = 10,000个点进行下采样，种子值为1234（与启动工具包中的本地评估器使用的种子相同）。
  4. 在整个10,000个点的集合上计算一个 CD、MMD、EMD和FPD。

1a. 倒角距离（CD）

CD(P, Q) = (1/|P|) Σ_{p ∈ P} min_{q ∈ Q} ||p - q||²
         + (1/|Q|) Σ_{q ∈ Q} min_{p ∈ P} ||p - q||²

平方L2最近邻成本；对称。越低越好。

1b. 最大平均差异（MMD）

MMD²(X, Y) = E[k(x, x')] + E[k(y, y')] - 2 E[k(x, y)],   k(a, b) = exp(-γ ||a - b||²)

无偏估计量（非对角线）。带宽γ由1,000个点的联合子样本上的中位数启发式设置（γ = 1 / (2 · median ||x - y||²)），使核在激光雷达空间尺度不会饱和。越低越好。

1c. 地球搬运距离（EMD）

EMD(X, Y) = √ ( min_{T ∈ Π(X, Y)} Σ_{i,j} T_{ij} · ||x_i - y_j|| )

Wasserstein-1距离，欧几里得地面成本，由网络单纯形精确求解（POT的ot.emd2）。以米为单位报告。越低越好。

1d. Fréchet点云距离（FPD）

FPD = ||μ_X - μ_Y||² + Tr(Σ_X + Σ_Y - 2 (Σ_X · Σ_Y)^{1/2})

FID风格：对每个集合的点拟合3变量高斯分布，计算高斯分布之间的2-Wasserstein距离。越低越好。

2. 三维物体检测

参赛者在50帧真实激光雷达帧上提交检测结果（predictions.json），这些帧的真实标签被保留。我们计算在本赛道定义的3个物体类别（车辆、行人、卡车）上的平均精度，IoU阈值为0.5（主要）和0.7（次要）。报告按类别的AP，类别间的平均AP（mAP）是排行榜的检测分数；保留集中真实标签数为零的类别被排除在平均值外。报告KITTI 11点和40点插值AP；40点形式是排行榜的主要指标。

真实标签和预测框使用OpenPCDet 7-DoF格式[x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading]。IoU计算为两个有向BEV矩形的三维交并比乘以Z重叠。未应用KITTI截断/遮挡/最小高度难度过滤，因为这些取决于对于路边激光雷达数据集不自然的二维边界框注释。

本赛道的有效类别字符串列在config.json中（在reference_data/中提供）和启动工具包中的submission_format.md中。任何具有无法识别的类别标签的预测都将被丢弃。

3. 综合分数

每个组件使用按赛道的归一化范围被最小-最大归一化到[0, 1]：

score_realism   = mean( norm(CD), norm(MMD), norm(EMD), norm(FPD) )    (越低越好 → 1 - clip)
score_detection = norm( AP_3d @ IoU 0.5 )                               (越高越好 → clip)
score_combined  = 0.6 · score_detection + 0.4 · score_realism

归一化端点在config.json中公开（在reference_data/中提供），因此本地评估器和服务器计算相同的分数。

pages.title: Data
pages.content:
Data

V2X-Real

Real V2X-Real data is publicly available from its original release. We do not redistribute it. Participants must obtain the real dataset directly from its source under its own license.

  • Source: https://github.com/ucla-mobility/V2X-Real
  • License: see the source.

Released for participants

The starting kit (Files tab → starting_kit) contains:

  • detection_test_frames/ — 50 real LiDAR frames (point clouds only, no labels) on which you must run your detector and submit predictions.
  • detection_test_frame_ids.json — the canonical list of frame IDs your predictions.json must cover, in order.
  • forbidden_frames.txt — 100 frame IDs you may not train, validate, or hyperparameter-tune on. This is the union of the 50 detection-test frames and the 50 realism-reference frames. Honor system, enforced by signed declaration in your submission.
  • local_eval.py — the exact scoring program shipped to the Codabench worker. Run it locally to reproduce server scores bit-for-bit, given a dummy reference set you generate from the released detection-test frames.
  • make_dummy_submission.py — produces a known-bad submission that exercises the format. Useful for sanity-checking your pipeline.
  • submission_format.md — full submission spec.

Held out (organizer-only)

  • 50 real frames used as the realism reference set.
  • Ground-truth boxes for the 50 detection-test frames.

Categories evaluated

This track is scored on 3 object categories defined for the V2X-Real dataset: vehicle, pedestrian, truck. The leaderboard's detection score is the mean AP across these categories; classes with zero ground-truth instances in the held-out 50-frame set are excluded from the mean.

Splits

Splits are stratified random samples with fixed seed 1234. The exact frame ID lists are published in the starting kit so anyone can reproduce them from the released real dataset.

Reference baselines

The numbers below are reported for the Car class only, taken from prior work on this dataset. The leaderboard's detection score is the mean AP across all categories defined for this track (see Evaluation), so submissions are scored on broader coverage than these single-class references. The baselines are included to demonstrate that sim → real transfer is achievable on this benchmark and to provide a per-class reference point for orientation while you iterate.

SystemCar 3D AP @ 0.5Car 3D AP @ 0.7
V2X-Real no-fusion benchmark (SECOND, real) 0.3556 n/r
SECOND (UT-V2X-Real synthetic → V2X-Real-IC, IEEE T-ITS 2026) 0.6318 n/r
pages.content_zh:
数据

V2X-Real

真实的V2X-Real数据从其原始发布以来已公开可用。我们不重新分发该数据集。参赛者必须根据其许可证直接从源获取真实数据集。

  • 来源： https://github.com/ucla-mobility/V2X-Real
  • 许可证：见来源。

为参赛者发布的资源

起始工具包（Files选项卡 → starting_kit）包含：

  • detection_test_frames/ — 50个真实激光雷达帧（仅点云，无标签），您必须在这些帧上运行检测器并提交预测。
  • detection_test_frame_ids.json — 您的predictions.json必须按顺序涵盖的规范帧ID列表。
  • forbidden_frames.txt — 100个帧ID，您不能在其上进行训练、验证或超参数调整。这是50个检测测试帧和50个真实性参考帧的并集。基于荣誉制度，由您提交中的签署声明执行。
  • local_eval.py — 发送到Codabench工作者的确切评分程序。在本地运行以从发布的检测测试帧生成虚拟参考集后，逐位重现服务器分数。
  • make_dummy_submission.py — 生成已知的不良提交来测试格式。对于验证您的管道很有用。
  • submission_format.md — 完整的提交规范。

保留（仅组织者）

  • 50个用作真实性参考集的真实帧。
  • 50个检测测试帧的真实标注框。

评估的类别

本赛道在V2X-Real数据集定义的3个目标类别上评分：车辆、行人、卡车。排行榜的检测分数是这些类别中的平均AP；在保留的50帧集中没有真实实例的类别从平均值中排除。

数据集划分

划分是使用固定种子1234的分层随机样本。精确的帧ID列表已在起始工具包中发布，以便任何人都可以从发布的真实数据集中重现它们。

参考基线

下面报告的数字仅适用于车辆类，来自该数据集上的先前工作。排行榜的检测分数是该赛道定义的所有类别的平均AP（见评估），因此提交在比这些单类参考更广泛的覆盖范围上评分。包括这些基线是为了证明模拟→真实转移在该基准上是可实现的，并为您迭代时提供每类参考点以供参考。

系统车辆3D AP @ 0.5车辆3D AP @ 0.7

pages.title: Submission
pages.content:
Submission Format

Pack everything below into a single submission.zip and upload it on the Submit tab.

submission.zip
├── synthetic/
│   ├── 0001.bin
│   ├── 0002.bin
│   ├── ...
│   └── 0050.bin           # exactly 50 files
├── predictions.json
└── declaration.pdf        # signed honor declaration (PDF). declaration.txt also accepted.

synthetic/<id>.bin

  • Exactly 50 files.
  • Each file is raw float32, shape N × 3, in row-major order, with channels (x, y, z) in metres.
  • Either N × 3 or N × 4 (xyz + intensity) is accepted; the intensity column, if present, is dropped before scoring.
  • Each file ≤ 1.5 MB on disk (~125,000 points). Realism is computed at the dataset level: all 50 frames are concatenated, masked to the track's point-cloud range, then subsampled to 10,000 points (seed 1234) before computing CD / MMD / EMD / FPD. Submitting denser frames does not improve scores; frame ordering does not matter.
  • The simplest valid naming is 0001.bin … 0050.bin.

predictions.json

JSON object whose keys are the frame IDs from detection_test_frame_ids.json (in the starting kit). For every frame ID you must include an entry, even if the value is an empty list.

{
  "<frame_id_1>": [
    {"box": [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading], "score": 0.97, "class": "vehicle"},
    {"box": [...],                          "score": 0.81, "class": "pedestrian"}
  ],
  "<frame_id_2>": [],
  ...
}
  • box: 7 floats, OpenPCDet convention. (x, y, z) is the box center in metres in the LiDAR frame, (dx, dy, dz) are full extents along the box-local axes, heading is rotation around +Z in radians.
  • score: confidence in [0, 1].
  • class: one of the valid class strings for this track. Valid values: vehicle, pedestrian, truck. Class strings are matched case-insensitively. Predictions with unrecognized class strings are discarded before AP is computed.

declaration.pdf (or declaration.txt)

The starter kit ships declaration_template.pdf, a one-page form with the required honor statement preprinted and a signature line. Fill in team name and date, sign (digitally with any PDF tool, or print → sign → scan), save as declaration.pdf, and include it in every submission.

If you cannot easily produce a signed PDF, a plain declaration.txt is also accepted. Required statement (verbatim, case-insensitive):

I confirm that I did not train on any frame listed in forbidden_frames.txt, and that all submitted detections were produced by a model trained only on synthetic data I generated.

What gets returned

After scoring (typically < 5 minutes for valid submissions) you'll see your position on the leaderboard plus a Detailed Results view with all component metrics, including per-class AP.
pages.content_zh:
# 提交格式

将以下所有内容打包到单个 `submission.zip` 中，然后在*提交*标签页上传。

```
submission.zip
├── synthetic/
│   ├── 0001.bin
│   ├── 0002.bin
│   ├── ...
│   └── 0050.bin           # 恰好50个文件
├── predictions.json
└── declaration.pdf        # 签署的荣誉声明（PDF）。也接受 declaration.txt。
```

## synthetic/<id>.bin

- 恰好 **50** 个文件。
- 每个文件为原始 `float32` 格式，形状为 `N × 3`，按行主序存储，通道为 `(x, y, z)`（单位：米）。
- 接受 `N × 3` 或 `N × 4`（xyz + 强度）格式；若存在强度列，计分前会将其丢弃。
- 每个文件 ≤ 1.5 MB（约 125,000 个点）。真实感在数据集级别计算：将所有 50 帧连接，遮罩到轨迹的点云范围，然后下采样到 10,000 个点（种子 1234），再计算 CD / MMD / EMD / FPD。提交更密集的帧不会改善分数；帧顺序无关。
- 最简单的有效命名为 `0001.bin … 0050.bin`。

## predictions.json

JSON 对象，其键为 `detection_test_frame_ids.json`（在初始工具包中）中的帧 ID。对每个帧 ID 必须包含一个条目，即使值为空列表也是如此。

```
{
  "<frame_id_1>": [
    {"box": [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading], "score": 0.97, "class": "vehicle"},
    {"box": [...],                          "score": 0.81, "class": "pedestrian"}
  ],
  "<frame_id_2>": [],
  ...
}
```

- `box`：7 个浮点数，遵循 OpenPCDet 规范。`(x, y, z)` 是盒子*中心*在 LiDAR 坐标系中的位置（单位：米），`(dx, dy, dz)` 是沿盒子局部轴的完整尺寸，`heading` 是围绕 `+Z` 的旋转（单位：弧度）。
- `score`：置信度，范围 [0, 1]。
- `class`：此轨迹的有效类别字符串之一。有效值：`vehicle`（车辆）、`pedestrian`（行人）、`truck`（卡车）。类别字符串匹配不区分大小写。计算 AP 前会丢弃具有无法识别类别字符串的预测。

## declaration.pdf（或 declaration.txt）

初始工具包包含 `declaration_template.pdf`，这是一份单页表单，具有预先打印的必需荣誉声明和签名行。填入团队名称和日期，签署（使用任何 PDF 工具进行数字签名，或打印 → 签署 → 扫描），另存为 `declaration.pdf`，并将其包含在每次提交中。

如果无法轻松生成签署的 PDF，也接受纯文本 `declaration.txt`。必需声明（逐字，不区分大小写）：

> *我确认我没有对 `forbidden_frames.txt` 中列出的任何帧进行训练，且所有提交的检测都是由仅在我生成的合成数据上训练的模型生成的。*

## 返回内容

评分后（有效提交通常 < 5 分钟），您将在排行榜上看到您的位置，以及包含所有组件指标的*详细结果*视图，包括按类别的 AP。

pages.title: Rules
pages.content:
Rules

Eligibility

  • Open to anyone — researchers, students, industry teams.
  • Each team must register one participant account; do not maintain multiple accounts.

Allowed

  • Any simulation framework or generative model (CARLA, Helios++, OpenScene, neural radiance fields, diffusion, GANs, custom physics). Open or closed source — what matters is the synthesized data.
  • Any 3D object detector architecture, trained on your synthetic data only.
  • Augmentations applied during detector training (rotation, scale, flip, ground-truth sampling, noise) — they operate on synthetic data, not on the forbidden real frames.
  • Using the train split of the public real dataset for hyperparameter selection or domain adaptation, provided no forbidden frame is touched. (The forbidden list contains only the 100 reserved frames, not the entire real train split.)

Forbidden

  • Training, validating, hyperparameter-tuning, or otherwise observing ground truth from any of the 100 frames listed in forbidden_frames.txt. This is enforced by signed declaration and is the foundational integrity rule of the challenge.
  • Submitting predictions produced by a model that has been trained on real labels for any roadside-LiDAR dataset. The detector must be sim-only.
  • Reverse-engineering or inferring the held-out realism reference frames via Codabench's leaderboard signal (e.g., probing submissions designed to leak the reference set's identity). Submissions found to be doing this will be disqualified.
  • Multiple accounts, sub-team accounts, or coordinating across registered teams.

Disqualification

Organizers reserve the right to inspect the synthetic frames and predictions of any submission for evidence of forbidden-frame leakage (e.g., synthetic frames that suspiciously resemble held-out real frames; predictions whose distribution implies access to held-out ground truth). Disqualified participants are removed from the leaderboard and from prize consideration.

Prizes

Per track: 1st place USD 500, 2nd place USD 300, 3rd place USD 200. Sponsor(s) will be announced before the Development phase opens.

Publication and credit

  • Every participating team submits a 4–8 page challenge report describing their approach.
  • Teams that prefer not to publish may opt into the workshop's non-publication track for their submission.
  • Top-3 teams per track are additionally invited to submit a full paper to the proceedings track of the next edition of the DriveX Workshop.
  • The challenge organizers may publish an aggregate analysis of all submissions (anonymized unless explicit permission is granted).
pages.content_zh:
规则

参赛资格

  • 面向所有人开放——研究人员、学生、产业团队均可参赛。
  • 每个团队必须注册一个参赛者账户，不得维持多个账户。

允许的内容

  • 任何仿真框架或生成模型（CARLA、Helios++、OpenScene、神经辐射场、扩散模型、GAN、自定义物理引擎）。开源或闭源均可——重要的是合成数据的质量。
  • 任何3D目标检测器架构，仅在你自己生成的合成数据上训练。
  • 检测器训练过程中应用的数据增强（旋转、缩放、翻转、真值采样、噪声）——这些操作作用于合成数据，而非禁止的真实图像。
  • 使用公共真实数据集的训练集进行超参数选择或域适应，条件是不接触任何禁止的图像。（禁止列表仅包含100个保留帧，不包括整个真实训练集。）

禁止的内容

  • 对forbidden_frames.txt中列出的任何100帧进行训练、验证、超参数调整或以其他方式观察其真值标注。这由签署声明强制执行，是本挑战赛的基础完整性规则。
  • 提交由在任何路侧激光雷达数据集的真实标签上训练过的模型所生成的预测结果。检测器必须仅基于仿真数据。
  • 通过Codabench排行榜信号逆向工程或推断被保留的真实参考帧（例如，设计用于泄露参考集身份的探测性提交）。发现进行此操作的提交将被取消资格。
  • 多个账户、子团队账户或已注册团队间的协调。

取消资格

组织者保留权利检查任何提交的合成图像和预测结果，以寻找禁止帧泄露的证据（例如，与被保留真实图像可疑相似的合成帧；其分布暗示获得了被保留真值标注的预测）。被取消资格的参赛者将从排行榜和奖项考虑中被移除。

奖金

每个赛道：第1名USD 500，第2名USD 300，第3名USD 200。赞助商信息将在开发阶段开始前公布。

发表与署名

  • 每支参赛团队提交一份4–8页的挑战赛报告，描述其方法。
  • 不愿发表的团队可选择参加研讨会的非发表赛道。
  • 每个赛道的前3名团队另外邀请向下一届DriveX研讨会论文集赛道提交完整论文。
  • 挑战赛组织者可发表所有提交的汇总分析（匿名处理，除非获得明确授权）。
