pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
##
[MICCAI FLARE26](https://flare-medfm.github.io/) Task 2: AutoMSC: Automated Medical image Segmentation and Classification
Deep learning models for 3D medical imaging have traditionally been handcrafted for individual tasks, either segmentation or classification, requiring extensive manual tuning of architectures, hyperparameters, and preprocessing pipelines. As clinical datasets grow in scale and complexity, this manual design process becomes increasingly inefficient and limits the deployment of adaptable, general-purpose models. Motivated by the success of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon challenge and nnU-Net (the winning solution), Task 2 focuses on building self-configured models capable of automatically adapting to diverse 3D medical imaging datasets while simultaneously performing both segmentation and classification. This task aims to advance the next generation of autonomous modeldesign systems for 3D medical imaging. Participants are required to design models that can automatically infer optimal configurations (e.g., architecture, resolution, patch size, normalization strategy, and loss balancing) and jointly learn highquality segmentation masks and clinically meaningful classification labels. These models should generalize across imaging modality, tumor types without taskspecific manual engineering, including prostate cancer recurrence prediction in MRI scans, lung nodule diagnosis in CT scans, and liver metastasis origin prediction in PET/CT scans. Key Features: - **Multi-task Learning**: Models must perform both 3D segmentation and classification from the same input volume, optimizing for accuracy in both outputs while maintaining computational efficiency. - **Self-configuration**: Solutions should include automated configuration mechanisms capable of adapting to dataset properties, such as voxel spacing, image size, contrast variability, and class imbalance, without human-designed heuristics. - **Dataset Diversity**: The benchmark includes heterogeneous 3D medical imaging scans with varying modalities (CT, MRI, and PET-CT) and classification targets, encouraging the development of truly generalizable 3D models. - **Robustness and Efficiency**: Models will be evaluated on segmentation accuracy (DSC and NSD), classification performance (balanced accuracy and AUROC), and resource efficiency (runtime), highlighting their potential for real-world clinical adoption. Participants are also encouraged to explore other challenge tracks at https://flare-medfm.github.io/, including: pan-cancer segmentation, and multimodal models. --- ## 🚀 Join the challenge (2026.04.01-8.20) * Register an account on this website and join the challenge * Fill out the [registration form](https://forms.gle/my1MimQ758oDyhWb9) Note: To change team information, please simply re-submit the form. * Test your account by making a submission with [baseline](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Awx9GE4kMNBCdZa0nxc5957f327tlQb5/view?usp=drive_link) * Request Dataset [FLARE-AutoMSC](https://huggingface.co/datasets/FLARE-MedFM/FLARE-AutoMSC). We will approve your request in 1-2 working days after reviewing your application. Remarks: * This challenge has two tracks: 1) Unified models for joint segmentation and classification (e.g., [JSC](https://github.com/bowang-lab/JSC)). 2) Independent models for segmentation (e.g., [nnUNet](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet)) or classification ([nnClass](https://github.com/bowang-lab/nnClass)). Participants can join one track or both tracks. * For both tracks, solutions should include automated configuration mechanisms capable of adapting to different datasets. * Clinical data (if available) is optional but encouraged for model development. * If you have any questions that are not listed on the QA page, please reach out to chingyuanyu.iec@gmail.com --- ## 🏊‍ Validation submission (2026.4.20-8.20) * All teams can directly submit the validation results on the challenge page to get the metrics. * To get the runtime metrics, participants are allowed to make one docker submission every week by sending email to chingyuanyu.iec@gmail.com. ### Baseline Docker output([example](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FA1eVlaJuXy9uOtpZY-2AXnQqNQLQGLc/view?usp=drive_link)) ### Submission format ([example](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Awx9GE4kMNBCdZa0nxc5957f327tlQb5/view?usp=drive_link)) Submit a **single ZIP** whose contents sit in one **flat** directory (no sub-folders): ``` submission.zip ├── predictions.csv # classification predictions ├── BT0001.nii.gz # predicted segmentation masks (same level as the CSV) ├── BT0007.nii.gz └── ... ``` **Segmentation masks** — one file per case, named `{identifier}.nii.gz` (e.g. `BT0001.nii.gz`), binary whole-tumor label (`1` = tumor, `0` = background), same geometry (spacing orientation, and origin) as the input image. **predictions.csv** — one row per case, with the exact column headers (case-sensitive, in this order): | Column | Description | |--------|---------| | `identifier` | case ID, e.g. `BT0001` | | `idh_wildtype` | Probability(IDH = Unaltered / wild-type) | | `idh_mutated` | Probability(IDH = Altered / mutated) | | `grade2` | Probability(Grade 2) | |`grade3` | Probability(Grade 3) | | `grade4` | Probability(Grade 4) | Example: |identifier|idh_wildtype|idh_mutated|grade2|grade3|grade4| |--------|---------|--------|---------|--------|---------| |BT0001|0.90|0.10|0.10|0.30|0.60| |BT0007|0.15|0.85|0.05|0.25|0.70| Notes: * Column headers and mask filenames must match exactly so predictions can be paired with the ground truth; missing cases are scored 0. * Model ensemble are not allowed in this competition. (If the data contains two different classification tasks, it's allowed to train two separate models but it's not allowed to train multiple models (or multi-fold ensemble) for ensemble for the same classification task.) --- ## 🏹 Testing submission (2026.8.20-8.31) The submitted Docker container will be evaluated with the following commands. If the Docker container does not work or the paper does not include all the necessary information to reproduce the method, we will return back the error information and review comments to participants. docker load -i teamname.tar.gz docker container run --gpus "device=1" -m 28G --name teamname --rm -v \$PWD/FLARE_Test/:/workspace/inputs/ -v \$PWD/teamname_outputs/:/workspace/outputs/ teamname:latest /bin/bash -c "sh predict.sh" ## Paper submission(Due on 8.31) Please parepare the paper with this [template-tbd]() and submit it on [openreview](https://openreview.net/group) by Aug. 31, 2026. Please carefully read the template and the common issue before writing the manuscript. The evaluation process mainly focuses on the paper's completeness. Don't worry about the low performance. Since this task is very challenging, all attempts are worth sharing with readers. We will not reject papers because of Iow performance. --- ## 🏆 Awards - If there are more than 20 testing docker submissions, we will provide cash prizes for the top 5 teams (Amazon gift cards with 300/200/150/100/100 CAD, respectively) and souvenirs for the top 6-10 teams. Otherwise, only the winning team will be provided with the cash prize. - The top 5 teams will be invited to give oral presentations during MICCAI 2026. - The first author of the top 5 teams will be invited to contribute to a challenge summary paper. - A certificate will be awarded to the top 10 teams. (Top teams should make their code publicly available on GitHub for reproducibility.) - All teams have the opportunity to publish their methods in the challenge proceeding (Tentative LNCS, EI Index). [Here](https://link.springer.com/conference/flare) is an example of our previous FLARE Challenge. The challenge summary paper will be submitted to top-tired journals. Here are some of our previous summaries: * "Fast and low-GPU-memory abdomen CT organ segmentation: the flare challenge." Medical Image Analysis 82 (2022): 102616. * "Unleashing the strengths of unlabeled data in pan-cancer abdominal organ quantification: the flare22 challenge." Lancet Digital Health (2024). * "The multimodality cell segmentation challenge: toward universal solutions." Nature Methods (2024): 21, 1103–1113.
pages.content_zh:
## <center>[MICCAI FLARE26](https://flare-medfm.github.io/) 任务2: AutoMSC: 自动医学图像分割和分类</center>

用于3D医学成像的深度学习模型传统上是为单个任务(分割或分类)手工设计的，需要对架构、超参数和预处理管道进行大量手动调整。随着临床数据集规模和复杂性的增加，这种手动设计过程变得越来越低效，限制了自适应通用模型的部署。受医学分割十项全能挑战赛和获胜方案nnU-Net成功的启发，任务2侧重于构建能够自动适应多样化3D医学成像数据集，同时执行分割和分类的自配置模型。

本任务旨在推进3D医学成像自主模型设计系统的下一代发展。参赛者需要设计能够自动推断最优配置(如架构、分辨率、补丁大小、归一化策略和损失平衡)的模型，并联合学习高质量分割掩码和临床有意义的分类标签。这些模型应能跨成像模态、肿瘤类型进行泛化，无需特定任务的手动工程，包括MRI扫描中的前列腺癌复发预测、CT扫描中的肺结节诊断和PET/CT扫描中的肝转移灶来源预测。

主要特征：

- **多任务学习**：模型必须从同一输入体积执行3D分割和分类，同时优化两个输出的精度并保持计算效率。
- **自配置**：解决方案应包含自动配置机制，能够适应数据集属性，如体素间距、图像大小、对比度变异性和类不平衡，无需人工设计的启发式方法。
- **数据集多样性**：基准包括具有不同模态(CT、MRI和PET-CT)和分类目标的异构3D医学成像扫描，促进真正可泛化3D模型的开发。
- **鲁棒性和效率**：模型将基于分割精度(DSC和NSD)、分类性能(平衡精度和AUROC)和资源效率(运行时间)进行评估，突出其在实际临床应用中的潜力。

参赛者还被鼓励探索其他挑战赛道，网址为https://flare-medfm.github.io/，包括：泛癌症分割和多模态模型。

---

## 🚀 加入挑战赛(2026.04.01开放)

* 在本网站注册账户并加入挑战赛
* 填写[注册表](https://forms.gle/my1MimQ758oDyhWb9)   注：若需修改团队信息，请重新提交表格。
* 申请数据集[FLARE-AutoMSC](https://huggingface.co/datasets/FLARE-MedFM/FLARE-AutoMSC)。我们将在审核申请后1-2个工作日内批准您的申请。

备注：
* 本挑战赛分为两个赛道：1) 用于联合分割和分类的统一模型(如[JSC](https://github.com/bowang-lab/JSC))。2) 用于分割(如[nnUNet](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet))或分类的独立模型([nnClass](https://github.com/bowang-lab/nnClass))。参赛者可参加一个或两个赛道。
* 对于两个赛道，解决方案应包含能够适应不同数据集的自动配置机制。
* 如有常见问题页面未列出的问题，请联系chingyuanyu.iec@gmail.com

pages.title: Dataset
pages.content:
## Datasets

### Dataset 001 — BrainMets (PROTEAS)
* A longitudinal multi-modal brain metastasis dataset with 6 co-registered channels (T1, T1c, T2, FLAIR, CT, RTP). Provides **3-class tumor segmentation** (necrotic core, enhancing tumor, edema) and **NSCLC vs. Breast Carcinoma** primary-origin classification. 
* 166 cases
* Licence: CC BY 4.0.

**Source:** Flouri D, Papanikas CP, Manikis GC, et al. *A longitudinal MRI dataset of brain metastases with tumor segmentations, clinical & radiomic data.* **Scientific Data**, 19 Nov 2025; 12:1828.

### Dataset 002 — MU_Glioma_Post
**Post-treatment glioma** multi-sequence MRI (t1c, t1n, t2f, t2w) with **4-class tumor segmentation** (NCR, ED, ET, NET_RC) and a **3-class primary diagnosis** label (GBM / Astrocytoma / Other). 591 timepoints from 203 patients (longitudinal).
**Source:** Mahmoud E, Gass J, Dhemesh Y, et al. *MU-Glioma Post: A comprehensive dataset of automated MR multi-sequence segmentation and clinical features.* **Scientific Data**, 20 Nov 2025; 12(1):1847.

### Dataset 003 — UCSD_PTGB
The **UCSD post-treatment glioblastoma** cohort imaged with T1post, FLAIR, and ADC. Provides **total cellular tumor** masks and **IDH mutation status** (wild-type vs. mutant). 184 cases, 3 channels.
**Source:** Gagnon L, Gupta D, Nguyen U, et al. *The University of California San Diego Post-Treatment Glioblastoma (UCSD-PTGBM) annotated multimodal MRI Dataset.* **Scientific Data**, 6 Jan 2026.

### Dataset 004 — PI-CAI
The largest dataset in the benchmark: **prostate MRI** (T2W, ADC, HBV) for **clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) segmentation** and **6-class ISUP grade** classification (Benign/Indolent + ISUP 1–5). 1,500 cases from 1,476 patients across 11 sites.
**Source:** Saha A, Bosma JS, Twilt JJ, et al. *Artificial intelligence and radiologists in prostate cancer detection on MRI (PI-CAI): an international, paired, non-inferiority, confirmatory study.* **Lancet Oncology**, 2024; 25:879–887.

### Dataset 005 — LUNA25
Cropped **low-dose chest CT patches** from the **LUNA25 challenge** for lung cancer screening. Each patch contains a nodule with a **segmentation mask** and a **benign vs. malignant** risk label. 6,141 nodule crops, single CT channel. Licence: CC BY 4.0.
**Source:** Peeters D, Obreja B, Antonissen N, Jacobs C. *Benchmarking of Artificial Intelligence and Radiologists for Lung Cancer Screening in CT: The LUNA25 Challenge.* **MICCAI 2025** (Zenodo: [10.5281/zenodo.15094631](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15094631)).

### Dataset 061 — PETWB_Lung
A subset of the **PETWB-REP** whole-body FDG PET/CT collection, paired with TotalSegmentator-derived **lung masks** and a **lung-cancer vs. other** label. 490 cases drawn from 4 cohorts, 2 channels (CT, PET). Tasks: binary lung segmentation + binary cancer-type classification. Licence: CC BY 4.0.
**Source:** Xue L, Feng G, Wenbo Z, et al. *PETWB-REP: A Multi-Cancer Whole-Body FDG PET/CT Dataset with Corresponding Radiology Reports.* **Scientific Data**, 2026.

### Dataset 062 — PETWB_Liver
Companion to Dataset 061 from the **same PETWB-REP source**, but targeting the **liver**: TotalSegmentator-derived liver masks paired with a **liver-cancer vs. other** label. 490 cases, 2 channels (CT, PET). Licence: CC BY 4.0.
**Source:** Xue L, Feng G, Wenbo Z, et al. *PETWB-REP: A Multi-Cancer Whole-Body FDG PET/CT Dataset with Corresponding Radiology Reports.* **Scientific Data**, 2026.
pages.content_zh:
## 数据集

### 数据集 001 — BrainMets (PROTEAS)
**纵向多模态脑转移瘤**数据集，包含6个共配准通道（T1、T1c、T2、FLAIR、CT、RTP）。提供**3类肿瘤分割**（坏死核心、增强肿瘤、水肿）和**非小细胞肺癌 vs. 乳腺癌**原发灶分类。40名患者共166个时间点。许可证：CC BY 4.0。
**来源：** Flouri D, Papanikas CP, Manikis GC, 等。*A longitudinal MRI dataset of brain metastases with tumor segmentations, clinical & radiomic data.* **Scientific Data**, 2025年11月19日; 12:1828。

### 数据集 002 — MU_Glioma_Post
**治疗后胶质瘤**多序列MRI（t1c、t1n、t2f、t2w），包含**4类肿瘤分割**（NCR、ED、ET、NET_RC）和**3类原发诊断**标签（胶质母细胞瘤/星形细胞瘤/其他）。来自203名患者的591个纵向时间点。
**来源：** Mahmoud E, Gass J, Dhemesh Y, 等。*MU-Glioma Post: A comprehensive dataset of automated MR multi-sequence segmentation and clinical features.* **Scientific Data**, 2025年11月20日; 12(1):1847。

### 数据集 003 — UCSD_PTGB
**加州大学圣地亚哥分校治疗后胶质母细胞瘤**队列，采用T1post、FLAIR和ADC成像。提供**全细胞肿瘤**掩模和**IDH突变状态**（野生型 vs. 突变型）。184个病例，3个通道。
**来源：** Gagnon L, Gupta D, Nguyen U, 等。*The University of California San Diego Post-Treatment Glioblastoma (UCSD-PTGBM) annotated multimodal MRI Dataset.* **Scientific Data**, 2026年1月6日。

### 数据集 004 — PI-CAI
基准中最大的数据集：**前列腺MRI**（T2W、ADC、HBV），用于**临床显著性前列腺癌（csPCa）分割**和**6级ISUP分级**分类（良性/惰性 + ISUP 1–5）。来自11个中心的1,476名患者的1,500个病例。
**来源：** Saha A, Bosma JS, Twilt JJ, 等。*Artificial intelligence and radiologists in prostate cancer detection on MRI (PI-CAI): an international, paired, non-inferiority, confirmatory study.* **Lancet Oncology**, 2024; 25:879–887。

### 数据集 005 — LUNA25
来自**LUNA25挑战赛**的裁剪**低剂量胸部CT图像块**，用于肺癌筛查。每个图像块包含一个结节及**分割掩模**和**良性 vs. 恶性**风险标签。6,141个结节裁剪图，单CT通道。许可证：CC BY 4.0。
**来源：** Peeters D, Obreja B, Antonissen N, Jacobs C。*Benchmarking of Artificial Intelligence and Radiologists for Lung Cancer Screening in CT: The LUNA25 Challenge.* **MICCAI 2025**（Zenodo: [10.5281/zenodo.15094631](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15094631)）。

### 数据集 061 — PETWB_Lung
**PETWB-REP**全身FDG PET/CT集合的子集，配对TotalSegmentator衍生的**肺掩模**和**肺癌 vs. 其他**标签。来自4个队列的490个病例，2个通道（CT、PET）。任务：二元肺分割 + 二元癌症类型分类。许可证：CC BY 4.0。
**来源：** Xue L, Feng G, Wenbo Z, 等。*PETWB-REP: A Multi-Cancer Whole-Body FDG PET/CT Dataset with Corresponding Radiology Reports.* **Scientific Data**, 2026。

### 数据集 062 — PETWB_Liver
来自**同一PETWB-REP来源**的数据集061的配套数据集，针对**肝脏**：TotalSegmentator衍生的肝脏掩模配对**肝癌 vs. 其他**标签。490个病例，2个通道（CT、PET）。许可证：CC BY 4.0。
**来源：** Xue L, Feng G, Wenbo Z, 等。*PETWB-REP: A Multi-Cancer Whole-Body FDG PET/CT Dataset with Corresponding Radiology Reports.* **Scientific Data**, 2026。

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content: ## Evaluation **Segmentation accuracy metrics:** * Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) * Normalized Surface Distance (NSD) **Binary classification accuracy metrics:** * Balanced Accuracy * Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC) **Accuracy Evaluation Scripts:** * https://github.com/medfm-flare/AutoMSC_Baseline **Segmentation efficiency metrics:** * Running time (s). We give running time a tolerance of 45s (including the docker starting time). Moreover, the inference time for each case should be within 60s. Otherwise, the corresponding case will be regarded as a failed case (DSC=0, NSD=0). ![running time](https://s2.loli.net/2024/04/06/Fvt1nmPYqZLWxsU.jpg) * GPU memory consumption (area under GPU memory-time curve). ![gpu memory](https://s2.loli.net/2024/03/14/XlnhM3qB27yVZtS.png) All metrics will be used to compute the ranking. We give GPU memory consumption a 4GB tolerance, GPU Memory = max(0, Real GPU Memory-4096MB) because all the previous top teams (i.e., FLARE21-23) can achieve state-of-the-art segmentation accuracy within this tolerance. We also give running time a tolerance (the running time of the winning solution in FLARE 2023) because it satisfies the typical clinical requirements and the code has been publicly available. Evaluation code has been publicly available at: https://github.com/JunMa11/FLARE docker load -i teamname.tar.gz docker container run --gpus "device=1" -m 28G --name teamname --rm -v \$PWD/FLARE_Test/:/workspace/inputs/ -v \$PWD/teamname_outputs/:/workspace/outputs/ teamname:latest /bin/bash -c "sh predict.sh" --- ## Evaluation Platform The submitted docker containers will be evaluated on a Ubuntu 20.04 desktop. Detailed information is listed as follows: * CPU: Intel® Xeon(R) W-2133 CPU @ 3.60GHz × 12 * GPU: NVIDIA QUADRO RTX5000 (16G) * RAM: 28G * CUDA Version: 13.0 * Docker version 29.4.2 --- ## Ranking Scheme Following the recommendation in ChallengeR [1], we eomply a rank-then-aggregate ranking scheme with the following three steps: Step 1. For each testing case, we compute the four metrics; Step 2. Rank participants for each of the N testing cases and each metric; Step 3. Average all these rankings. [1] Wiesenfarth, M., Reinke, A., Landman, B.A. et al. Methods and open-source toolkit for analyzing and visualizing challenge results. Sci Rep 11, 2369 (2021).
pages.content_zh: ## 评估 **分割精度指标：** * 骰子相似系数（DSC） * 归一化表面距离（NSD） **二分类精度指标：** * 平衡精度 * 受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUROC） **精度评估脚本：** * https://github.com/medfm-flare/AutoMSC_Baseline **分割效率指标：** * 运行时间（秒）。我们对运行时间给予45秒的容差（包括docker启动时间）。此外，每个病例的推理时间应在60秒以内。否则，该病例将被视为失败病例（DSC=0，NSD=0）。 ![运行时间](https://s2.loli.net/2024/04/06/Fvt1nmPYqZLWxsU.jpg) * GPU内存消耗（GPU内存-时间曲线下的面积）。 ![GPU内存](https://s2.loli.net/2024/03/14/XlnhM3qB27yVZtS.png) 所有指标都将用于计算排名。我们对GPU内存消耗给予4GB的容差，GPU内存 = max(0, 实际GPU内存-4096MB)，因为所有前期顶级团队（即FLARE21-23）都能在该容差范围内实现最先进的分割精度。我们还对运行时间给予容差（FLARE 2023中获胜方案的运行时间），因为它满足典型的临床要求且代码已公开发布。 评估代码已公开发布于：https://github.com/JunMa11/FLARE docker load -i teamname.tar.gz docker container run --gpus "device=1" -m 28G --name teamname --rm -v \$PWD/FLARE_Test/:/workspace/inputs/ -v \$PWD/teamname_outputs/:/workspace/outputs/ teamname:latest /bin/bash -c "sh predict.sh" --- ## 评估平台 提交的docker容器将在Ubuntu 20.04桌面上进行评估。详细信息如下： * CPU：Intel® Xeon(R) W-2133 CPU @ 3.60GHz × 12 * GPU：NVIDIA QUADRO RTX5000（16G） * RAM：28G * CUDA版本：13.0 * Docker版本29.4.2 --- ## 排名方案 根据ChallengeR [1]中的建议，我们采用先排名后聚合的排名方案，包含以下三个步骤： 步骤1. 对于每个测试病例，计算四项指标； 步骤2. 对每个测试病例和每项指标对参赛者进行排名； 步骤3. 对所有排名进行平均。 [1] Wiesenfarth, M., Reinke, A., Landman, B.A. et al. Methods and open-source toolkit for analyzing and visualizing challenge results. Sci Rep 11, 2369 (2021).

pages.title: Q&A
pages.content:
## Common Questions

Please send emails to chingyuanyu.iec@gmail.com if you have any other questions. 

**Q:  How long can the participation request be approved after sending the signed challenge rule?**

A:  The request will be approved within 2-4 working days if the signed challenge rule document is filled out correctly.

**Q: I'm only interested in the challenge dataset but I do not want to join the challenge. Can I download the dataset without joining the challenge?**

A: Thanks for your interest. To ensure enough submissions, the dataset is only available to participants during the challenge. 

**Q: How many people can form a team？**

A: Each team can have at most 6 people. The authors in your paper should be the same as the team member list.

**Q: I have joined the challenge and downloaded the dataset. Can I quit the challenge?**

A: No! Please respect the signed agreement. If registered participants do not make successful submissions, all the team members will be listed in the dishonest list.

Algorithm-related issues

**Q: Can we use other datasets or pre-trained models to develop the segmentation algorithms?**

A: Yes, but you need to post them in the forum first. 

**Q: Can we manually annotate the unlabeled images to enlarge the training set?**

A: No. Any manual interventions are not allowed. 

**Q: Can we manually select the high-quality pseudo labels for the unlabeled images?**

A: No. Any manual interventions are not allowed. 

**Q: Does the validation submission affects the final ranking?**

A: No.

**Q: During the testing phase, can I modify the methods and the paper?**

A: Yes, you can make modifications before the testing submission. After making the testing submission, you cannot make modifications.


**Q: Can I use validation set for model pre-training?**
A: No!

**Q: Can I use other public datasets for model pre-training?** 
A: Yes, but you should post the dataset link on forum and also need to submit an algorithm that is trained only with the challenge dataset. 

**Q: When can I access the testing set?**
A: The testing set will not be released during the challenge to avoid data leakage.

12418.title: PBVS 2026 - Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution (HISR) challenge
12418.description:
This challenge benchmarks ×4 super-resolution for close-range SWIR hyperspectral imaging.
Participants receive low-resolution HSI cubes acquired using the same sensor with different lenses to create controlled resolution variation without spectral bias. The task is to reconstruct a high-resolution SWIR hyperspectral image from a ×4 downsampled input.

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# PBVS @ CVPR 2026 - Hyperspectral Images Super-Resolution (HISR) challenge

## Overview

Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution (HISR) goes beyond conventional SR: hyperspectral data contain rich wavelength-dependent information, where each band encodes material-specific spectral signatures. This means HISR must simultaneously preserve spatial detail and spectral integrity, ensuring reconstructed images remain physically meaningful rather than visually plausible only.

HSI data are also large and acquisition-intensive, making full-resolution capture costly and slow. Super-resolution therefore offers a powerful and practical pathway to reduce acquisition burden while enabling high-quality analysis.

This challenge introduces the **first** hyperspectral super-resolution benchmark within the PBVS CVPR 2026 workshop. It focuses on real LR-HR pairs, at ×4 SR under controlled lab conditions, using data collected with the same sensor and different optics to isolate spatial scaling while maintaining spectral consistency. 

**The challenge is to reconstruct ×4 real super-resolution hyperspectral images from the provided low-resolution hyperspectral patches image.**

Each low-resolution cube has a perfectly aligned high-resolution counterpart that serves as ground truth, enabling precise evaluation of both spatial recovery and spectral fidelity.
Participants develop methods that upscale the LR data by x4 while preserving spectral consistency across all wavelengths.


## Important dates

- 2026.01.12 Release of train and validation dataset (input and output)
- **2026.01.15 Test data release (inputs only)**
- 2026.01.15 Testing phase server online

- **2026.03.01 Test output results submission deadline**
- 2026.03.03 Contribution from participants (top results should provide a brief description of the proposed solution together with an illustration of the architecture; code also should be shared)
- **2026.03.06 Paper submission deadline for entries from the challenge**
- 2026.06.03 PBVS workshop and challenges, results and award ceremony (CVPR 2026)
pages.content_zh:
# PBVS @ CVPR 2026 - 高光谱图像超分辨率（HISR）挑战赛

## 概述

高光谱图像超分辨率（HISR）超越了传统超分辨率的范畴：高光谱数据包含丰富的波长相关信息，每个波段编码特定材料的光谱特征。这意味着HISR必须同时保持空间细节和光谱完整性，确保重建的图像在物理意义上仍然有效，而不仅仅是视觉上可信。

高光谱图像数据量大且获取成本高，全分辨率采集成本昂贵且耗时。因此，超分辨率提供了一条强大而实用的途径来降低采集负担，同时实现高质量的分析。

本挑战赛引入了**首个**PBVS CVPR 2026研讨会内的高光谱超分辨率基准。它专注于真实的低分辨率-高分辨率配对数据，采用×4超分辨率，在受控的实验室条件下进行，使用同一传感器和不同光学系统采集的数据，以隔离空间缩放并维持光谱一致性。

**本挑战赛的目标是从提供的低分辨率高光谱图像块重建×4实超分辨率高光谱图像。**

每个低分辨率立方体都有一个完美对齐的高分辨率对应物作为真值标签，这使得能够精确评估空间恢复和光谱保真度。

参与者需要开发方法，将低分辨率数据上采样4倍，同时保持所有波长间的光谱一致性。


## 重要日期

- 2026.01.12 训练和验证数据集发布（输入和输出）
- **2026.01.15 测试数据发布（仅输入）**
- 2026.01.15 测试阶段服务器上线

- **2026.03.01 测试结果提交截止日期**
- 2026.03.03 来自参与者的贡献（排名靠前的结果应提供建议方案的简要说明和架构图示；还应共享代码）
- **2026.03.06 挑战赛参赛作品论文提交截止日期**
- 2026.06.03 PBVS研讨会和挑战赛、结果及颁奖仪式（CVPR 2026）

pages.title: Dataset
pages.content:
# Dataset

## Description
The dataset used in this challenge is **Version 2 of the HSI Lens Dataset**, introduced in the PBVS CVPR 2025 paper:  
[Ulrichsen et al., *“A True Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution Dataset”](
https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025W/PBVS/html/Ulrichsen_A_True_Hyperspectral_Image_Super-Resolution_Dataset_CVPRW_2025_paper.html)

This dataset provides **perfectly aligned low- and high-resolution SWIR hyperspectral image pairs**, acquired using a single Specim FX17 line-scanning camera (900–1700 nm). Spatial resolution differences were generated purely through **lens swapping**, ensuring identical spectral content while isolating spatial resolution as the primary challenge.

- High-resolution images: **3172 × 640 px**, captured with a 12° lens  
- Low-resolution images: **793 × 160 px**, captured with a 38° lens  
- Focus ensured using automated focus metrics and verified with sub-pixel registration  

Scenes cover **spectrally rich and diverse SWIR materials**, including plastics, wood, electronics, metals, fabrics, corrosion, printed text, painted surfaces, and various industrial objects.

## Splits
The dataset includes **70 registered image pairs**, divided as follows:
- **55** pairs for training  
- **10** pairs for validation  
- **5** pairs reserved for testing (not released)

Participants receive LR–HR pairs for training and validation.  
For the **test set**, only LR inputs are provided; high-resolution ground truth remains withheld for fair evaluation.
The LR version of the test set patches can be downloaded here: https://filesender.belnet.be/?s=download&token=237989c4-8c1a-4bd8-b652-49e5dbd90778

## Availability
The dataset can be downloaded from the repository “Files” section or via:  
**Zenodo DOI:** https://zenodo.org/records/18171738

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation Metrics

Submissions are evaluated using **Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR)** and **Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM)**, computed on 20 random patches with a size of **200x200x224 (w x h x bands)** of the hidden hyperspectral test set. Rankings are based on the combined performance across these metrics.

The LR patches of the test dataset can be downloaded here: https://filesender.belnet.be/?s=download&token=237989c4-8c1a-4bd8-b652-49e5dbd90778

Both metrics are computed **per band and averaged** over the hyperspectral cube. 

## Evaluation Dataset
Evaluation is performed only on a fixed set of patches, not on the full images.

* **5 test scenes** are selected.
* From each scene, **6 patches are extracted.**
* Each patch has dimensions** 200 × 200 × 224** (height × width × spectral bands).

This results in a total of 30 evaluation patches (5 scenes × 6 patches).
**All metrics are computed exclusively on these 30 patches.**
Full-resolution test images are not used for evaluation.

## Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR)
PSNR measures the pixel-wise reconstruction fidelity between the super-resolved output and the high-resolution ground truth.  
Higher PSNR values indicate more accurate spatial reconstruction.


## Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM)
SAM quantifies the **spectral similarity** between reconstructed and ground-truth spectra at each pixel by measuring the angle between their spectral vectors.  
Lower SAM values indicate better preservation of material-relevant spectral signatures and higher physical plausibility.

Only low-resolution inputs are provided for the test phase; corresponding HR ground truth remains hidden and is used exclusively for evaluation.

## Reproducibility and code availability (mandatory)

To ensure transparency, fairness, and reproducibility, all participating teams are required to make their full source code publicly available, preferably via a GitHub repository.

The released code must include all components necessary to reproduce the reported results, including:
- Training and evaluation scripts
- Model architectures and configuration files
- Dataset loading and preprocessing steps
- Environment specifications (e.g., requirements.txt, environment.yml, or Docker files)
- Clear, step-by-step instructions to run the code end to end

**The challenge organizers will independently train and evaluate all submitted methods from scratch to verify the reported results.
This verification process will directly affect the final ranking.**

**Teams that fail to provide their source code**, or that do not include sufficient information to reproduce their results, **will be disqualified** from the challenge.
pages.content_zh:
# 评估指标

提交的方案使用**峰值信噪比（PSNR）**和**光谱角制图仪（SAM）**进行评估，计算基于隐藏高光谱测试集中20个随机补丁，每个补丁大小为**200x200x224（宽x高x波段）**。排名基于这些指标的综合性能。

测试数据集的LR补丁可从以下地址下载：https://filesender.belnet.be/?s=download&token=********-****-****-****-************

两个指标均**逐波段计算，然后在高光谱立方体上取平均**。

## 评估数据集
评估仅在固定的补丁集上进行，不在完整图像上进行。

* **选择5个测试场景**
* 从每个场景中**提取6个补丁**
* 每个补丁的尺寸为**200 × 200 × 224**（高 × 宽 × 光谱波段）

共产生30个评估补丁（5个场景 × 6个补丁）。
**所有指标仅在这30个补丁上计算**。
完整分辨率测试图像不用于评估。

## 峰值信噪比（PSNR）
PSNR衡量超分辨率输出与高分辨率真实值之间的像素级重建保真度。
更高的PSNR值表示空间重建更准确。

## 光谱角制图仪（SAM）
SAM通过测量每个像素处重建光谱与真实光谱向量之间的角度，量化**光谱相似性**。
更低的SAM值表示对材料相关光谱特征的保留更好，物理可行性更高。

测试阶段仅提供低分辨率输入；对应的HR真实值保持隐藏，仅用于评估。

## 可重现性和代码可用性（强制性）

为确保透明度、公平性和可重现性，所有参赛队伍必须将完整源代码公开发布，最好通过GitHub存储库。

发布的代码必须包含重现报告结果所需的所有组件，包括：
- 训练和评估脚本
- 模型架构和配置文件
- 数据集加载和预处理步骤
- 环境规范（例如requirements.txt、environment.yml或Docker文件）
- 明确的端到端分步说明

**挑战赛组织者将从头独立训练和评估所有提交的方法，以验证报告的结果。
此验证过程将直接影响最终排名**。

**未能提供源代码的团队**，或未包含足够信息来重现其结果的团队，**将被取消资格**。

pages.title: Submission
pages.content:
# Submission format

Participants must submit their predictions according to the instructions provided below. **Failure to comply with these rules may result in disqualification or incorrect scoring.**

## Packaging
- The submission must be uploaded as a single ZIP file.
- The ZIP file must contain the corresponding scale folder (x4) with the generated SR images.

```
submission.zip/
├── x4/
│   ├── HR_00.h5
│   ├── HR_01.h5
│   ├── HR_02.h5
│   ├──  ...
```
Make sure there is only one key in the .h5 file, it does not matter what the name of that key is.
The dataset must be a 3D array shaped like: (H, W, C) where C = #spectral bands

## Results

- Once uploaded, refresh the page to update the submission status.
- Scoring could take up to 5 minutes.
- For debugging, click on the submission, navigate to Logs tab, and view Scoring Logs > stdout

pages.title: Publication
pages.content:
# Publication
Participants are invited to submit full research papers detailing the methodologies, findings, and contributions developed within the scope of this challenge. Accepted manuscripts will be published in the official proceedings of the CVPR 2026 Workshop.

### Submission Guidelines
Should participants choose to submit a paper, the following protocols must be observed:
* Submission System: All manuscripts must be submitted electronically via the workshop’s OpenReview system (platform subject to confirmation).
* Formatting: Submissions must strictly adhere to the CVPR Author Guidelines, adopting the mandated structure and formatting requirements.
* Page Limits: Papers are limited to eight pages, including all figures and tables. Additional pages containing only cited references are permitted.
* Review Process: All submissions will undergo a double-blind peer review process.
* Important Date: The deadline for paper submission is first week of March (check main page).

### Challenge Report Co-authorship
For each individual evaluation metric, the top-ranked team will be invited to serve as co-authors on the PBVS HISR challenge report. Furthermore, the results and methodologies of the top three teams per metric will be acknowledged and discussed in the final published paper. Winning teams will be contacted directly with further instructions.

**Note:** Top teams should provide a brief description of their proposed solution along with an illustration of the architecture. This information may be included in a potential publication if the submission is accepted. Additionally, the code should be uploaded in github and shared according to the Terms and Conditions.
pages.content_zh:
# 发表
邀请参赛者提交详细的研究论文，阐述在本次竞赛范围内开发的方法、发现和贡献。被接受的稿件将发表在CVPR 2026研讨会的官方论文集中。

### 投稿指南
如参赛者选择投稿论文，必须遵守以下规程：
* 投稿系统：所有稿件必须通过研讨会的OpenReview系统以电子方式提交（平台待确认）。
* 格式要求：投稿必须严格遵循CVPR作者指南，采用规定的结构和格式要求。
* 页数限制：论文限制为八页，包括所有图表和表格。仅含引用文献的附加页面不受限制。
* 审稿流程：所有投稿将经过双盲同行评审。
* 重要日期：论文投稿截止日期为三月第一周（详见主页）。

### 竞赛报告联合作者
对于每个评估指标，排名最高的团队将被邀请作为PBVS HISR竞赛报告的联合作者。此外，每个指标排名前三的团队的结果和方法将在最终发表的论文中得到承认和讨论。获奖团队将收到直接联系和进一步的说明。

**注意：** 排名靠前的团队应提供其所提方案的简要描述以及架构图示。如果投稿被接受，此信息可能被纳入潜在的出版物中。另外，代码应上传至GitHub并根据《条款和条件》进行分享。

pages.content:
# Mixed Signals: V2X Collaborative 3D Object Detection Challenge

Welcome! This competition runs on the [Mixed Signals](https://mixedsignalsdataset.cs.cornell.edu/) dataset (ICCV 2025). The task is collaborative 3D object detection: given the LiDAR point clouds for a frame from up to four agents (five LiDAR streams), predict 3D bounding boxes for three meta-classes.
Class idClassGrouped from (10 fine-grained classes)
1Vehiclecar, truck, emergency vehicle, bus, electric vehicle, trailer
2Bikemotorbike, bicycle, portable personal mobility
3Pedestrianpedestrian
The sensors see the scene from different positions, so you can choose to fuse their point clouds to fill occlusions and extend the range of detection beyond a single viewpoint. You may use any subset of the agents and any fusion strategy (early, intermediate, or late fusion, or a single-agent baseline). The only requirement is that predictions are expressed in the "top" ego frame and follow the submission format. See the Evaluation & Submission tab for the format and how entries are scored. ## Getting started 1. Download the data. The point clouds, odometry and training labels are on HuggingFace; download what you need and extract it in place: 2. Train a detector. Clone the dev-kit for the PointPillar baselines (no, early, intermediate and late fusion) to build on: . Any approach is allowed, single-agent or fused across the five LiDARs. 3. Build and check a submission. The starting kit has the frame lists, a dataloader, the format spec and a submission checker. Use them to produce one prediction file per frame and validate it before uploading. See the Evaluation & Submission tab. The dataset page and starting kit have the exact commands and file layout. By participating you agree to the dataset's license and terms (see the Terms tab). ## Splits

Train29 scenes (the 33 official train scenes minus the 4 validation)training your modelpublic

## Timeline
PhaseDatesScored on
DevelopmentAug 1 to 28, 2026Public validation split, for leaderboard feedback.
FinalAug 29 to Sep 4, 2026Held-out test set of 4 scenes.
Submissions do not carry over between phases. To be ranked in the Final, submit your predictions on the test set yourself before the phase closes. ## Prizes
PlacePrize
🥇 1st500 USD
🥈 2nd300 USD
🥉 3rd200 USD
Rankings are by mAP on the held-out test set. Winners will be contacted by the organizers shortly after the competition ends to arrange their prize. See the Terms tab for eligibility. ## Citation If you use the dataset, please cite: ```bibtex @inproceedings{luo2025mixedsignals, title = {Mixed Signals: A Diverse Point Cloud Dataset for Heterogeneous LiDAR V2X Collaboration}, author = {Luo, Katie Z. and Dao, Minh-Quan and Liu, Zhenzhen and Campbell, Mark and Chao, Wei-Lun and Weinberger, Kilian Q. and Malis, Ezio and Fr\'emont, Vincent and Hariharan, Bharath and Shan, Mao and Worrall, Stewart and Berrio Perez, Julie Stephany}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)}, year = {2025} } ```

pages.title: Evaluation & Submission
pages.content:
# Evaluation & Submission

This page covers how to format a submission and how entries are scored. For the
task, dataset and timeline, see the Overview tab.

## Building predictions

Produce one detection file per evaluation frame, named after that frame's id.
The frame ids you must predict are listed in the starting kit
(`validation_frames.txt` for Development, `test_frames.txt` for Final). Each
line is one detection with nine fields:

```
# cls cx cy cz dx dy dz yaw score
1 12.34 -3.21 0.05 4.10 1.92 1.55 1.5708 0.97
```

* `cls` ∈ {1=Vehicle, 2=Bike, 3=Pedestrian}
* `cx cy cz`: box centre in metres, "top" ego frame
* `dx dy dz`: length, width, height in metres
* `yaw`: heading (rotation about +z) in radians
* `score`: confidence in [0, 1] (used for ranking detections)

Zip the per-frame files at the root of the archive and upload on the Submit tab.
The starting kit's `SUBMISSION_FORMAT.md` is the authoritative spec, with a
sample submission and a format-checker. Run the checker before you upload.

## Evaluation

We follow the official Mixed Signals / OpenCOOD evaluation protocol exactly,
so leaderboard numbers are directly comparable to the dataset paper.

### Metric

* Matching: Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) rotated-box IoU between predicted and
  ground-truth boxes (the z/height dimension is not used for matching, in line
  with the dataset benchmark).
* Average Precision (AP): VOC-2010 "all-points" interpolation, the area
  under the precision-recall curve (not the 11-point variant).
* Per class: AP is computed independently for vehicle, bike and
  pedestrian at IoU thresholds 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7.
* Matching rule: within each frame, detections are ranked by descending
  confidence and greedily matched to ground-truth boxes. Each ground-truth box
  can be matched at most once. Unmatched detections (or matches below the IoU
  threshold) are false positives.
* Evaluation range: boxes whose centre falls outside `x, y ∈ [-51.2, 51.2] m`
  are excluded from both predictions and ground truth before scoring.

### Ranking by mAP

The leaderboard is ranked by the headline mAP, the mean of the three per-class
operating points reported in the paper:

```
mAP = mean( Vehicle AP@0.5 , Bike AP@0.5 , Pedestrian AP@0.3 )
```

(Pedestrians are scored at the looser 0.3 IoU because the boxes are small.) The
leaderboard also reports Vehicle and Bike AP at IoU 0.5/0.7 and Pedestrian AP at
IoU 0.3/0.5, matching the published tables, but only mAP decides the ranking.
Ties on mAP are broken by the leaderboard columns left to right (starting with
Vehicle AP@0.5), then by submission time, so earlier submissions rank higher.

### Scoring program

The scoring program is open and downloadable from the Submit / Files
area. It depends only on `numpy` and implements the BEV IoU and VOC AP from
scratch, so you can run it locally against your own validation labels to
reproduce leaderboard scores exactly.
pages.content_zh:
# 评估与提交

本页介绍如何格式化提交内容以及条目的评分方式。有关任务、数据集和时间表，请参阅"概览"选项卡。

## 构建预测

为每个评估帧生成一个检测文件，文件名以该帧的id命名。您需要预测的帧id列在起始工具包中（开发集使用`validation_frames.txt`，最终测试使用`test_frames.txt`）。每一行是一个检测，包含九个字段：

```
# cls cx cy cz dx dy dz yaw score
1 12.34 -3.21 0.05 4.10 1.92 1.55 1.5708 0.97
```

* `cls` ∈ {1=车辆, 2=自行车, 3=行人}
* `cx cy cz`：边界框中心，单位为米，"顶部"自车坐标系
* `dx dy dz`：长、宽、高，单位为米
* `yaw`：航向角（绕+z轴旋转），单位为弧度
* `score`：置信度 ∈ [0, 1]（用于排序检测）

将各帧文件压缩到存档根目录并在"提交"选项卡中上传。起始工具包中的`SUBMISSION_FORMAT.md`是权威规范，包含示例提交和格式检查器。上传前运行检查器。

## 评估

我们完全遵循官方Mixed Signals / OpenCOOD评估协议，因此排行榜数据可直接与数据集论文进行比较。

### 指标

* 匹配：预测框与真实框之间的鸟瞰图（BEV）旋转框交并比（IoU）（不使用z/高度维度用于匹配，与数据集基准一致）。
* 平均精度（AP）：VOC-2010"全点"插值法，精确率-召回率曲线下的面积（非11点变体）。
* 各类别：AP在IoU阈值0.3、0.5和0.7处分别针对车辆、自行车和行人独立计算。
* 匹配规则：在每一帧内，检测按置信度降序排列，并贪心地与真实框匹配。每个真实框最多只能匹配一次。不匹配的检测（或低于IoU阈值的匹配）为假正例。
* 评估范围：中心落在`x, y ∈ [-51.2, 51.2] m`范围外的边界框在评分前从预测和真实数据中排除。

### 按mAP排名

排行榜按标题mAP排名，即论文中报告的三个各类别操作点的平均值：

```
mAP = mean( 车辆 AP@0.5 , 自行车 AP@0.5 , 行人 AP@0.3 )
```

（行人使用较宽松的0.3 IoU评分，因为其边界框较小。）排行榜还报告车辆和自行车在IoU 0.5/0.7处的AP以及行人在IoU 0.3/0.5处的AP，与已发表的表格一致，但仅mAP决定排名。mAP的平局按排行榜列从左到右打破（从车辆AP@0.5开始），再按提交时间打破，因此较早的提交排名较高。

### 评分程序

评分程序是开源的，可从"提交/文件"区域下载。它仅依赖`numpy`，从零开始实现BEV IoU和VOC AP，因此您可以在本地针对您自己的验证标签运行它，以精确再现排行榜分数。

# Terms and Conditions

By registering for and participating in the Mixed Signals: V2X Collaborative 3D
Object Detection Challenge (the "Competition"), you agree to the following terms.

## 1. Dataset license and use

A. The Competition uses the Mixed Signals dataset, released under
   [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/). The
   dataset is not redistributed through this platform. You must obtain it from

   and comply with that license.

B. The license permits non-commercial research use with attribution, and
   requires that any redistributed derivatives carry the same license
   (share-alike). Do not use the data commercially or in violation of the license.

C. You must cite the Mixed Signals paper (see the Overview tab) in any
   publication or report that uses the dataset or your Competition results.

## 2. Submissions

A. Submissions consist of prediction files only. Do not attempt to upload or
   execute code that probes, reverse-engineers, or exfiltrates the hidden test
   ground truth.

B. You may not attempt to identify, scrape, or reconstruct the held-out test
   labels by any means other than honest model inference.

C. Each participant or team must use a single account. Creating multiple
   accounts to gain extra submissions or to probe the leaderboard is prohibited
   and will result in disqualification.

D. Per-phase submission limits are enforced by the platform and may be adjusted
   by the organizers if abuse is detected.

## 3. Eligibility, teams and fair play

A. Teams may have one or more members. All members must be registered and a
   member may belong to only one team.

B. Organizers and individuals with access to the hidden test annotations are not
   eligible for prizes.

C. The use of any data, pretrained models, or external resources must comply
   with their respective licenses. If external data or pretrained weights are
   used, organizers may require disclosure for verification.

## 4. Prizes

A. Cash prizes are awarded to the top three entries on the Final (test)
   leaderboard: 1st = 500 USD, 2nd = 300 USD, 3rd = 200 USD. The organizers
   reserve the right to add, modify, withhold, or cancel prizes at their
   discretion.

B. Prize winners will be contacted by the organizers shortly after the
   competition ends, using the contact details associated with their Codabench
   account, to arrange prize delivery. No fixed notification date is guaranteed.

C. Prizes may be subject to applicable laws, taxes, and export restrictions.

## 5. Leaderboard, results and publicity

A. The Development leaderboard is for feedback only and does not determine
   final standings. The Final leaderboard determines official rankings.

B. The organizers may publish participant usernames/team names, scores, and
   aggregate statistics.

C. The organizers' decisions on scoring, ranking, eligibility, and rule
   interpretation are final.

## 6. Disclaimer

The Competition, dataset, and scoring software are provided "as is" without
warranty of any kind. The organizers are not liable for any damages arising from
participation. The organizers reserve the right to modify these terms, the
schedule, or the evaluation at any time, with reasonable notice to participants
via the competition pages.

## 7. Contact

For questions, contact the organizers at the email listed on the competition
homepage.

17265.title: 第十届全国激光雷达大会——City-Facade建筑立面点云实例分割大赛
17265.description:
本比赛面向城市级建筑立面构件精细理解，采用City-Facade大规模三维点云数据集。

数据由车载移动激光扫描系统采集，覆盖厦门市多类典型城市街区，累计道路长度约60 km。数据包含墙面、窗户、门、屋顶、广告牌、空调外机、雨棚和阳台等细粒度建筑立面要素标注，并提供语义级与实例级标签。

参赛者需要识别测试点云中的独立建筑立面构件实例，并输出相应实例编号和语义类别。

比赛采用结果提交模式。参赛者在本地完成模型训练和推理，仅向Codabench提交预测结果，平台使用隐藏实例标签进行自动评分。
17265.description_zh:
This competition focuses on fine-grained understanding of urban-level building facade components, utilizing the City-Fac dataset.

The data is collected by vehicle-mounted mobile laser scanning systems, covering multiple types of typical urban street blocks in Xiamen, with a cumulative road length of approximately 60 km. The dataset includes fine-grained building facade element annotations such as walls, windows, doors, roofs, billboards, air conditioning units, canopies, and balconies, with both semantic-level and instance-level labels provided.

Participants need to identify independent building facade component instances in the test point cloud and output the corresponding semantic categories and instance numbers.

The competition adopts a result submission mode. Participants complete model training and inference locally and only submit prediction results to Codabench, where the platform automatically scores using hidden instance labels.

pages.content:
# **建筑物立面点云语义/实例分割**

## **Overview**

本赛道采用 City-Facade 城市建筑立面点云数据集，开展建筑立面点云语义分割与实例分割。

参赛者需要为测试集中的每个点预测语义类别，并进一步区分同一语义类别下不同建筑立面构件的实例编号。

City-Facade 数据由车载移动激光扫描系统采集，覆盖厦门市 6 类典型城市街区场景，累计道路长度约 60 km，包含约 2 亿个带标注点。

语义类别如下：

| **编号** | **英文类别**              | **中文类别** |
| -------- | ------------------------- | ------------ |
| 0        | Background / Unclassified | 背景或未分类 |
| 1        | Wall                      | 墙面         |
| 2        | Window                    | 窗户         |
| 3        | Door                      | 门           |
| 4        | Roof                      | 屋顶         |
| 5        | Advertisement             | 广告牌       |
| 6        | Air Conditioner           | 空调外机     |
| 7        | Rain Shed                 | 雨棚         |
| 8        | Balcony                   | 阳台         |

参赛流程：

1. 在训练数据集上开发三维点云语义分割与实例分割模型；
2. 使用训练完成的模型预测测试数据；
3. 为每个测试点生成语义标签和实例标签；
4. 按指定目录结构压缩预测结果；
5. 将结果上传至 Codabench；
6. 平台自动评测并更新排行榜。

数据集项目地址：

```text
https://github.com/Ting-Devin-Han/City-Facade
```

## **Evaluation**

主排名指标为综合得分：

```text
Score = 0.5 × mIoU + 0.5 × AP50
```

其中：

- mIoU 用于评价语义分割精度；
- AP50 用于评价实例分割精度。

辅助指标包括：

- mIoU
- OA
- 各类别 IoU
- AP
- AP25
- AP50

所有指标均为越高越好。

每支队伍每日最多提交 5 次。

若综合得分相同，建议依次按照 AP50、mIoU、AP25 和提交时间确定排名。

## **Submission Format**

参赛者须为测试集中的每个点提供语义标签和实例标签，并提交一个 ZIP 压缩包。

压缩包根目录必须包含`predictions/`文件夹：

```text
submission.zip
└── predictions/
    ├── CAR/
    │   ├── CAR-30-003_000000.txt
    │   ├── CAR-30-003_000001.txt
    │   └── ...
    ├── JMC/
    ├── SGS/
    ├── XHR/
    └── YWR/
```

目录名称和预测文件名称必须与测试数据保持一致。例如：

```text
test/JMC/JMC-1-013_000000.txt
predictions/JMC/JMC-1-013_000000.txt
```

每个预测 `.txt` 文件为 `N x 7` 数组，字段顺序固定为：

```text
X Y Z intensity instance_id semantic_label instance_score
```

其中：

- `N` 为点云点数；
- `X Y Z` 为三维坐标；
- `intensity` 为激光强度；
- `instance_id` 为预测实例编号；
- `semantic_label` 为预测语义类别；
- `instance_score` 为预测实例置信度

字段索引从 `0` 开始时：

```text
X=0, Y=1, Z=2, intensity=3, instance_id=4, semantic_label=5, instance_score=6
```

提交文件必须满足：

1. 每个测试 `.txt` 文件都必须有对应预测文件；
2. 预测文件的相对路径和文件名必须与测试集一致；
3. 每个预测文件的点数必须与对应测试文件完全一致；
4. 点顺序必须与测试文件完全一致；
5. `X Y Z intensity` 四列应保持与测试文件一致；
6. `semantic_label` 必须为整数，取值范围为 `0` 到 `8`；
7. `instance_id` 必须为非负整数；
8. `instance_score` 必须是 `[0,1]` 范围内的有限数值，不允许使用 `NaN` 或正负无穷。
9. 对于语义类别 `1` 到 `8` 的前景构件，不同实例应使用不同的实例编号；
10. 对于类别 `0` 的背景或未分类点，`instance_id` 可设为 `0`；
11. ZIP 根目录必须包含 `predictions/` 文件夹，不要额外嵌套一层目录。

## **Citation**

使用 City-Facade 数据集开展研究或发表成果时，请引用：

```bibtex
@article{chen2026cityfacade,
  title={City-Facade: A city-level large-scale point cloud building facade dataset for semantic \& instance segmentation},
  author={Chen, Yiping and Li, Jonathan and Han, Ting and Feng, Huifang and Chen, Jun and Wang, Cheng},
  journal={ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing},
  volume={232},
  pages={675--688},
  year={2026},
  doi={10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.01.003}
}
```
pages.content_zh:
# **Building Facade Point Cloud Semantic/Instance Segmentation**

## **Overview**

This track uses the City-Facade dataset to conduct semantic segmentation and instance segmentation of building facade point clouds.

Participants need to predict semantic categories for each point in the test set and further distinguish instance numbers of different building facade components within the same semantic category.

The City-Facade dataset is collected by vehicle-mounted mobile laser scanning systems, covering 6 typical urban street scene categories in Xiamen City, with a total road length of approximately 60 km and containing approximately 200 million annotated points.

Semantic categories are as follows:

| **ID** | **English Category**      | **Chinese Category** |
| ------ | ------------------------- | -------------------- |
| 0      | Background / Unclassified | Background/Unclassified |
| 1      | Wall                      | Wall                 |
| 2      | Window                    | Window               |
| 3      | Door                      | Door                 |
| 4      | Roof                      | Roof                 |
| 5      | Advertisement             | Advertisement Board  |
| 6      | Air Conditioner           | Air Conditioner Unit |
| 7      | Rain Shed                 | Rain Shed            |
| 8      | Balcony                   | Balcony              |

Competition workflow:

1. Develop 3D point cloud semantic and instance segmentation models on the training dataset;
2. Use the trained model to predict test data;
3. Generate semantic labels and instance labels for each test point;
4. Compress prediction results according to the specified directory structure;
5. Upload results to Codabench;
6. The platform automatically evaluates and updates the leaderboard.

Dataset project address:

```text
https://github.com/gorgeouseping/City-Facade
```

## **Evaluation**

The main ranking metric is the comprehensive score:

```text
Score = 0.5 × mIoU + 0.5 × AP50
```

Where:

- mIoU is used to evaluate semantic segmentation accuracy;
- AP50 is used to evaluate instance segmentation accuracy.

Auxiliary metrics include:

- mIoU
- OA
- IoU for each category
- AP
- AP25
- AP50

All metrics are higher the better.

Each team can submit a maximum of 5 times per day.

If the comprehensive score is the same, it is recommended to determine rankings in order by AP50, mIoU, AP25, and submission time.

## **Submission Format**

Participants must provide semantic labels and instance labels for each point in the test set and submit a ZIP compressed package.

```text
submission.zip
└── predictions/
    ├── CAR/
    │   ├── CAR-30-003_000000.txt
    │   ├── CAR-30-003_000001.txt
    │   └── ...
    ├── JMC/
    ├── SGS/
    └── ...
```

Directory names and prediction file names must be consistent with the test data.

Each TXT file contains 6 fields:

```text
X Y Z intensity semantic_label instance_id
```

Array dimensions are:

```text
N × 6
```

Where:

- `N` is the number of points in the point cloud;
- `X Y Z` are 3D coordinates;
- `intensity` is laser intensity;
- `semantic_label` is the predicted semantic category;
- `instance_id` is the predicted instance number.

Submitted files must satisfy:

1. The number and order of points are completely consistent with the original test files;
2. The 3D coordinates and intensity fields must not be modified;
3. Semantic category ID range is 0-8;
4. Instance IDs must be non-negative integers;
5. Different instances use different instance IDs;
6. Prediction file directories and file names must be consistent with the test set;
7. The ZIP root directory must contain a `predictions` folder.

## **Citation**

When using the City-Facade dataset, please cite:

```bibtex
@article{chen2026cityfacade,
  title={City-Facade: A city-level large-scale building facade point cloud dataset for semantic and instance segmentation},
  author={Chen, Yiping and Li, Jonathan and Han, Ting and Feng, Huifang and Chen, Jun and Wang, Cheng},
  journal={ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing},
  volume={232},
  pages={675--688},
  year={2026},
  doi={10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.01.003}
}
```

17680.title: Who is Behind the Avatar?  Verifying Teleoperator Identity in Reenacted Avatar Videos
17680.description: Welcome to the first International Competition on Verifying Teleoperator Identity in Reenacted Avatar Videos. The competition will be in conjunction with [ACCV2026](https://https://accv2026.org/])
17680.description_zh: 欢迎来到首届"重演化身视频中远程操作者身份验证"国际竞赛。本竞赛将与[ACCV2026](https://https://accv2026.org/)联合举办。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content: Welcome to the first International Competition on **Teleoperator Identity Verification in Reenacted Avatar Videos — WBA 2026**. ## Motivation Photorealistic avatars are increasingly used in telepresence, mixed reality, gaming, virtual environments, and AI-mediated video communication. In these settings, the visible face may be synthetic or may differ entirely from the person controlling it. Consequently, conventional face-recognition methods may not be sufficient to verify the identity of the underlying user. The **Who Is Behind the Avatar? (WBA)** challenge investigates whether behavioral information preserved in avatar videos can be used to authenticate the human teleoperator independently of the avatar’s visual appearance. Unlike conventional DeepFake-detection challenges, WBA does not ask participants to determine whether a video is real or synthetic. Avatar-generated videos are treated as legitimate communication media. The objective is instead to verify **operator authenticity**: whether an avatar is controlled by the authorized person. ## Challenge Task WBA 2026 is a **cross-avatar teleoperator verification challenge**. For each verification trial, participants are provided with: 1. a gallery avatar video driven by a known teleoperator; and 2. a probe avatar video driven by an unknown teleoperator. Participants must determine whether the two avatar videos are driven by: * the **same teleoperator**, representing a genuine trial; or * **different teleoperators**, representing an impostor trial. The gallery and probe videos may represent the same person through different avatar identities. Therefore, systems should focus on teleoperator-specific behavioral information rather than the visible appearance of the avatar. Potential behavioral cues include: * facial-motion dynamics * head movement and pose * expression timing * gaze behavior * speech-related facial movement * temporal motion patterns * other person-specific behavioral characteristics Participants may develop systems using RGB video, facial landmarks, head-pose features, expression dynamics, temporal motion descriptors, video embeddings, or other suitable representations. ## Dataset The source driving videos were collected in Japan during controlled dyadic online first-meeting conversations. The selected sequences are taken from the self-introduction portion of the conversations and include both speaking and listening segments. The original recordings were captured under controlled frontal-camera and lighting conditions. However, the original human videos are retained by the organizers and are not released to challenge participants. Instead, the motion and expression information from the original recordings are transferred to photorealistic avatar templates through a face-reenactment pipeline. The avatar appearances are selected from the publicly available **NVFAIR** dataset, while the reenacted videos are generated using **GAGAvatar**. This design reduces the direct exposure of the original participants’ visual identities while preserving motion and behavioral information relevant to teleoperator verification. Audio is not included in the released dataset and is not used during evaluation.
pages.content_zh: 欢迎来到首届**重演头像视频中的远程操作者身份验证国际竞赛——WBA 2026**。 ## 动机 超逼真头像越来越多地被应用于远程呈现、混合现实、游戏、虚拟环境和人工智能中介的视频通信。在这些应用中，可见的面孔可能是合成的，或者可能与控制它的人完全不同。因此，传统的面部识别方法可能不足以验证底层用户的身份。 **谁在头像后面？(WBA)** 挑战赛调查了头像视频中保留的行为信息是否可以用于独立于头像视觉外观的人类远程操作者身份认证。 与传统的深伪检测挑战不同，WBA不要求参与者判断视频是否真实或合成。头像生成的视频被视为合法的通信媒介。目标是验证**操作者的真实性**：头像是否由授权人员控制。 ## 挑战任务 WBA 2026是一项**跨头像远程操作者验证挑战**。 对于每次验证试验，参与者获得： 1. 由已知远程操作者驱动的图库头像视频；以及 2. 由未知远程操作者驱动的探针头像视频。 参与者必须确定这两个头像视频是否由以下任一情况驱动： * **相同的远程操作者**，代表真实试验；或 * **不同的远程操作者**，代表冒充试验。 图库和探针视频可能通过不同的头像身份代表同一个人。因此，系统应专注于远程操作者特定的行为信息，而不是头像的可见外观。 潜在的行为线索包括： * 面部运动动态 * 头部运动和姿态 * 表情时序 * 注视行为 * 与语音相关的面部运动 * 时间运动模式 * 其他人员特定的行为特征 参与者可以使用RGB视频、面部特征点、头部姿态特征、表情动态、时间运动描述符、视频嵌入或其他合适的表示方法开发系统。 ## 数据集 源驱动视频是在日本进行的受控二人组在线首次会面对话期间收集的。所选序列取自对话的自我介绍部分，包括说话和聆听片段。 原始录制是在受控的正面摄像头和照明条件下捕获的。但是，原始人类视频由组织者保留，不会向挑战参与者发布。 相反，来自原始录制的运动和表情信息通过人脸重演管道转移到超逼真头像模板。头像外观选自公开可用的 **NVFAIR** 数据集，而重演视频使用 **GAGAvatar** 生成。 这种设计减少了原始参与者视觉身份的直接暴露，同时保留了与远程操作者验证相关的运动和行为信息。 所发布的数据集中不包含音频，评估期间也不使用音频。

If you have any questions or need further assistance, please don’t hesitate to reach out to ammar@yy.d3c.osaka-u.ac.jp and cc: allam@yy.d3c.osaka-u.ac.jp We will provide You can use the following repo to extract the data, [Starter kit](https://github.com/jasam-sheja/OUMVLP-OF-challenge). ## Released Resources The organizers plan to provide: * training data * test-data access instructions * official verification trial lists * a baseline embedding and similarity system * evaluation code * a sample submission * a submission-validation tool * competition rules and documentation The baseline system is intended to support reproducibility, reduce the entry barrier, and encourage participants to investigate stronger temporal and behavioral representations. ## Data-Use Policy The challenge data may only be used in accordance with the official WBA 2026 participation rules and the licenses associated with the source datasets and avatar-generation resources. pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
## Training and Test Protocol

The training and test sets are disjoint with respect to both:

* teleoperator identity; and
* avatar appearance.

No teleoperator appearing in the test set is included in the training set. Similarly, the avatar templates used for testing are not included in the training data.

This protocol evaluates whether submitted systems can generalize to:

* unseen teleoperators;
* unseen avatar identities;
* different speaking conditions;
* variations in avatar geometry and motion response.

The challenge is designed to discourage reliance on avatar appearance and encourage the development of representations that capture persistent teleoperator-specific behavioral characteristics.

## Submission

Participants are required to generate and submit an embedding for every test video.

For each verification pair, the submitted gallery and probe embeddings are compared using one of the following measures:

* cosine similarity or cosine distance; or
* Euclidean distance.

Participants specify the comparison method used by their system at submission time.

The Codabench evaluation program calculates the verification scores and corresponding performance metrics from the submitted embeddings.

## Evaluation

The official evaluation metrics are:

* **Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve — AUC**
* **Equal Error Rate — EER**

Teams are ranked exclusively according to **AUC**.

EER is reported as an additional reference metric and is not used to determine the final leaderboard ranking.

Performance is evaluated under three conditions:

### Speaking Condition

Both the gallery and probe videos contain speaking sequences.

### Non-Speaking Condition

Both the gallery and probe videos contain listening or non-speaking sequences.

### Cross-Condition

One video contains a speaking sequence, while the other contains a non-speaking sequence.

The final leaderboard score is calculated as the **average AUC across the three evaluation conditions**.
pages.content_zh:
## 训练和测试协议

训练集和测试集在以下两个方面是互不相交的：

* 遥操作员身份；以及
* 虚拟形象外观。

测试集中出现的任何遥操作员都不包含在训练集中。同样，用于测试的虚拟形象模板不包含在训练数据中。

该协议评估提交的系统是否能够泛化到：

* 未见过的遥操作员；
* 未见过的虚拟形象身份；
* 不同的说话条件；
* 虚拟形象几何形状和运动响应的变化。

该挑战旨在抑制对虚拟形象外观的依赖，并鼓励开发能够捕捉持久遥操作员特定行为特征的表示方法。

## 提交

参赛者需要为每个测试视频生成并提交一个嵌入向量。

对于每对验证样本，提交的库嵌入和探针嵌入使用以下度量之一进行比较：

* 余弦相似度或余弦距离；或
* 欧几里得距离。

参赛者在提交时指定其系统使用的比较方法。

Codabench评估程序从提交的嵌入向量计算验证得分和相应的性能指标。

## 评估

官方评估指标包括：

* **受试者工作特征曲线下面积 — AUC**
* **等错误率 — EER**

团队的排名仅根据 **AUC** 确定。

EER作为附加参考指标报告，不用于确定最终排行榜排名。

性能在三种条件下进行评估：

### 说话条件

库视频和探针视频都包含说话序列。

### 非说话条件

库视频和探针视频都包含聆听或非说话序列。

### 交叉条件

一个视频包含说话序列，另一个包含非说话序列。

最终排行榜得分计算为**三种评估条件下的平均AUC**。

17677.description_zh: LiDAR-惯性SLAM赛道的仅翻译评估。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# LiDAR-Inertial SLAM

This is the independent LiDAR-inertial track of the Multi-Sensor LiDAR SLAM Challenge 2026. Participants process the two released scenes locally and submit estimated trajectories only. Reliable ground truth and its timestamps remain private on Codabench.

Both `scene_0001` and `scene_0002` are required. Completion has no hard threshold; missing trajectory coverage reduces AUC recall and the final score.

The dataset was recorded with an Airy LiDAR and its built-in IMU. The following images are route-shape references only and contain no ground truth.

![Scene 1 trajectory reference](images/scene_0001_trajectory_reference.png)

pages.content:
# Evaluation

Scoring uses EVO time synchronization and one no-scale SE(3) alignment per scene against the private reference trajectory. Completion has no hard threshold and is published; missing pose pairs reduce AUC recall. Evaluation timestamps and ground truth are not published.

ATE is EVO translational APE RMSE. AUC uses EVO one-frame translational RPE and the F1-AUC protocol. RTE is the RMSE of EVO translational RPE normalized at 1 m, 5 m, and 10 m. Aggregate and per-scene RTE@1m, RTE@5m, and RTE@10m are all published alongside the combined RTE. Gaps over 0.3 s are never crossed.

AUC and RTE use aligned world-frame positions with identity orientations, so a fixed participant body-axis convention does not affect translation scores. Every scene uses one scene-level SE(3) alignment.

The total score is `100 * (0.40 * AUC + 0.40 * exp(-ATE / tau_ate) + 0.20 * exp(-RTE / tau_rte))`. Reference result is the published reference: its aggregate ATE and RTE define `tau_ate` and `tau_rte` after the final scorer is frozen.

Results publish the total score, aggregate and per-scene AUC/ATE/combined RTE/RTE@1m/RTE@5m/RTE@10m, normalized score components, completion, and match counts. Per-timestamp errors, associations, alignment transforms, and ground truth remain private.

# 评估

ATE是EVO平移APE均方根误差。AUC使用EVO单帧平移RPE和F1-AUC协议。RTE是EVO平移RPE的均方根误差，在1 m、5 m和10 m处归一化。总体和各场景的RTE@1m、RTE@5m和RTE@10m均与合并RTE一起公开发布。超过0.3 s的间隔不被跨越。

AUC和RTE使用对齐的世界坐标系位置和单位方向，因此固定的参与者机体坐标系约定不影响平移得分。每个场景使用一个场景级SE(3)对齐。

总分为`100 * (0.40 * AUC + 0.40 * exp(-ATE / tau_ate) + 0.20 * exp(-RTE / tau_rte))`。参考结果是已发布的参考值：其总体ATE和RTE在最终评分器冻结后定义`tau_ate`和`tau_rte`。

结果公开发布总分、总体和各场景AUC/ATE/合并RTE/RTE@1m/RTE@5m/RTE@10m、归一化得分组件、完成度和匹配计数。单时间戳误差、关联、对齐变换和真值保持私有。
